story_text_a: Kathy, a 31-year-old woman, reflects on her past. Her memoir takes her back to her formative years, spent in a British boarding school lost in the middle of the countryside, with little contact with the outside world. The young woman seems unable to overcome old childhood wounds. As the novel progresses, the truth about these children cut off from the world for several years is revealed...
story_text_b:
Billy Lynn, a 19-year-old US Army specialist from Texas, is caught on camera dragging wounded Sergeant Virgil "Shroom" Breem to safety during an intense firefight in Iraq on October 23, 2004. This act of courage earns Lynn the Silver Star and quickly ascends him and his unit, erroneously designated "Bravo Squad" by the media, to celebrity status. They return to the U.S. for Shroom's funeral, then are sent on a publicity tour culminating at the halftime show of the November 25 Dallas Cowboys Thanksgiving home game.
Now led by Sgt. David Dime, the members of Bravo Squad are driven in a limousine to the stadium with the Cowboys' PR representative Josh and film producer Albert Brown, who is in the process of securing a film deal for the squad. A flashback reveals that Billy joined the army after destroying the car of his older sister Kathryn's boyfriend, who left her after she was in a car accident that required multiple facial reconstruction procedures. At the stadium, the group is greeted by anxious fans who express gratitude for their actions in the Iraq War. During a press conference, Billy spots a Cowboys Cheerleader, Faison, smiling at him. They strike up a conversation and begin a flirtation. Billy tells her how it feels weird to be honored for the worst day of his life.
As the game starts, Billy recalls his time in Iraq, where Shroom had offered him karmic philosophical insight and advice during their downtime. It is revealed that once the game ends, Bravo Squad will have to return to duty. Billy receives a phone call from a psychiatrist to whom Kathryn had spoken, regarding a plan to get Billy honorably discharged so he doesn't have to return to Iraq, thereby sparing him further suffering.
During the halftime show, featuring Destiny's Child, the loud music and pyrotechnics traumatize an already unstable squad member, Sykes, and he reacts violently against a security guard. Billy experiences a flashback to the battle that made them famous. The squad was called in to rescue soldiers pinned down by insurgents at a school. Shroom is shot while advancing from cover, and Billy rushes to save him, firing on the nearby insurgents with his sidearm. Billy drags Shroom into a trench, but an insurgent attacks Billy at close range. Billy kills him in self-defense, but is traumatized by the incident and, upon returning to help, discovers Shroom has bled to death. Billy's flashback ends when troop members get his attention and point out that the halftime show has been over for a few minutes. Billy had been frozen in place all the while. As they are urged to leave by stage hands and security, the soldiers are diverted from a fight by cheerleaders led by Faison. Billy takes her name and number on his cell phone, learning that her last name is Zorn, meaning 'anger'.
Billy and Dime meet with the owner of the Cowboys, Norm Oglesby, who is considering investing in Albert's movie about the incident in Iraq. However, instead of the $100,000 that Albert was hoping to get for each squad member, Oglesby offers them only $5,500 apiece. Dime angrily rebuffs Oglesby's offer. In private, Oglesby tells Billy that the squad's story is no longer theirs, but instead belongs to the American people. Billy tells Oglesby off, joining Dime. Albert promises Billy that he will find investors one way or another, and that their story deserves to be told "the right way."
As the squad leaves, Billy meets up with Faison briefly before leaving. He says he would run away with her, even though he has to go back. In a clumsy deflection, she reinforces his duty to redeploy, and he accepts with understanding. They share a kiss. As Billy meets back up with his squad, they are attacked by the security guards from earlier, briefly triggering Billy's PTSD, which fills his mind with surreal imagery of war and death. The altercation is halted with a warning gunshot. Kathryn arrives to retrieve Billy and effect his medical discharge. He makes it clear he is redeploying with his squad, more for his sense of belonging than for duty. She is upset, but after Billy explains, they share a tearful hug.
Billy returns to the limo, but hallucinates and sees a Humvee. He gets in, sees Shroom's familiar icon of Ganesha and has a philosophical conversation with Shroom. Billy tells Shroom "I love you," then returns to the reality of the Bravo Squad members in the limo, each of whom responds with "I love you."

story_text_a: Milo Boyd (Gerard Butler), un cazarrecompensas venido a menos, obtiene el trabajo de sus sueños al serle asignada la búsqueda de su exmujer, la periodista Nicole Hurley "Nic" (Jennifer Aniston), que se ha saltado su libertad condicional. Él piensa que el trabajo representará dinero fácil, pero cuando Nicole logra zafarse para seguir una pista sobre el encubrimiento de un asesinato, Milo se da cuenta de que entre él y Nicole nunca nada es sencillo.
story_text_b:
Milo Boyd è un ex detective del dipartimento di polizia di New York che lavora come agente di riscossione cauzioni (cacciatore di taglie). L'ex moglie di Milo, Nicole Hurley, è una giornalista investigativa che è stata arrestata per aver aggredito un ufficiale di polizia.
Quando Nicole riceve un suggerimento su una storia, un apparente suicidio che potrebbe essere stato un omicidio, salta la sua udienza obbligazionaria per andare ad incontrare il suo informatore Jimmy, così il giudice revoca la sua cauzione ed emette un mandato per il suo arresto. Poco prima dell'arrivo di Nicole, Jimmy viene rapito.
Milo è sorpreso quando Sidman, il garante di Nicole, gli offre il compito di portarla in prigione, per una taglia di 5000 $. Dopo aver parlato con la madre di Nicole, Kitty, Milo la cattura in un ippodromo del New Jersey, la getta nel bagagliaio della sua auto e torna in auto verso Manhattan. Nicole riesce a scappare brevemente prima che Milo la raggiunga.
Sono perseguitati da due criminali inviati da Irene, un allibratore, a causa di debiti di gioco di Milo; Nicole viene seguita dal poliziotto corrotto Earl Mahler, che è collegato alla storia a cui sta indagando, ed entrambi dall’innamorato perso collega di Nicole, Stewart, che ha deciso di salvarla da Milo. I teppisti di Irene scambiano Stewart per Milo e lo rapiscono erroneamente.
Earl cerca di uccidere Nicole, ma sia Milo che Nicole scappano per un pelo. Milo non è interessato a spiegazioni fino a quando Nicole ammette di aver trovato prove che implicano il loro amico comune ed ex partner di Milo nella polizia, Bobby, indicando che è coinvolto con Earl. Milo decide di indagare con lei.
Indizi dalla macchina di Earl li portano in un country club, dove apprendono da un caddy che Earl possiede un negozio di tatuaggi nel Queens, quindi iniziano a dirigersi lì. Bobby avverte la coppia di rimanere lontano dalla strada.
L'hotel più vicino è il bed and breakfast dove hanno trascorso la luna di miele. Provano sentimenti reciproci e ammettono i loro errori. Nicole, uscendo dal bagno, sente Milo dire a Sid che potrebbe fare sesso con Nicole, ma che la sta ancora portando in prigione. Ammanetta Milo sul letto e si dirige verso il negozio di tatuaggi, trovando Jimmy e liberandolo prima che venga catturata dai teppisti di Irene.
Milo la salva in uno strip club dove stava per essere catturata. Chiama un vecchio amico delle forze di polizia e viene a sapere che Bobby si sta dirigendo verso il magazzino prove della polizia, che viene trasferito in un nuovo edificio. Bobby si confronta con Earl, che era suo amico ma ha usato il nome di Bobby per accedere al magazzino e rubare una grande quantità di narcotici e denaro. Bobby decide di arrestare Earl, ma Earl estrae la pistola e gli spara. Milo e Nicole entrano nel magazzino e a Milo viene tesa un'imboscata, ma Earl si arrende quando Nicole gli punta un fucile.
Bobby spiega che Earl lo stava usando, così come l'uomo che si presumeva si suicidasse, per ottenere l'accesso al magazzino. Non c'erano prove, quindi Bobby stava aspettando che Earl facesse la sua mossa prima di arrestarlo. Milo nota con orgoglio che Earl avrebbe potuto cavarsela se Nicole non avesse raccolto alcuni indizi. Lui e Nicole sembrano essersi riconciliati. Ammettono che a volte il loro lavoro deve venire prima. Milo consegna Nicole alla polizia, in modo che possa presentarsi all’udienza il giorno successivo.
Mentre esce dalla stazione di polizia, Milo incontra il poliziotto che lo ha insultato prima e gli dà un pugno in faccia. Viene arrestato e messo nella cella accanto a quella di Nicole. Le ricorda che è il loro anniversario e che lo devono passare insieme. Attraverso le sbarre ammettono il loro amore e si baciano.

story_text_a:
Colin Lamb, biologo marino e anche agente del controspionaggio inglese, è in Wilbraham Crescents alla ricerca del numero 61, quando dal n. 19 esce urlando una ragazza (Sheila Webb) molto carina che ha appena trovato un cadavere. Si era recata nell'appartamento perché la Signorina Pebmarsh aveva richiesto proprio la sua presenza, telefonando presso la copisteria dove la ragazza lavorava.
Il morto non abita però in quella casa, vi abita una donna cieca, la signorina Pebmarsh. Nell'appartamento vengono trovati, oltre agli orologi della proprietaria di casa, altri quattro orologi che segnano le ore 16 e 13. La polizia inizia a indagare, ma non si riesce a stabilire l'identità del cadavere. Lamb allora si rivolge a un amico, l'investigatore Hercule Poirot. Con il solito acume, l'investigatore riuscirà a scoprire l'identità del morto e anche l'assassino e a dare una mano a Lamb per risolvere il mistero che lo aveva portato a Wilbraham Crescents.
Il piano era stato architettato dalla signora Katherina Martindale per impedire all'uomo, che proveniva dal Canada, di scoprire la truffa ordita dalla sorella per ottenere un'eredità. L'idea degli orologi era stata tratta da un manoscritto che aveva avuto da uno scrittore, ma poi non più pubblicato per la morte dello stesso. Poirot, grande lettore di romanzi gialli, ne aveva una copia.
La casa che Lamb stava cercando era proprio il numero 19, perché il foglio con gli appunti che aveva era stato visto al contrario.
Vorrà dare anche la possibilità alla signorina Pebmarsh di fuggire, in quanto aveva scoperto che sarebbe stata la sua futura suocera, era infatti la madre di Sheila.
story_text_b:
On his way to visit the settlement on Wilbraham Crescent Road, Secret Service Special Agent Colin Lamb suddenly holds a young woman in his arms. She came screaming from the 19th house. Lamb was in the alley pursuing a lead that another agent had left before he was murdered. He'd recorded an M, a 61 and a crescent.
In the jacket pocket of the body that Sheila discovered, you will find a business card of an insurance agent named "R.H. Curry". This quickly turns out to be false because neither the insurance company nor an agent with that name exists.
Miss Martindale, Sheila's boss, states that the appointment at the home of the blind lady, Miss Pebmarsh, was arranged by telephone and that Miss Pebmarsh specifically requested Sheila. Miss Pebmarsh, however, denies having ordered Sheila.
Inspector Hardcastle joins Lamb at Miss Waterhouse's house number 18 to learn all about the neighborhood. A colorful mixture of different ages and social backgrounds. In house number 20, Mrs. Hemming lives in a house full of cats. In No. 61, just behind No. 19, Mr. and Mrs. Bland have just inherited a lot of money from a relative overseas. No. 62 is where Mrs. Ramsay lives with her two boys, who are a constant nuisance. Her husband, an engineer, often works abroad.
Sheila's getting suspicious now. Her aunt is being questioned, and she's testifying that Sheila's first name is Rosemary. The name was on the case of a travel clock that was found at the scene of the crime and now suddenly disappeared. Frustrated by the development, Lamb decides to contact Poirot, an old friend of his father. He visits Poirot, who now wants to solve the case from his armchair. Lamb describes the facts and leaves Poirot with a list of what to do next.
Edna Brent, a colleague of Sheila's, is completely confused because she has an important thought. She's trying to get in touch with Hardcastle, but he doesn't have time. She was later found dead in a telephone booth in Wilbraham Crescent, strangled with her own scarf.
A woman, Merlina Rival, enters the scene and identifies the body of "Mr. Curry" as her alleged husband, whom she has not seen in 15 years. The man had met her as Harry Castleton and had made it his profession to rob women of their savings. To confirm her identification, she says her husband has a scar behind his ear. Hardcastle quickly realizes that the scar isn't even 15 years old, so she couldn't have known about it. After he confronts her, she secretly calls the person from whom she received the assignment for the false identification, threatening to tell the truth. She'll be the third victim.
The investigation gains momentum when Colin meets ten-year-old Geraldine Brown. She had, because she had broken her leg, watched the proceedings in Wilbraham Crescent from her room with an opera glass. She reports that a new laundry service delivered a heavy bag of laundry on the day of the murder.
He also discovers that Mrs. Ramsay's husband has defected behind the Iron Curtain. Otherwise, she's not involved.
Poirot's idea now is that this seemingly complicated murder should distract from a very simple one. That's how the watches turn out to be Red Herring. Also, the appearance of Sheila and the confusion over the identity of the body are just a distraction. Edna, having returned to the office earlier from dinner because of a broken paragraph, had noticed that Miss Martindale had not called. And it turns out that Miss Martindale is Mrs. Bland's sister. Mrs. Bland is Mr. Bland's second wife, but the heiress to the overseas fortune was his first wife. Then suddenly Quentin Duguesclin showed up, who knew the first Bland woman from Canada. So he was murdered and put in Miss Pebmarsh's house. All of Miss Martindale's distractions came from a previously unpublished novel that she had copied in her office.
It also gives Poirot a clue to the other agent's mysterious note. It has always been held in the wrong place, and so now stands a W (for Wilbraham), a crescent (for Crescent) and a 19  Miss Pebmarsh's house. He can frame her as an agent, but he also knows now that she's Sheila's mother. Because Colin wants to marry Sheila, he's offering her escape. However, she does not accept his offer.

story_text_a:
While scrubbing the floor at home, Belle  is interrupted by her brother's friend Avenant  who tells her she deserves better and suggests they get married. Belle rejects Avenant, as she wishes to stay home and take care of her father, who has suffered much since his ships were lost at sea and the family fortune along with them. Belle's father arrives home announcing he has come into a great fortune that he will pick up the next day, along with gifts for his daughters, Belle and her shrewish sisters Adelaide and Felicie. Belle's roguish brother Ludovic, believing they will soon be wealthy, signs a contract from a moneylender allowing him the ability to sue Ludovic's father if he can't pay. Belle's sisters ask for a monkey and a parrot as gifts, but Belle asks only for a rose.
However, the next day, Belle's father finds on his arrival that his fortune has been seized to clear his debts and he is as penniless as before. He has no money for lodging and is forced to return home through a forest at night. He gets lost in the forest and finds himself at a large castle whose gates and doors magically open themselves. On entering the castle, he is guided by an enchanted candelabra that leads him to a laden dinner table where he falls asleep. Awakened by a loud roar, he wanders the castle's grounds. Remembering that Belle asked for a rose, he plucks a rose from a tree which makes the Beast appear. The Beast threatens to kill him for theft but suggests that one of his daughters can take his place. The Beast offers his horse Magnificent to guide him through the forest and to his home.
Belle's father explains the situation to his family and Avenant. Belle agrees to take her father's place and rides Magnificent to the castle. Upon meeting the Beast, Belle faints at his monstrous appearance and is carried to her room in the castle. Belle awakens to find a magic mirror which allows her to see anything. The Beast invites Belle to dinner, where he tells her that she's in equal command to him and that she will be asked every day to marry him. Days pass as Belle grows more accustomed to and fond of the Beast, but she continues to refuse marriage. Using the magic mirror, Belle sees that her father has become deathly ill. Belle begs for permission to visit her family, and the Beast reluctantly grants her permission to leave for a week. He gives Belle two magical items: a glove that can transport her wherever she wishes and a golden key that unlocks Diana's Pavilion, the source of the Beast's true riches. He tells Belle that he gives her these precious items to show his trust in her, and says that if she does not return at the end of the week, he will die of grief.
Belle uses the glove to appear in her bedridden father's room, where her visit restores him to health. Belle finds her family living in poverty, having never recovered from Ludovic's deal with the moneylender. Jealous of Belle's rich life at the castle, Adelaide and Felicie steal her golden key and devise a plan to turn Ludovic and Avenant against the Beast. Avenant and Ludovic devise a plan of their own to kill the Beast, and agree to aid Belle's sisters. To stall Belle, her sisters trick her into staying past her seven-day limit by pretending to love her. Belle reluctantly agrees to stay.
The Beast sends Magnificent with the magic mirror to retrieve Belle but Ludovic and Avenant find Magnificent first, and ride him to the castle. Belle later finds the mirror which reveals the Beast's sorrowful face in its reflection. Belle realizes she is missing the golden key as the mirror breaks. Distraught, Belle returns to the castle using the magic glove and finds the Beast in the courtyard, near death from a broken heart.
Meanwhile, Avenant and Ludovic stumble upon Diana's Pavilion. Thinking that their stolen key may trigger a trap, they scale the wall of the Pavilion. As the Beast dies in Belle's arms, Avenant breaks into the Pavilion through its glass roof, whereupon he is shot with an arrow by an animated statue of the Roman goddess Diana and is himself turned into a Beast. As this happens, arising from where the Beast lay dead is Prince Ardent who is cured of being the Beast. He explains that because his parents did not believe in spirits, in revenge the spirits turned him into the Beast. Prince Ardent and Belle embrace, then fly away to his kingdom where she will be his Queen. He promises that her father will stay with them and Belle's sisters will carry the train of her gown.
story_text_b: Bertha Thompson's father, pressed by her employer to finish his work, dies before her eyes. Since that incident, she's been traveling in cattle cars, crisscrossing Great Depression America. She meets a young unionist who is trying to get the railroad workers to strike and then a gambler who carries a revolver. She follows them on their adventures.

story_text_a:
Raven, killer a pagamento, viene assoldato da Willard Gates per uccidere un certo Baker e sottrargli dei documenti. Dopo averlo sfruttato, Gates lo paga con banconote segnate in modo che la polizia possa catturarlo.
Mentre lo inseguono per arrestarlo, Raven riesce a scappare giurando di vendicarsi e incontra Ellen Graham, un'artista di night club che in realtà è la fidanzata di un poliziotto, Michael Crane, e un'agente del controspionaggio. La ragazza lavora per il governo che cerca di smascherare Alvin Brewster, mandante di Gates e presidente di un'importante industria chimica, che lavora in realtà per i giapponesi.
Ellen cerca di salvare Raven e di convincerlo a collaborare con la giustizia per smascherare i veri criminali. Accortosi di essere stato tradito, Raven uccide i traditori ma viene a sua volta abbattuto dalla polizia.
story_text_b: A contract killer, Phillip Raven (Alan Ladd) shoots an industrialist, a police informant, and soon realizes that he was paid with dirty money. Pursued by the police, Raven encounters Ellen Graham (Veronica Lake), the fiancée of the detective tracking him, on his trip to Los Angeles. However, Ellen who is a magician and nightclub singer will be of great help to him, as Raven wants to find her sponsor Willard Gates (Laird Cregar), a nightclub owner, and take revenge. Melville will use the film as inspiration for his "Samurai"

story_text_a:
Dr. Jan Żabiński and his wife, Antonina, run the Warsaw Zoo, one of the largest zoos in Europe. The couple lovingly cares for the animals. However, when Germany invaded Poland on September 1, 1939, marking the beginning of World War II, the zoo was hit by bombs dropped by the Wehrmacht's Luftwaffe. Plants are destroyed and wild animals roam free.
Jan is worried about Antonina and her young son Ryszard, but they can't leave town. Dr. Lutz Heck, the director of the Berlin Zoo and Hitler's chief zoologist, informs Antonina that the zoo is being liquidated. He initially offers to take over the best animals, but on his next visit in the winter, he shoots some of the animals.
In October 1940, the city's Jews were taken to the Warsaw Ghetto. The Żabińskis talk with their Jewish friends Maurycy Fraenkel and Magda Gross about Szymon Tenenbaum's insect collection, which they hide in the basement. But Antonina has another idea: she also wants to offer Magda a hiding place in the house.
Jan initially reacts skeptically because of the danger, but after Magda has come to them, he reveals an even greater plan. He supports the Home Army, which provides temporary shelter for Jews before they are moved to safe houses in other parts of the country. Antonina describes the plan as a "human zoo", but she agrees. The couple go to Heck and suggest that he open a pig farm at the zoo to feed the soldiers. The food for the animals should come from the ghetto. Heck also dreams of reviving the extinct aurochs. After the pigs and bison are delivered to the zoo, Antonina speaks of using Heck's personal interest in her to control him.
Jan goes to the ghetto to collect kitchen waste. But he hides Jews in his truck to take them to the zoo. He also takes the girl Urszula, who is traumatized after being raped by Nazis. Antonina slowly finds access to Urszula by telling about her own childhood and giving the child a rabbit. More and more Jews are coming to the Żabińskis. Antonina's piano music serves late at night as a sign that the Jews can come out of hiding, and during the day as a warning. Especially when Heck's in the house, it gets dangerous. The Żabińskis also try to free some of the Jews by bleaching their hair to make them look Aryan.
Jan observes Antonina and Heck getting closer during the mating of a bison. Then a Dr. Ziegler comes to them and reports Simon's death. Ziegler is the head of the employment office whose building borders the ghetto. He knows about the commitment of the Żabińskis and offers to use the passage to bring more Jews out of the ghetto. That's how Jan saves Maurycy.
In August 1942, the evacuation of the ghetto begins. Jan can not prevent many children and the pedagogue Janusz Korczak from getting on a train going to the concentration camp. Back at the zoo, the couple argue. Jan is blaming Antonina for her relationship with Heck. When she speaks of fear, he points out that many people are dying nearby. But Antonina believes that the couple was handed over to the Nazis.
In April 1943, Roza Anzelowna and her mother, two light-haired women rescued by the Żabińskis, are discovered in their new hiding place and shot by the Nazis. On the evening of April 19, the eve of Hitler's birthday, the people at the zoo learn of the impending destruction of the ghetto in connection with the uprising there. While the Nazis burn down the ghetto, the Jews secretly celebrate a Seder at the beginning of Passover. Later, Heck observes an argument between Jan and Ryszard. He challenges the boy who claims his father is in Zalesie. However, after Heck leaves the house, he hears Ryszard shouting "Hitler is broken", a saying he has seen in the ghetto.
Later Antonina gives birth to the girl Teresa. Jan participated in the Warsaw Uprising in August 1944. In the process, he is shot and captured.
In January 1945, as the German troops prepare to withdraw, Antonina goes to the rear to find out about the whereabouts of her husband. However, because of Ryszard's statement, he suspects that the Żabińskis have something to hide, and suggests to rape Antonina. Antonina hurries back to the zoo and can quickly get the hidden Jews into a truck that will take them away from the zoo before Heck arrives with other soldiers. Heck finds in the basement the drawings that the Jews have painted on the walls. In a tunnel, he chases Ryszard and he locks Antonina in a cage. He's pretending to shoot the boy. Then he leaves the zoo for good. Antonina and her son join the march from Warsaw, releasing a young bison.
After the surrender of the Wehrmacht in September 1945, the people of Warsaw work to rebuild the city and Antonina returns with the children to the zoo, where she meets the faithful employee Jerzyk. The rebuilding of the zoo has also begun. The following spring, Jan shows up. The Żabińskis are painting stars of David all over the zoo. They saved 300 Jews, and 20 years later, they're honored by Yad Vashem as Righteous Among the Nations.
story_text_b: It is the true story about the caretakers of the Warsaw Zoo, Antonina and Jan Żabiński, who saved about three hundred Jews from the Holocaust during World War II by hiding them in animal cages.[2] It is based on Antonina's personal diary.[3]

story_text_a:
La historia comienza en una ciudad centroeuropea en medio de la guerra a finales del siglo XVIII. Entre explosiones y disparos de un gran ejército turco situado en las afueras, tiene lugar una fantástica puesta en escena teatral sobre la vida y las aventuras del barón de Münchhausen. Entre bastidores, el oficial Jackson refuerza el compromiso de la ciudad con la razón, es decir con la uniformidad y la normalidad, ordenando la ejecución de un soldado que ha acabado de realizar actos de valor sobrehumano, argumentando que su valentía está desmoralizando a los otros soldados.
Poco después en el curso de representación, un hombre mayor que alega ser el verdadero Barón interrumpe la representación, protestando por sus múltiples inexactitudes. Entre las quejas de la audiencia, la compañía teatral y Jackson, el "verdadero" Barón se gana la atención de todos y narra sus aventuras, comenzando por una apuesta de vida o muerte con el Gran Turco, cuando de joven debió su vida a su increíble suerte y a la ayuda de sus notables colaboradores: Berthold, el corredor más veloz del mundo; Adolphus, un tirador con una vista sobrehumana; Gustavus, quien posee un extraordinario oído y poder pulmonar como para derrotar a un ejército al exhalar; y Albrecht, un hombre descomunalmente fuerte.
Cuando un disparo de cañón interrumpe la narración del Barón ya anciano, la representación se ve opacada por la urgencia de salvar la ciudad. El Barón deambula tras bambalinas esperando la muerte, pero con su entusiasta interrogatorio Sally Salt, la hija del director de la compañía teatral, lo convence de permanecer con vida.
Insistiendo en que él solo puede salvar a la ciudad, el Barón escapa en un globo de aire caliente construido con ropa interior femenina, sin darse cuenta de que Sally se ha colado como polizón. La expedición en globo llega a la Luna, donde el Barón, rejuvenecido por la huida, encuentra a su antiguo asociado Berthold, pero discute con el Rey de la Luna, quien tiene celos del Barón por su pasado romántico con su mujer, la Reina de la Luna.
Tras escapar de la Luna por medio de una cuerda, el trío regresa a la Tierra, aterrizando en la morada del dios romano Vulcano recibe a sus invitados con cortesía y donde Albrecht se encuentra. Su esposa, la diosa Venus, traza un interludio romántico danzando un vals aéreo, por lo que se acaba la hospitalidad de Vulcano, quien expulsa ahora al grupo de cuatro hacia los mares del sur.
Devorados por una enorme criatura marina, los viajeros ubican a Gustavus, Adolphus, y a Bucéfalo, el fiel caballo del Barón. El Barón (quien de nuevo luce anciano tras ser -en sus propias palabras- "expulsado de un estado de beatitud") lucha contra los objetivos contradictorios de heroísmo y una muerte tranquila, antes de decidirse a escapar soplando "un poquito de rapé" dentro el cavernoso interior de la criatura, lo que hace que la criatura marina "estornude" a los héroes a través de su agujero nasal similar al de una ballena.
De regreso en tierra, el ejército turco está listo, pero los ayudantes del Barón están demasiado viejos para luchar como en los viejos días. El Barón los sermonea con firmeza sin ningún provecho, y abandona el lugar con la intención de rendirse a los turcos y a Jackson. Pero sus amigos no lo permiten, y lo salvan junto a la ciudad.
Durante el desfile de celebración, el Barón es sin embargo asesinado por Jackson, cuya figura se confunde con la de la muerte. El funeral es público y muy emotivo, pero su desenlace muestra que tan sólo se trata de la escena final de otra historia, que el Barón está contando a los mismos asistentes del teatro del principio de la cinta. El Barón se refiere a ella como "sólo una de las  muchas ocasiones en que conoció a la muerte" y termina su historia diciendo "todo aquel que tuvo el talento para hacerlo, fue entonces feliz para siempre."
Un ambiguo final muestra que la ciudad ha sido de hecho salvada, aunque los eventos de la batalla aparentemente sucedieron en la historia, y no en la realidad. El Barón se aleja cabalgando en Bucéfalo. Bañados por la luz solar, desaparecen entre las nubes, y a los créditos de la cinta los acompaña una explosión musical.
story_text_b:
In a city besieged by the Turks, a play tells the adventures of the famous Baron of Münchhausen. Then an old man appears, claiming to be the  real  Baron of Münchhausen. He makes a scene and interrupts the play. Horatio Jackson, the town's leader, a notorious scornful man, ignores him while the troopers think he's crazy. Only Sally, the daughter of the theater company manager, takes him seriously. He tells him how, with the help of his companions Berthold, Adolphus, Albrecht and Gustavus, he gained the sultan's treasure, and thus started the war.
While enjoying a delicious wine in the sultan's palace, Münchhausen tells his host that he knows a better wine. The sultan, both insulted and intrigued, takes a bet with the baron that he will be able to taste this wine within the hour. If Münchhausen succeeds (that is, if the wine is there and is indeed better than the sultan's), he can take from the treasury anything a giant can carry. If he loses, he loses his head. Berthold, an extremely fast runner, was sent to Vienna, but fell asleep on the way home. Gustavus, thanks to his excellent hearing and his powerful breath (this gift will be revealed during the battle between the baron and the soldiers of the sultan), marks him, and Adolphus, thanks to his sight and his rifle, wakes him by dropping an apple on him. Münchhausen wins his bet, and Albrecht, the giant with superhuman strength, manages to take the entire treasure with them. This puts the sultan in a mad rage, and ignites the war.
In the besieged city, Münchhausen decides to go and get his comrades, from whom he was separated a few years ago, in order to lift the siege. So he flees in a balloon, a balloon made with women's panties (long panties, anyway), and goes to the moon to find the first of his former companions, Berthold. Sally followed him, so she's running out of town with him. On the way, they see Death, who has been trying in vain to reach Münchhausen for years.
They balloon up to the Moon, where they are greeted by the Moon King and Queen. They can separate their heads from their bodies; they also have a mood change (lunatic), becoming milder, more peaceful and calm when their heads and bodies are separated. The Queen is under the spell of the baron, who is gradually rejuvenated. The King notices this, and locks Sally and Münchhausen in a large cage, where Berthold is already. But this one doesn't remember anything, and shouts that his name is Desmond, and that he doesn't know the baron. The Queen's head, while her body is near her husband, saves them; they manage to escape the King and fall from the moon.
They fall into a volcano, home to Vulcan's forge. With the help of his Cyclops, he manufactured many weapons. They find Albrecht in the forge, now tender and delicate, fulfilling the duties of a maid by serving tea. The comrades also meet Venus, Vulcan's wife and a perfect match for one of the actresses in Sally's theater troupe. Venus seduces Münchhausen, and he kisses her. Vulcan then becomes enraged and drives them out of his kingdom by throwing them into the sea. Albrecht courageously followed them. That's when all four of them were swallowed by the Kraken.
Inside the Kraken, Münchhausen begins to lose the youth he had regained until now. In the monster's stomach are many ships, inside which aging sailors play to pass the time. Gustavus has become deaf, and Adolphus has become blind. Münchhausen, tired, begins a game of cards, when Sally recognizes frightened in his opponent Death, that the baron expects war tired. Sally defeats Death and Münchhausen, regaining his youth, uses snuff to make the monster sneeze and spit them out through his vent. Münchhausen, reassured, set sail in the boat they had recovered from the city and its besiegers. Their arrival interrupted negotiations between Jackson and the sultan, who apparently attacked and fought each other in turn, exchanging treasure for treaties.
Münchhausen and his companions all regained their youthful vigor. Berthold regained his memory and speed, Albrecht his strength, and Adolphus his marksmanship. Gustavus did not lose his breath, and hurled a small mouse into the midst of the fighting elephants, who broke their chains and ransacked the enemy camp. The city is saved, and its heroes triumph. But Jackson, hidden behind a large statue of an angel, killed Münchhausen with a shotgun, avenging the losses he had suffered at the end of the siege. Then the statue comes to life, and Death reappears. This time, she seizes the soul of Münchhausen; he is buried with honors, and a monument is built over his grave.
We later find ourselves in the theater as the story presented was only a Münchhausen narrative to the members of the theater troupe, as well as to those of the spectators (including Jackson) who stayed to listen to it. When the baron finally stops and declares the story to be true, no one believes him. Nevertheless, Münchhausen emerged from the theater with the gates of the city wide open - the enemy army had disappeared. Münchhausen goes back on his horse, leaving his admirers behind.

story_text_a: Durant l'été 1977, le jeune Scott Thorson (en), dresseur de chiens, entre dans la loge du célèbre pianiste Liberace. Malgré leur différence d'âge et leurs origines sociales opposées, les deux hommes entament une liaison secrète. Cette relation, souvent orageuse, va durer cinq ans.
story_text_b:
It's 1977. After a difficult childhood and adolescence, eighteen-year-old Scott Thorson travels to Los Angeles to look for work as a veterinarian; here, in a gay bar, he meets theater producer Bob Black, who invites him to Las Vegas to attend a show of his friend, the famous pianist Liberace, at the time at the peak of his fame. Scott is introduced to the pianist, who is immediately fascinated by him; offering him to care for his elderly dog, the young man begins to frequent his sumptuous residence: soon the two will begin to exchange confidences and intimacy, until they begin a real relationship.
Scott declares to Liberace that he is bisexual, while Liberace replies that he has always been homosexual, despite hiding it from the public; the pianist is also a fervent Catholic despite the fact that the Church does not approve of homosexual relationships: he tells him of the meeting he had years earlier with a messenger of God, after which he was convinced that God loves him as he is. Liberace is very fond of Scott, takes him to live with him and covers him with jewelry and other precious gifts; later he will make him perform in his show and will even propose to adopt him, without success.
Little by little, however, the dark side of Liberace emerges, obsessed with his public image to the point of paying his manager Seymour profusely to invent any excuse to justify the absence of a woman at his side. The pianist is also morbidly jealous of his physical appearance, so much so that he undergoes drastic diets and continuous plastic surgery, forcing Scott to do the same to become a "younger version" of him; however, this will create a gradual fracture in the couple as Scott, to lose weight, begins to use amphetamines in increasing doses. The boy will end up paying for his doses by selling the jewels given to him by Liberace, and having frequent bouts of nervousness because of which Liberace will gradually distance himself from him.
The couple's crisis lasts until 1982: Scott is now totally addicted to drugs and, although he continues to live in Liberace's house, there is no longer any relationship between the two. When the pianist becomes infatuated with the young singer Cary-James, he begins to regularly cheat on Scott, even on the day he is in Los Angeles for his adoptive mother's funeral. This causes a violent reaction from Scott, following which the two separate. In 1984 a bitter legal battle takes place in which Scott sues Liberace for defamation, demanding the conversion into money of the properties titled to him in the years of their relationship; all he gets is a decent sum of money and some gifts offered in exchange for silence on his relationship with Liberace.
Scott returns to live a much more modest and secluded life than he did with Liberace. In December 1986 he receives a call from the latter, who, knowing that he is dying due to AIDS contracted some time ago, asks him to see him one last time. The two ex-lovers manage to say a final goodbye before Liberace dies, on February 4, 1987; despite Seymour's efforts to keep the illness hidden, the true cause of his death soon emerges. At the funeral, Scott imagines Liberace performing in his final, lavish show before soaring off to heaven.

story_text_a: The action takes place under the Rashō gate from which the novel takes its name. One night, a starving man takes shelter from the rain and discovers an old woman pulling the hair of the corpses. This account of Akutagawa Ryūnosuke's youth is steeped in a dark and strange atmosphere.
story_text_b:
# General presentation
A few years after the Civil War, coachman O.B. Jackson drove in his diligence the bounty hunter John Ruth and his captive, Daisy Domergue, to Red Rock, Wyoming. On the road they meet Major Marquis Warren, a former Union soldier and bounty hunter, and Chris Mannix, the new sheriff of Red Rock. Surprised by the blizzard, the five find shelter in a cabin already occupied by four other people: Bob, who takes care of the relay in the absence of the owner, Oswaldo Mobray, the executioner of Red Rock, herdsman Joe Gage and Confederate General Sanford Smithers. Trapped by the storm, the nine travelers prepare to live together when the killing begins: one of the occupants is an accomplice of Daisy who is ready to kill them all to get her to escape.
# Detailed synopsis
## Chapter one:
A stagecoach driven by a man named O.B. Jackson, move through the snow. On the way, the stagecoach encounters a bounty hunter, Major Marquis Warren, a former cavalry officer in the Union Army. The latter wishes to bring to Red Rock the bodies of three wanted criminals in order to recover the bounty on their heads. So he makes a deal with the coach's occupant, bounty hunter John Ruth. The latter also brings a catch to Red Rock, but a live one: Daisy Domergue. He agrees to take Warren to Red Rock, but warns him not to try anything to steal the bounty on Daisy. After a few exchanges during which Warren presents John Ruth with a letter written by Abraham Lincoln, Daisy spits on the letter and Warren punches her, dragging her off the stage, logically accompanied by John Ruth, who is handcuffed to her. Warren stops the stage to bring his traveling companions back up. Before you go, O.B. Another man walks up to them through the snow. Out of vigilance, Ruth orders Warren to put on handcuffs, in case he and the other man are complicit in both having Daisy as their prisoner.
## Chapter two:
The man in question is a man named Chris Mannix who introduces himself as the new sheriff of Red Rock. The latter, who says he had to slaughter his injured horse, is finally accepted by the two bounty hunters. Along the way, Ruth, who has just denounced Warren for never teaming up with Chris, reveals that the latter's father, Erskine Mannix, led the Mannix Marauders aka the Plague of South Carolina, a troop of Confederate soldiers who became rebels during and after the war, specializing in the slaughter of blacks, Chris being a part of; the latter thus attracts Warren's animosity. Mannix, for his part, reveals that the major's head was put up for auction by the Confederacy (initially at $30,000, then lower over time). Warren confesses to escaping from his prison camp by setting it on fire, killing 47 Confederate soldiers in their sleep. Returning home, Warren was immediately discharged from the army because of the 37 Northern prisoners also killed in the flames; only his brilliant service record saved him from execution. He fought in the mountains against all the people in his wake for a bounty, and none of those he crossed turned back.
## Chapter three:
O.B., Ruth, Warren, Daisy and Mannix now arrive at the last stop before Red Rock: Minnie's Laundry. This large cabin, usually kept by Minnie and her husband Dave, known as  the Good Dough, serves as a resting place for travelers. However, Minnie and Sweet Dave are absent. Bob, a Mexican working for Minnie, informs Warren that Minnie has left him in charge of the lace shop while she visits her mother with Dave. Warren can't help but notice that it doesn't look like Minnie, but he doesn't insist. Meanwhile, O.B. and Mannix are out planting picket fences to mark a path from the mercery to the latrines, while John Ruth and his prisoner enter the mercery, where there are already three other people: Oswaldo Mobray, the Red Rock executioner, Joe Gage, a cowboy, who says he's on his way to see his mother, and old Confederate General Sanford Smithers, who's going to Red Rock to tend to the gravestone of his deceased son, Chester Charles Smithers, who's gone missing in the area.
A certain tension develops between the protagonists. In fact, John Ruth fears that someone may want to pocket the bounty on Daisy Domergue instead, or that one or more of the occupants may be complicit with Domergue, who came to free her. He then makes a deal with Warren and confiscates the guns of everyone present except Warren's. The latter, in turn, faced the animosity of General Smithers, who executed many blacks at the Battle of Baton Rouge, in which Warren participated. Warren is on the verge of killing him in cold blood, but Mannix and Mobray both remind him of what it might cost him to kill an unarmed man. Because of this tension, Oswaldo proposes to  cut  the hut in half, between the Northern and Southern partisans, with the dining table as neutral territory; the group then calmly eats the stew freshly prepared by Bob. During the meal, Mannix claims that the letter from Abraham Lincoln that Warren is carrying is a forgery, which Warren confirms, claiming that this letter serves to guarantee him the respect of the whites, as was the case with John Ruth who allowed him to travel in his diligence. Warren, sitting in the chair of  Dave the Good Dough, then begins to argue with General Smithers, whom he eventually provokes by claiming to have captured, tortured, raped, and eventually killed his son. Smithers, next to whom Warren had deposited one of his revolvers, attempts to shoot Warren, but Warren kills him first, in self-defense.
## Chapter four:
However, while this first murder takes place and everyone seems busy, a character (not explicitly shown on the screen) poisons the coffee served by John Ruth. Only Daisy witnesses the scene and keeps silent. John Ruth and O.B. both drink it, and as Mannix is about to drink it, they begin to vomit blood. John Ruth hits a hilarious Daisy, but she manages to grab the bounty hunter's revolver and shoots him, before being disarmed by Warren. Still handcuffed to John Ruth, she can't really move because of the weight of the body. O.B. also dies from the effects of the poisoning. Warren then orders the other four men to stand against the wall of the tannery and obey him while he searches for the murderer. Deciding to trust Mannix, who also nearly drank the poison, he gives him Ruth's revolver and asks him to keep the other three in check. Claiming that one of these three other men is here to free Daisy, Warren then confronts Mexican Bob, whom he accuses of being a liar. Indeed, Warren claims that Bob's stew that they ate (and prepared the same morning) tastes exactly the same as that of his old friend Minnie, the mercery owner, yet absent for a week, and he finally shows that a large bloodstain was hidden on Sweet Dave's own chair ("The Good Dough"), which he allegedly brought with him. Besides, Minnie hates Mexicans, so she would never have let him have her lace shop. Based on these clues, Warren deduced that Bob was an impostor and killed him.
Warren, however, knows that Bob is not the one who poisoned the coffee since he was playing the piano during Smithers' murder: he was just an accomplice. He then threatens Mobray and Gage to make Daisy drink the rest of the poisoned coffee if the culprit does not come forward. Joe Gage then confesses to having poisoned the coffee, but before Mannix can execute him, an individual hiding under the floorboards of the hardware store shoots Warren and hits him between the legs. Mobray, using a pistol he had hidden on him, fires at Mannix, who responds and wounds Mobray. Mannix, wounded in the abdomen, grabs Gage by the cheek without firing at him, unarmed as he is.
## Chapter five:
A reversal then opens up. Several hours earlier, a stagecoach, driven by one Judy "Six Horses" and her colleague Ed, arrived at Minnie's hardware store with four passengers: Mobray, Gage, Bob and another man named Jody. The latter, after settling in, murder everyone present, including Minnie and Sweet Dave, except General Smithers. Jody makes a deal with him: Smithers will have to say nothing about what happened, open his mouth only to say the bare minimum, such as "hello", and in exchange he will have his life saved, which he gladly accepts, not caring what happened to the other people. But during the massacre, Bob pulls on the door handle, which is why now you have to nail two planks to the door so that it closes and you can kick it violently when you come in from the outside. The fourth man then reveals his full identity: Jody Domergue, Daisy's brother, whom he intends to free. After hiding the bodies in a well next to the laundry room and cleaning up the bloodstains, the four men hide weapons in the laundry room while Jody, borrowing a trapdoor, hides under the floor in the basement. A few hours later, John Ruth arrives with Domergue, O.B., Mannix and Warren.
## The last chapter:
Back to the present. Warren and Mannix, both in very bad shape, force Jody out of hiding, threatening to kill Daisy, while taking care to force him to get rid of his weapons. Jody gets out, but before he can do anything for his sister, Warren executes her. Daisy, enraged, tries to strike a deal with Mannix. If he shoots Warren and lets her go, he can take Bob's body to Red Rock to collect the reward offered for his capture. Bob, whose real nickname is Marco the Mexican, is, like the rest of the people in this room, a member of Domergue's gang, each of whose members is wanted for at least ten thousand dollars. Daisy tells them that about fifteen bandits are present in Red Rock, ready to kill Mannix and ravage the city, if he does not behave as Daisy wishes. However, Warren, irritated by Domergue's provocations and a dying Mobray, shoots Daisy in the foot before firing again at the still-dying Mobray (even revealing his nickname, Pete Hicox the Englishman), who was offering his own body to Mannix to validate the deal. Joe Gage (also revealing his nickname, Grouch Douglass) grabs a gun hidden under a table but is shot by Warren and Mannix. Warren decides to shoot Daisy as well when he runs out of bullets. Mannix, who believes Daisy is bluffing about the fifteen bandits, decides to shoot her instead, but collapses, having lost too much blood. Warren, panicked because he could barely move, watched in horror as Domergue moved back and forth, weighed down by John Ruth's corpse, to grab Douglass' revolver; fortunately for them, Mannix regained consciousness and wounded her before she could reach the gun. Mannix and Warren then decided to hang her from a beam in the mercery, in honor of John Ruth (who always brought criminals back alive to be hanged, hence his nickname "the Executioner"). After the execution, both of them, badly wounded, decide to await death by rereading Lincoln's fake letter to Warren.

story_text_a: After making a mistake that cost the life of one of his colleagues and left his best friend a quadriplegic, Inspector Carl Mørck (Nikolaj Lie Kaas) is relegated to a new department dedicated to archived cases. Carl, along with his new partner of Syrian origin Hafez al-Assad (Fares Fares), becomes aware of the numerous irregularities committed in the case of Marete Lyngaard (Sonja Richter), a young promise of Danish politics disappeared in 2002 while making a ferry trip accompanied by his brother with mental disability.
story_text_b:
Black Bill is a mysterious vigilante who rides singing across the prairies and fights for the rights of the innocent. No one knows it's Freddy, whose parents were once killed by Desperados. Freddy, also known as Black Bill, returns after many years to the ranch of old Ted Daniels, where he grew up after the death of his parents. But Ted's been kidnapped by bandits because he knows about a legendary gold vein. Black Bill travels to the notorious gold-mining town of Moon Valley to hunt down the unscrupulous criminals. He has no idea that Ted's daughter Anita, whom he last saw as a child, is also staying there.
When Anita learns from the sheriff's sister that he's always drunk, she quickly becomes Moon Valley's deputy sheriff and goes by the name Betty Wilson. Meanwhile, Black Bill, who again poses as John Burns, meets a man named Steve Perkins, who rules the city like a despot. His fiancée, Olivia, has only recently learned that Perkins is also the head of the infamous Moon Valley gang that Ted Daniels captured in the basement of the saloon. The thugs don't know that the blueprint for the gold vein is in Daniel's pocket watch, which was taken from him by a gang member.
Through a series of coincidences, Anita gains possession of the pocket watch and suspects the alleged John Burns of being involved in the robbery of the ranch. Olivia discovers that Burns is Black Bill and reveals to him that Perkins is the head of the gang. The next day, Burns starts spreading the rumor that he's leaving town with Olivia. He sets a trap for Perkins, and it becomes a dramatic chase. During a shootout, Anita shows up unexpectedly. She still thinks Black Bill is the alleged criminal John Burns and has him arrested. It's not until they're in Moon Valley Prison that they both discover their true identities. In the end, Freddy, aka Black Bill, manages to free Ted and bring down Steve Perkins once and for all.

story_text_a: In a small village in Holland in 1943, the German occupation and the war penetrate deeper and deeper into the lives of the children. The two twelve-year-old boys Lambert and Tuur are best friends, although Lambert's father sympathizes with the Germans and Tuur's family with the resistance. At first the boys don't tell anyone about the hiding place of a downed Allied pilot in a tunnel system that they found together. However, after Tuur discovers that families from the neighborhood are being deported in freight cars, he becomes radicalized. He finally understands that his parents and older brother are active in the resistance against the Germans. In Lambert, whose father has meanwhile been appointed mayor by the Germans, he begins to see a traitor. When Tuur flirts with his new classmate Maartje and turns his back on Lambert, Lambert reveals that Maartje's host family is hiding a pig from the occupiers. Little does he know that he is putting the lives of Maartje –- whose real name is Tamar and is Jewish –- and her host family in danger. When Tuur follows the arrested Tamar to Maastricht and is arrested himself, Lambert promises his father that he will join the Nazi youth if he gets Tuur out of prison. Shortly after Tuur's release, Maartje's host father, under torture, betrays the other members of the resistance. Although the entire village is surrounded by German soldiers, Tuur and his family are able to flee to Belgium via the tunnels. Lambert supports them in this by bringing them food and other supplies. The fate of Tamar and the other villagers remains unknown.

story_text_a:
October of 1945. 19-year-old German prisoner of war Mark Niebuhr arrives with other prisoners at a Warsaw train station. A Polish woman waiting for her train believes she recognizes the SS officer who murdered her daughter during a raid in Lublin. Niebuhr sees her talking to one of his Polish guards, but cannot understand the content of the conversation. Shortly thereafter, he is taken away and placed in solitary confinement in a prison.
The former grenadier of an infantry unit does not know why he is being detained. When questioned by a young Polish officer, he is repeatedly asked to write down his resume and give his real name. Niebuhr does not understand the harassment he is subjected to, and keeps insisting that he is just Mark Niebuhr.
In prison, he experiences the hatred of a Polish fellow prisoner, and during work assignments, he is assigned to the most dangerous tasks. So he has to unsecured, sitting on the wall of a bombed-out Warsaw house, throwing stones and breaking his arm in an accident.
At the hospital, he learns that he's being investigated for murder. He is transferred to a new cell where other German prisoners of war are already being held. Among them there is a strict military order based on their former ranks. Corps spirit and fascist ideals are reflected in this microcosm led by General Eisensteck and Major Lundenbroich. Niebuhr is the new guy who's slowly getting to know the others. Everybody tells him he's innocent. But Niebuhr slowly realizes that he's in a cell with murderers, hangmen, and real war criminals. He begins to distance himself from them, isolates himself, and is eventually rejected by them. During the months of his imprisonment in this cell, he is persuaded that as a German soldier he has incurred personal guilt.
As the rest of the prisoners are taken one by one to be executed, Mark Niebuhr's story is finally believed. Although one of his former comrades refuses to identify him during a confrontation, the Polish woman's accusation is recognized as a mistake and he is eventually released.
story_text_b:
Dr. Thomas Abernathy, the owner of Filadyne company, is leading the experiment in the particle accelerator in Luxembourg to create a small black hole which would be used as the powerful energy source. Although another scientist Dr. Soderstrom, who is present at the test site, tries to stop the experiment due to the possible danger, the experiment is started and the black hole created. However, the experiment goes awry and the black hole destroys the accelerator and claims the life of Dr. Soderstrom, as well as the lives of other personnel present in the control room.
Eight years later, his daughter Dr. Eva Soderstrom discovers that Dr. Abernathy has built a new accelerator and so she wants to prove he was responsible for the death of her father. She approaches professor Steven Price who works for Filadyne who could provide her with the data about the company activities. After she learns that Dr. Abernathy plans a new experiment, whose consequences are underestimated because of erroneous calculation, she is determined to stop him. Despite her best efforts, the experiment is started and again goes out of control and the black hole threatens to either suck in the whole planet or cause very devastating explosion. The majority of personnel escapes thanks to the actions of Dr. Sondestrom while Dr. Abernathy is sucked into the black hole. The AEC prepares the report and classifies all information about the experiment.

story_text_a:
Several odd occurrences, including a suspicious fire, happen at the farm where Alec Ramsay (Kelly Reno) and his mother (Teri Garr) stable Alec's horse, the Black. One night, the Black is taken away. Sheik Ishak (Ferdy Mayne) says he is responsible, claiming the stallion is his stolen property that he has retrieved, learning his whereabouts after the Black's win in the Match Race. The Black's real name is Shêtân. After learning the sheik is returning the Black to his kingdom in the Moroccan desert, Alec stows away on a plane to Casablanca.
In Morocco, Alec is found on the plane and taken to the American embassy. The police intend to return him to the United States. At the stables, he makes some friends who disguise him as a local Casablancan. They take him to a man named Kurr (Allen Garfield) the leader of a rogue tribe called the Uruk, who is interested in the Black and Sheik Ishak. He allows Alec to travel with him and another man, but they abandon Alec in the desert after the truck breaks down. Alec is picked up by another truck driver. Aboard the truck, he meets Raj (Vincent Spano), who speaks English, and says the Black will probably compete in "The Great Race". The two become friends and travel across the desert on foot with Meslar (Woody Strode), Raj's friend and mentor. Then the Uruk kidnap Meslar, and  Raj and Alec defend themselves against the harsh elements. After running out of water, they collapse but recover when they find a river. Raj's tribe discovers them, welcoming Raj home and Alec to the tribe. Raj takes Alec to the outskirts of Ishak's domain where he is reunited with the Black.
While attempting to retrieve the Black, Alec is apprehended by Ishak's men. He pleads his case to Sheik Ishak, who is sympathetic but will not give up the Black. He is racing the stallion in the "Great Race" with his granddaughter, Tabari (Jodi Thelen) as the rider. Alec insists the Black can only win if he rides him. Denied, Alec coaches Tabari, but the Black throws her off. Then, the Uruk led by Kurr, capture the Black and Alec to a hidden location. Alec escapes with the Black. As they flee, Alec discovers that Meslar is being held prisoner and gives him his pocket knife to cut his bonds. Alec and the Black escape to Ishak's. As a reward for safely returning the Black, Alec is allowed to ride him in the race.
On race day, Alec reunites with Raj, who is also competing. They and the other riders begin their run across the desert. The Uruk's rider tries to kill Alec, but he and the Black escape. Alec discovers that the Uruk's rider pushed Raj off his horse. He returns Raj's mount to him. Together, they race against the Uruk rider until Meslar appears and spooks the rider's horse, unseating him. Suddenly, Kurr chases Raj and Alec in his truck, shooting at them. However, the truck crashes into a ditch.
Alec wins the race, then pleads with Ishak to spare Raj's horse, despite the winning sheik taking any horses he chooses. Ishak grants the reprieve, which allows Alec to repay Raj for his kindness. Meslar returns with Kurr, his accomplice, and the Uruk rider, who are all taken prisoner.
Although Ishak gives the Black to Alec, he decides to leave his horse in Morocco, believing he belongs there.
story_text_b: Lorsqu'on lui vole Black, rien ne peut arrêter Alec dans sa quête pour le retrouver: ni un voyage clandestin dans un avion jusqu'à Casablanca, ni la traversée du terrible désert du Sahara...

story_text_a: Michael Rockefeller, son of Nelson Rockefeller, was a young anthropologist who mysteriously disappeared in 1961 while exploring New Guinea. Some 40 years after his disappearance, a group of young people try to track him down by making a documentary of the search.
story_text_b:
The American Isabel Walker is visiting her pregnant sister, the poet Roxeanne de Persand, in Paris. Roxeanne's husband, Charles-Henri de Persand, left her and married Magda Tellman. Roxeanne claims ownership of a valuable painting, "Saint Ursula" by Georges de La Tour, although the painting originally belonged to her husband's family. Although the Louvre considers the painting to be a copy or a forgery, the Getty Museum expressed interest in acquiring the painting.
Isabel and her sister meet author Olivia Pace, who asks Roxeanne if she wants to work for her. Roxeanne declines the offer, but praises her sister's academic education. Pace sums it up as "she can read and write" and hires Isabel.
Isabel enters into a relationship with the young artist Yves. She also begins an affair with the married politician Edgar Cosset, an uncle of Charles-Henri, who directly asks her if she wants to be his mistress. He gives her a red Hermès handbag, a sure sign to his sister that the two are having an affair. Charles-Henri's sister calls her relatives after Isabel and Roxeanne's visit and asks them to tell her brother about the affair.
Depressed, Roxeanne makes an attempt to kill herself. Her and Isabelle's parents are coming to Paris. Meanwhile, Suzanne de Persand, Charles-Henri's mother, is trying to secure the Georges de La Tour painting for her family. Charles-Henri de Persand is killed by Magda's betrayed husband. The man follows Isabel to the Eiffel Tower, where he gives up his gun. Isabel puts them in the handbag that Cosset received and throws them off the tower. The man is sentenced to 20 years in prison. Isabel is breaking up with Cosset. Roxeanne and the attorney representing her are becoming a couple. The painting will be sold by the Walkers at an auction.

story_text_a:
In Nazi occupied France, Jean Blomart sits by a bed in which his lover Hélène lies dying. Through a series of flashbacks, we learn about both characters and their relationship to each other. As a young man filled with guilt about his privileged middle-class life, Jean joins the Communist Party and breaks from his family, determined to make his own way in life. After the death of a friend in a political protest, for which he feels guilty, Jean quits the Party and concentrates on trade union activities. Hélène is a young designer who works in her family's confectionery shop and is dissatisfied with her conventional romance with her fiance Paul. She contrives to meet Jean, and although he initially rejects her, they form a relationship after she has an abortion following a reckless liaison with another man. Jean tells Hélène he loves her even though he believes he does not. He proposes to her and she accepts.
When France enters World War II, Jean, conceding the need for violent conflict to effect change, becomes a soldier. Hélène intervenes against his will to arrange a safe posting for him. Angry with her, Jean breaks their relationship. As the German forces advance towards Paris, Hélène flees and witnesses the suffering of other refugees. Returning to Paris, she briefly takes up with a German who could advance her career, but soon sees what her countrymen are suffering. She also witnesses the roundup of Jews. Securing the safety of her Jewish friend Yvonne leads Hélène back to Jean, who has become a leader in a Resistance group. She is moved to join the group. Jean has reconnected with his father with the common goal to liberate France from Germany. His mother, however, is less impressed by the lives lost to the Resistance.
Hélène is shot in a resistance activity and during Jean's night vigil at her side, he examines his love for Hélène and the wider consequences of his actions. As morning dawns, Hélène dies and Jean decides to continue with acts of resistance.
story_text_b:
Die Amerikanerin Hélène lernt im Jahr 1938 in Paris den Kommunisten Jean kennen. Hélène schreibt Liebesbriefe an Jean, die dieser nicht beantwortet. Er sagt Hélène während eines Treffens, er wolle sie nicht ermutigen. Später wird Hélène doch von Jean schwanger, sie treibt aber ab.
Nach Beginn des Zweiten Weltkriegs wird Jean Soldat und geht in die Gefangenschaft. Der Unternehmer Bergman kommt nach Paris. Er verliebt sich in Hélène, die ihrerseits weiterhin Jean liebt und seine Freilassung erreicht. Bergman lockt Hélène mit Versprechungen, ihr eine Karriere in der Modewelt zu ermöglichen. Jean schließt sich der Résistance an.
Die Kämpfer der Résistance bezichtigen Hélène der Kollaboration mit den Deutschen; um ihre Unschuld zu beweisen, nimmt sie an einem Anschlag gegen die Besatzer teil.

story_text_a: The film tells five interwoven stories, all set in the Arab Muslim, Arab Christian and Jewish communities of the Jaffa/Tel Aviv metropolitan area, Israel.
story_text_b:
The story takes place in high society among the lovers of classical concert music. In the center of the action is the famous and celebrated stardirigent René von Geldern. The man is a widower and has a little daughter with Susi. Since he is a busy artist, he hires a young and beautiful educator named Inge Salinger, who turns out to be a good-hearted person. René's ex-girlfriend Vilma Cortini, on the other hand, presents herself as an attention-seeking diva and extremely jealous superior, who sees Inge as a tough competitor to regain the conductor's favor. That's why she's asking for Miss Salinger's release. Eventually, Vilma's pressure builds up over money, and he fires the teacher.
This, however, does not fit Little Susie at all, she has become very fond of Inge and wishes nothing more than that the young woman becomes her new mother. To achieve this goal, the girl tears herself open. He now has all hands full of money in the aftermath: he must get rid of the annoyingly intriguing Vilma Cortini, at the same time prepare for the upcoming wish concert and, by the way, also find his daughter again. In the end, everything adds up at the title-giving great wish concert, and von Geldern has not only orchestrated an artistic success, but has also found himself a new wife for life and a new mother for the super-lucky Susi.

story_text_a:
Dmitry Maykov, a student from Moscow, is in love with Anastasia Svetlova, one of his classmates from Lomonosov University. Coming from a modest family, his rival is his rich friend Maxime, who drives a Mercedes, booking flights on a state-of-the-art mobile phone... while Dimitri settles for the bus and tram to go to university.
Until the day when Dimitri's father, for his birthday, surprises him by giving him a used car. It's an old model from the 1950s, a Volga M21. Dimitri is doubly embarrassed, on the one hand because of the effort his father had to make to please him, and on the other hand because this collector car seems quite pushy, which may ridicule him in the eyes of his university classmates, but especially those of Anastasia. But one day, he realizes that the Volga GAZ M21 is not ordinary: it is actually the secret prototype of a flying car, a prototype built during the Soviet period, but whose project had been abandoned...
Forced to work to pay for his education, Dimitri became a florist. Under the influence of Victor Kuptsov, a powerful oligarch with thoughts as dark as his plans and a lecturer at the university, Dimitri is convinced that to succeed one must be selfish. He then uses his car to deliver as many flowers as possible in record time, in order to earn more and more money and with the secret hope of seducing Anastasia. In his pursuit of riches, he gradually neglects his family.
But the day his father is murdered, and even though he could have saved him, Dima realizes how far he's gone. From now on the car that was bequeathed to him will no longer be used to chase after money, but will be put at the service of the citizens of Moscow. Dimitri then becomes the  Black Lightning, who engages in the fight against crime and injustice and will watch over ordinary people...
story_text_b:
Korean gangster Han Ki-Chul (Lee Beom-soo) is put in charge by his Big Boss of looking after Lim Aryong (Shu Qi) who comes from Hong Kong. They expect Lim Aryong to be some big male gangster but she turns out to be a woman and acts very cold toward him and his associates. Moreover, none of them speak her language and she doesn't understand Korean. A translator called Yeon-Hee (Hyun Young) arrives. She is immature and very scared of the gangsters so at the beginning, instead of translating Aryong's rather rude answers, she changes them to nice ones. Quickly, Aryong shows her fierce fighting skills beating other bosses to save her companions. Ki-Chul and his associates, who are rather unskilled, are impressed and become afraid of her while, upon finding that they are actually nice, she's trying to be more friendly. Her efforts are ruined by Yeon-Hee who, taking advantage of Aryong's fearsome aura, 'translates' very threatening sentences.
Soon after, they are attacked by professional assassins. They think that they are after Ki-Chul while, in fact, they want to kill Aryong who is the daughter of a boss in Hong Kong and is accused of having killed another boss, triggering a gangster war there. They then separate and Aryong and Ki-Chul's car is chased by the assassins but they manage to take refuge in his family. His parents believe that she is his girlfriend and give him a family necklace to give her. The assassins find her again but she overcomes them, especially the woman who really killed the boss. She then goes to meet her mother who is the reason why she chose to hide in Korea, but seeing that she found a new family and is happy, she gives up speaking to her.
After that, she leaves Korea despite Ki-Chul's confession, even if she accepts the necklace. In Hong Kong, her father (Ti Lung) dies from his injuries caused by an explosion decided by the other boss. Even though Ki-Chul comes to support her, she leaves to take revenge. She then fights the other boss's gangsters with success and eventually she faces the boss. After cheating, he was going to shoot her as Ki-Chul arrives, distracting him. The boss shoots Ki-Chul first, allowing Aryong to come close to him and to kill him. Ki-Chul is not dead but is going to leave Hong Kong. Aryong, after becoming the new boss, succeeding her father, is advised by her father's right-hand man not to let him leave, as did her father who let her mother leave and then regretted it all his life. She follows the advice, stopping him on his way to the airport with all her gangsters and proposes to Ki-Chul, the right-hand man making the translation (not always a very accurate one, like Yeon-Hee). Ki-Chul accepts it and they embrace on the motorway.

story_text_a:
Die Aborigines, die im Outback unter schwierigen Bedingungen lebten und keinen Kontakt zu Weißen hatten, bewegten sich im Gebiet der Percival Lakes in Western Australia. In das Gebiet in der Great Sandy Desert, das von Salzseen geprägt ist, wurden zwei weiße Australier geschickt, die die Aufgabe hatten, es nach Menschen abzusuchen. Es war beabsichtigt Mittelstreckenraketen vom Typ Blue Streak nach einem Start auf dem Testgelände von Woomera in der Wüste aufschlagen zu lassen.
Der Film zeigt Material aus dem Jahr 1964, das Walter MacDougall mit einer 16mm-Kamera drehte, und aktuelle Interviews mit Yuwali. Sie war damals ein 17-jähriges Mädchen und in der Zeit der Filmproduktion 62 Jahre alt. Yuwali lebte mit ihrer Mutter in einer Gruppe von 20 Mädchen unterschiedlichen Alters. Die Gruppe bewegte sich ohne Männer in der Wüste. Yuwali sah erstmals in ihrem Leben Weiße und hielt den LKW für einen wandernden Felsen mit weißen Teufeln. Sie hatte Angst und versteckte sich. In der Nacht folgte sie den Spuren ihrer Mutter in der Wüste. Die Kontaktaufnahme mit den Aborigines gestaltete sich schwierig, da die Aborigines stets flohen. Glücklicherweise wurde der erste Raketenstart in Woomera wegen schlechten Wetters verschoben. Die Weißen folgten ebenso den Spuren der Gruppe und kamen mit ihnen in Kontakt. Die Angst löste sich, als die Männer ihnen Essen gaben. Da ihnen das Essen nicht schmeckte, vergruben sie es im Sand. Die nackten Frauen und Mädchen wurden eingekleidet und in eine von der Apostolischen Kirche geführte Aborigines-Missionsstation in Jigalong gebracht.
story_text_b:
The Aborigines, who lived in difficult conditions in the outback and had no contact with whites, moved to the Percival Lakes region of Western Australia. Two white Australians were sent to the Great Sandy Desert, an area of salt lakes, to search for people. It was intended to launch medium-range missiles of the Blue Streak type after a launch at the Woomera test site in the desert.
The film features footage from 1964, shot by Walter MacDougall with a 16mm camera, and recent interviews with Yuwali. She was a 17-year-old girl at the time and 62 years old at the time of filming. Yuwali lived with her mother in a group of 20 girls of different ages. The group moved without men in the desert. Yuwali saw white people for the first time in her life and mistook the truck for a walking rock with white devils. She was scared and hid. At night, she followed her mother's footsteps into the desert. Contact with the Aborigines proved difficult because the Aborigines were always fleeing. Fortunately, the first rocket launch at Woomera was postponed due to bad weather. The whites also followed in the group's footsteps and came into contact with them. The fear disappeared when the men gave them food. Since they didn't like the food, they buried it in the sand. The naked women and girls were dressed and taken to an Aboriginal mission station run by the Apostolic Church in Jigalong.

story_text_a:
Set in late September 2020, the story follows Katie Mitchell, a quirky aspiring filmmaker from Kentwood, Michigan, who often clashes with her nature-obsessed and technophobic father Rick, and who has recently been accepted into film school in California. The night before Katie leaves, Rick accidentally breaks her laptop after a fight with her. Rick decides to cancel Katie's flight and instead take her, along with her mother Linda, her younger brother Aaron and the family dog named Monchi, on a cross-country road trip to their college as a final bonding experience.
Meanwhile, tech entrepreneur Mark Bowman declares his highly intelligent AI PAL obsolete by unveiling a new line of home robots in its place. In revenge, PAL takes over Mark's company and orders all the robots around the world to capture humans and launch them into space. The Mitchells manage to avoid capture at a coffee shop in Kansas. Rick decides that his family must remain in the cafe for their own safety, but Katie coerces him to help save the world. They team up with two defective robots, Eric and Deborahbot 5000, who tell the Mitchells to use a death code to shut down PAL and all the robots.
The Mitchells arrive at a nearby mall to upload the death code to the network, but PAL orders all PAL appliances to try and stop them. Katie attempts to upload the death code, but is stopped after a giant Furby stalks the family. Ultimately, they catch the Furby by destroying a PAL router and disabling the enabled devices, which also stops the death code upload, so they must come up with a new plan. On the way to Silicon Valley, where the company is headquartered, Linda reveals to Katie that she and Rick had originally lived in a cabin in the mountains years ago, as it was their lifelong dream before he gave it up.
Upon arriving in Silicon Valley, the Mitchells disguise themselves as robots and head to the PAL Labs headquarters to shut it down, but PAL manipulates them by revealing surveillance footage from Katie's coffee shop by secretly telling Aaron that she was pretending to have faith in Rick just so he could hear what she wanted to hear. Disconsolate, the Mitchells fail to reach PAL's lair and Rick and Linda are captured after PAL creates stronger and smarter robots, and reprograms Eric and Deborahbot to obey him.
Katie, Aaron and Monchi escape headquarters and hide from the robots. Katie discovers Rick's childhood recordings on her camera, realizing that Rick gave up his lifelong dream of living in a cabin to take care of his daughter. Revitalized, she and Aaron infiltrate PAL Labs headquarters again and use Monchi to make the robots malfunction, as his programming cannot distinguish him as a dog. With Mark's help, Rick and Linda break free and plan to upload a home movie of Katie with Monchi in it to short-circuit the robots. However, Rick is outnumbered by the robots as he is about to upload the video.
Katie is finally captured. Facing PAL to justify saving humanity, Katie explains that no matter how hard their family fights, they will always remain connected despite how different they are. PAL rejects this reasoning and leaves Katie in her den. Eric and Deborahbot, having been inspired by Rick's "reprogramming" to use a computer, go back to their faulty states and upload Katie's home movie, saving her and helping the rest of the Mitchells. The family bands together to fight off the rest of the upgraded robots, and Katie destroys PAL, dropping her into a glass of water, freeing all the humans and disabling all the robots except for Eric and Deborahbot.
A few months after the uprising, Katie and her family arrive at the university, as she and Rick share one last heartfelt goodbye before actually parting ways. Months later, he joins them on another road trip with Eric and Deborahbot to Washington, D.C. to accept the Congressional Medal of Honor for his action against the robots.
story_text_b: Satire of Hollywood, it tells how a film producer receives a series of death threats by a screenwriter, which this in his day did not hire. Tim Robbins plays this producer, who will have to fight to keep his job and who will have to do everything possible to evade police action when he is accidentally involved in the death of a screenwriter.

story_text_a:
