For the latter, Anthony blames and beats his children, Jan and Mark, then beats Dolores for intervening, resulting in a fight between the entire family. Concerned by these developments, Dolores tries to have the local Catholic priest, Father Frank Adamsky, bless the house, but an argument breaks out within the family shortly after another demonic incident causes significant damage to the kitchen. Anthony blames the younger children again and hits Jan as Adamsky tries to intervene, but Anthony rudely orders him to leave. To Dolores' mortification, Adamsky leaves, disgusted at Anthony's behavior. He finds his car door open and the Bible on the passenger seat torn to pieces. The situation inside the home continues to deteriorate; Anthony is shown to be strict, abusive, sacrilegious towards the Catholic faith, violent towards his family, and forcing his wife to have sex with him against her will. Dolores tries to keep things together for the youngest children.
The family goes to church with Anthony, so he can apologize for being rude to Adamsky, although Anthony only agrees to do it after Dolores threatens to divorce him. Sonny stays at home, claiming to feel unwell. He soon hears an alarming noise and goes downstairs to get his father's gun. He hears demonic laughter and follows it to a tunnel in the basement. The unseen presence pursues a frightened Sonny to his room, and he then falls victim to demonic possession. Now possessed, Sonny approaches Patricia to play a game with him. They pretend he is a famous photographer and she is his nude model. Patricia agrees to pose naked, and the pair end up having incestuous sex. Patricia is then seen at confession, partially confessing to the act and telling the priest that he does it to "hurt God" but not revealing that it was her brother she slept with.
Sonny becomes more sinister and demonic, as his face starts contorting demonically. Startled, he tries to keep his family away but is unsuccessful due to the demon's influence. On Sonny's birthday, he isolates himself from his birthday party, but  Patricia goes to check on him. She tells him she does not feel guilty about what they have been doing, but due to his demonic phases and his body's gradual demonic contortions, Sonny sends her away, using foul language. Patricia runs away crying, and she tries to tell Adamsky that she thinks Sonny is possessed, but he does not respond. Later that night, the evil spirit tells Sonny to "kill them all." Sonny goes and gets his father's rifle and kills his parents, Jan, Mark, and finally Patricia, after hunting her down.
The next day the police arrive, pick up the bodies, and Sonny is arrested. Sonny tells Adamsky at the scene that he does not recall killing his family. Adamsky then realizes that Sonny is possessed and asks the bishops if he can perform an exorcism on him, but they refuse, not believing him. He then decides to perform an exorcism without the support of the Catholic Church. After freeing him from police custody, Adamsky takes Sonny to church. Sonny attacks him and escapes after seeing the crosses on the doors. Adamsky runs after Sonny, traces him to the house, and performs the exorcism, releasing Sonny's soul. As the police arrive, Adamsky asks Father Tom to take Sonny away from him. Tom takes Sonny outside, where the police arrest him and take him back into custody. It is revealed that the demon has transferred itself into Adamsky. Father Adamsky's fate and his whereabouts are left unknown, and eventually, the house is put up for sale.
story_text_b: La familia Montelli se ha mudado a lo que creen será la casa de sus sueños, desconociendo que en el interior de la casa hay una presencia maligna al acecho. Unos demonios comienzan a aterrorizar a los integrantes de la familia, haciendo que comiencen a tener problemas y discusiones. Dolores, la madre, trata que el sacerdote local, el padre Adamsky, visite la casa para bendecirla, pero no lo logra ya que Anthony, el abusivo esposo de Dolores, obliga al padre Adamsky a irse de la casa sin saber que Sonny, su hijo mayor, es víctima de una posesión demoníaca. Sonny comienza a jugar con su hermana Patricia con el fin de incitarla a tener relaciones sexuales con él. Los espíritus malignos mueven a Sonny sembrar la discordia en su familia y más tarde lo fuerzan a asesinar a sus padres y hermanos. El padre Adamsky se da cuenta de que Sonny fue poseído y pide a la Iglesia permiso para realizar un exorcismo, pero se lo niegan al no creerle. Por lo tanto, el padre Adamsky se decide a realizar por su propia cuenta el exorcismo para liberar el alma de Sonny de los espíritus malignos.

story_text_a:
In the mid-1950s, Richard Dadier is a new teacher at North Manual Trades High School, an inner-city school of diverse ethnic backgrounds.  Led by student Gregory Miller, most engage in anti-social behavior. The school principal, Mr. Warneke, denies there are discipline issues, but the school faculty, particularly Mr. Murdock, warn Dadier otherwise. Dadier befriends two other new teachers, Joshua Edwards and Lois Hammond.
Dadier's class includes Miller and Artie West, a rebellious bully and gang leader. The class shows no respect for Dadier.  Dadier encourages Miller to lead the class in the right direction.  After Dadier subdues a student who attacks Miss Hammond, the class gives Dadier the silent treatment and are even more uncooperative. Dadier and Edwards are mugged by a gang that includes West.
Reluctant to quit, Dadier seeks advice from his former teacher, Professor Kraal, the principal of an academically superior school with disciplined students. Kraal offers Dadier a job, but he declines. After chastising his class for calling each other racially divisive names, Dadier is himself falsely accused by Mr. Warneke of using racial epithets in the classroom. West encounters Dadier during his gang's robbery of a newspaper truck. West tells Dadier his classroom is on the streets and to leave him alone. Several students, led by West, assault Edwards in his classroom and destroy his music record collection.
Dadier's wife, Anne, who is pregnant, begins receiving anonymous letters and phone calls telling her Dadier and Miss Hammond are having an affair. Dadier discovers Miller can play piano and sing, and wonders why Miller can show such talent but also be so rebellious. Dadier shows his class an animated film about "Jack and the Beanstalk" which sparks discussion about moral choices. Anne goes into premature labor caused by the stress of the phone calls about Dadier's alleged affair. When a neighbor shows Dadier the anonymous letters, he angrily decides to quit. Mr. Murdock encourages him to stay telling Dadier he is making progress and has inspired him too. Anne apologizes for doubting Dadier's loyalty in their marriage and says she was wrong for telling him to quit. Their premature baby boy, though weak, eventually thrives.
When Dadier observes West openly copying from another student, he demands that West bring his paper to the front to have it docked five points. West rebuffs his repeated request, but Dadier is unrelenting.  The conflict quickly escalates, and West pulls out a switchblade.  Dadier does not back down.  Miller stops Belazi from jumping Dadier from behind.  The rest of West's gang fails to assist.
Dadier accuses West of the false allegations made to both Mr. Warneke and Anne. Dadier subdues West, and the other students join in to subdue classmate Belazi, who has picked up the knife to escape. Miller then leads the class in helping Dadier take West and Belazi to the principal's office. In the final scene, Miller and Dadier ask if the other is quitting at the end of the school year. Miller said no, because the two of them had a pact that neither would quit if the other stayed, and Dadier's expression makes clear he has no intention of breaking the agreement.
story_text_b:
Veteran Eddie Dugan (Richard Gere) is in the final stages of his career, fed up with so many years of service and a week away from retiring and retiring to a small cabin in Connecticut to fish. On the other hand Sal Procida (Ethan Hawke) is clear that there is nothing he could not do to provide his wife and their seven children with a stable life. Clarence "Tango" Butler (Don Cheadle), is a cop who has always surrounded himself with loyal men and who has a special relationship with Caz (Wesley Snipes), who is one of the Brooklyn drug dealers, currently in jail.
Engaged in the NYPD's operation to clean up the city's drug streets, the three officers are drawn into the extreme violence and corruption that plagues the Brooklyn area. For a week, Eddie, Sal and Clarence will hopelessly head for the same crime scene.

story_text_a: Un ours noir américain trouve dans les bois de Géorgie une cargaison de cocaïne. Après en avoir avalé une grande quantité, il entre dans une rage meurtrière à laquelle touristes, habitants locaux et malfrats vont devoir survivre.
story_text_b:
In 1985, drug smuggler Andrew Thornton drops several duffel bags of cocaine from an airplane over the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest in Georgia, but dies in the parachute jump. The bags lying in the forest are found by a black bear, who subsequently develops a pronounced cocaine addiction and is noticed with aggressive behavior towards hikers and park visitors. Meanwhile, in Tennessee, drug lord Syd learns of Thornton's crash and sends his son Eddie and his friend Daveed to retrieve the scattered cocaine. Also, Detective Bob, after finding Thornton's body, is on his way to Georgia to take down Syd.
Meanwhile, in the national park, the children Henry and Dee Dee are skipping school to paint a nearby waterfall. On their way there, they discover the discarded cocaine packages and make the acquaintance of the bear that Dee Dee is carrying away. Meanwhile, their mother, Sari, has informed Liz, a park ranger, and Peter, a zoologist, of her daughter's disappearance and has begun a search in the forest area. When the trio finds frightened Henry in a tree, Peter is torn to pieces by the bear. Liz manages to escape with minor injuries and tries to call for reinforcements, but is attacked and killed by the animal, as well as the paramedics Beth and Tom who rushed to help. Meanwhile, Sari and Henry decide to search for the missing Dee Dee.
Two drug dealers, Eddie and Daveed, have also arrived in the national park and have discovered that a local youth gang is in possession of much of the cocaine. Together with their leader, they make their way to the gang's drug stash, where the three also meet Detective Bob. A gunfight between Daveed and the policeman is interrupted by the abrupt appearance of the bear, who is after Bob's confiscated cocaine. After the cop manages to distract the animal with the help of the drugs, both parties first agree to a ceasefire, before Bob is shot by Syd, who is also present. He explains to his son, Eddie, who wants to get away from crime, that he and his family are being hunted by Mexican drug cartels, so recovering the cocaine is a top priority.
Sari and Henry can follow a trail laid by Dee Dee to the Bear Cave, where they also find two cocaine-addicted cubs. Syd, Eddie and Daveed were also able to follow the bear to their hideout, where the animal had hoarded a large quantity of the drugs. Syd threatens to shoot the mother or one of the children if the cocaine is not handed over to him, but Eddie and Daveed refuse the order due to the involvement of minors. When the bear appears, Sari, Henry, Dee Dee, Eddie and Daveed save themselves by jumping into a waterfall, while Syd tries to take on the animal. The bear is then shot first by Syd, but eventually defeats the drug lord and throws him alive to her cubs for food.
Some time later, the drug-addicted bear and her cubs attack hikers in the national park. Eddie and Daveed were able to leave crime behind and find their peace, while Henry and Dee Dee were put under house arrest for one-time cocaine use.

story_text_a:
Tras el fallecimiento de Nawal Marwan, una inmigrante canadiense, sus dos hijos -los mellizos Jeanne y Simon- se reúnen con el notario canadiense Jean Lebel, empleador de su madre y amigo de la familia. El testamento de Nawal hace referencia a una promesa incumplida, negándole a ella una lápida y un ataúd, a menos que Jeanne y Simon rastreen a su misterioso hermano, cuya existencia desconocían previamente, y a su padre, a quien creían muerto.
Una serie de flashbacks revelan que Nawal provenía de una familia árabe cristiana en un país no identificado del Medio Oriente, y que se enamoró de un refugiado, lo que resultó en su embarazo. Su familia asesina a su amante y casi la mata a ella como un crimen de honor, pero su abuela la perdona y le hace prometer que abandonará la aldea después del nacimiento de su bebé y comenzará una nueva vida en la ciudad ficticia de Daresh. La abuela tatúa al bebé y lo envía a un orfanato.
Mientras Nawal cursa estudios universitarios en Daresh, estalla una guerra civil en el país, donde se cometen una serie de crímenes de guerra; la joven se opone al conflicto bélico por motivos de derechos humanos. El orfanato de su hijo en Kfar Khout es destruido por un militante musulmán, Chamseddine, que lo convierte en un niño soldado islámico. Después de escapar de la masacre de un autobús lleno de refugiados musulmanes por los nacionalistas cristianos, Nawal se une a los combatientes musulmanes y dispara a un líder nacionalista. Posteriormente, es encarcelada en Kfar Ryat y violada por su torturador Abou Tareq. Producto de esta violación, queda embarazada y da a luz a los gemelos.
Después de viajar al país natal de su madre, Jeanne descubre su pasado y persuade a Simon, quien está enojado con la personalidad inusual de su madre, a unirse a ella. Con la ayuda de Lebel, aprenden que el nombre de su hermano es Nihad de Mai y rastrean a Chamseddine. Simon se reúne con él personalmente, y revela que los nacionalistas capturaron a Nihad, quien estaba enfurecido por la guerra, lo entrenaron como torturador y lo enviaron a Kfar Ryat, donde adoptó el nombre de Abou Tareq, siendo de esta manera tanto el medio hermano de los gemelos como su padre. Posteriormente, Nihad emigró a Canadá y Nawal solo se enteró de su verdadera identidad después de reconocerlo en una piscina canadiense y ver su tatuaje.
Los gemelos encuentran a Nihad en Canadá y le entregan las cartas de Nawal sin hablarle. La primera carta se dirige a él como el padre de Jeanne y Simon, y está llena de desprecio, ya que Nawal le escribe a Nihad como su violador. La segunda carta se dirige a él como el hermano de ellos y, en cambio, está escrita con palabras cariñosas, diciendo que él, como hijo de Nawal, merece amor. Nawal obtiene su lápida después del envío de las cartas, y su tumba es visitada por Nihad.
story_text_b:
After the death of Nawal Marwan, a Canadian immigrant, her two children - the twins Jeanne and Simon - meet with the Canadian notary Jean Lebel, their mother's employer and family friend. Nawal's will refers to a broken promise, denying her a tombstone and a coffin, unless Jeanne and Simon track down her mysterious brother, whose existence they previously did not know, and her father, whom they believed to be dead.
A series of flashbacks reveal that Nawal came from a Christian Arab family in an unnamed Middle Eastern country, and that she fell in love with a refugee, resulting in her pregnancy. Her family murders her lover and nearly kills her as an honor killing, but her grandmother forgives her and makes her promise that she will leave the village after the birth of her baby and start a new life in the fictional city of Daresh. The grandmother tattoos the baby and sends him to an orphanage.
While Nawal is attending university in Daresh, a civil war breaks out in the country, where a series of war crimes are committed; the young woman opposes the war conflict on human rights grounds. His son's orphanage in Kfar Khout is destroyed by a Muslim militant, Chamseddine, who turns him into an Islamic child soldier. After escaping the massacre of a bus full of Muslim refugees by Christian nationalists, Nawal joins the Muslim fighters and shoots a nationalist leader. Subsequently, she is imprisoned in Kfar Ryat and raped by her torturer Abou Tareq. As a result of this rape, she becomes pregnant and gives birth to twins.
After traveling to her mother's home country, Jeanne discovers her past and persuades Simon, who is angry at her mother's unusual personality, to join her. With Lebel's help, they learn that his brother's name is Nihad de Mai and track down Chamseddine. Simon meets with him personally, and reveals that the nationalists captured Nihad, who was enraged by the war, trained him as a torturer and sent him to Kfar Ryat, where he adopted the name Abou Tareq, thus being both the twins' half-brother and their father. Subsequently, Nihad emigrated to Canada and Nawal only learned of his true identity after recognizing him in a Canadian swimming pool and seeing his tattoo.
The twins find Nihad in Canada and give him Nawal's letters without speaking to him. The first letter is addressed to him as the father of Jeanne and Simon, and is full of contempt, as Nawal writes to Nihad as his rapist. The second letter is addressed to him as their brother and, instead, is written in loving words, saying that he, as Nawal's son, deserves love. Nawal gets her tombstone after the letters are sent, and her grave is visited by Nihad.

story_text_a:
Annie Wilson gagne sa vie en lisant les cartes aux habitants de son village de Brixton en Géorgie. Elle possède un véritable don de voyance dû à une perception extrasensorielle. Lors de ses consultations, Valerie Barksdale lui parle de son mari Donnie qui la frappe constamment mais dont elle n'arrive pas à se séparer, malgré les conseils répétés d'Annie. Donnie Barksdale, en apprenant que sa femme continue à se faire tirer les cartes, menace Annie et ses trois fils de mort.
Peu de temps après, Annie fait la connaissance de Jessica King, la fiancée de Wayne Collins. Elle a une vision morbide de l'avenir de la jeune fille. La police va alors demander à Annie de les aider dans leur enquête sur la disparition de Jessica. Annie découvre que la jeune fille avait une liaison avec Donnie.
story_text_b:
Annie Wilson è una giovane madre vedova, in seguito a un'esplosione nella centrale telefonica che le ha portato via il marito. Rimasta sola con tre figli piccoli, Mike, Miller e il piccolo Ben per guadagnarsi da vivere legge le carte ai cittadini di Brixton in cambio di piccole donazioni in denaro o regali. Annie ha davvero il dono di vedere nel futuro e riuscire così a prevedere avvenimenti non ancora accaduti, ma il più delle volte queste visioni sono tremendamente realistiche e violente.
Nonostante sia considerata una benefattrice da molte delle persone che si rivolgono a lei, il suo modo di "tirare avanti" è contestato dagli immancabili scettici che non credono nell'esistenza di tali capacità sensoriali; questo le causerà non pochi problemi, specie col violento marito di una delle sue clienti, Donnie Barksdale, che l'accusa di riempire di sciocchezze la testa della moglie e di averle suggerito di lasciarlo. In soccorso di Annie, che riceve minacce da Donnie anche verso i figli, arriva spesso Buddy Cole, un ragazzo che fa il meccanico e consulta Annie per i suoi problemi legati al passato. Buddy è infatti affezionato a lei e ai piccoli e fa di tutto per difenderli.
Un giorno, giunge la notizia della scomparsa di una bella e disinibita ragazza di buona famiglia dal comportamento scorretto, Jessica King, la quale sta per sposarsi con Wayne Collins, preside della scuola elementare frequentata dai figli di Annie. Dal momento che Wayne nutre stima per Annie le chiede, assieme al padre di Jessica, di occuparsi del caso e dare una mano con le sue capacità poiché le indagini sono giunte a un punto morto. Annie avrà delle spaventose visioni e dopo aver consultato le carte e aver visto un cancello, uno stagno e dei fiori bianchi, consiglierà di effettuare le ricerche proprio nella proprietà che più assomiglia a ciò che le si è rivelato; sfortunatamente, si tratta della proprietà di Barksdale. L'uomo minaccia di farla bruciare insultandola pesantemente quando si accorge che tutto il corpo di polizia investigativa della città si trova nella sua proprietà con un mandato di perquisizione, e subito pensa che Annie lo abbia voluto incastrare per punirlo delle minacce subite.
Le indagini proseguono e la ragazza viene effettivamente ritrovata nello stagno, avvolta in una catena e seminuda. Durante il processo in tribunale, viene assodato che Barksdale e la King erano stati amanti, e Donnie viene condannato. Fuori dal tribunale, Annie trova Buddy ad aspettarla, finalmente deciso a rivelare alla donna gli avvenimenti del passato che lo avevano profondamente segnato. Nonostante il suo sforzo, viene freddamente zittito dalla donna, troppo stanca e rattristata per via dei pesanti insulti a lei recati durante il processo. Poco dopo si viene a sapere che Buddy, non avendo nessuno con cui parlare e non riuscendo più a trattenere i suoi demoni, ha rapito il padre, causa di tutti i suoi problemi, e che vuole ucciderlo, per punirlo dello stupro che lo ha segnato per tutta la vita. Viene chiamata in tempo la polizia, e il giovane non arriva a portare a termine l'omicidio, lasciando però il padre ustionato gravemente. Non appena Annie viene a sapere dei fatti, inizia a sentirsi molto in colpa per non aver ascoltato il ragazzo.
Nel frattempo Annie, grazie a nuove visioni, si convince che l'assassino non sia Donnie, e che quindi sia stato incastrato l'uomo sbagliato. La donna prega che il caso venga riaperto, ma non viene ascoltata, poiché non si può riaprire un caso chiuso sulla base di premonizioni. A questo punto Annie continua da sola le sue indagini e grazie al suo dono scopre che l'assassino è Wayne, futuro marito di Jessica. La stessa notte in cui Donnie e Jessica si erano visti per uno dei loro incontri intimi, il fidanzato l'aveva scoperta e strangolata per poi gettarla nello stagno. Wayne è con Annie nel momento della rivelazione e cerca di strangolarla, ma viene fermato da Buddy, evaso dall'ospedale psichiatrico, che lo colpisce alla testa. Una volta dalla polizia, la donna rivela come sia riuscita a salvarsi grazie al giovane amico, che non sembrava portarle rancore per non averlo ascoltato. La polizia le rivela però che Buddy si è ucciso in cella, prima che Annie fosse aggredita da Wayne. Il caso viene chiuso e la donna può finalmente vivere in pace con i suoi tre bambini, ricordando il giovane problematico come suo salvatore, di cui stringe ancora tra le mani il fazzoletto donatole quando l'ha salvata.

story_text_a: En Afrique, en 1885, le chercheur d'or Patrick O'Brien et sa fille Kathleen découvrent un diamant qui s'avère n'être qu'un simple caillou. Ils décident de rejoindre la côte car on peut y chercher de l'ivoire. Au même moment, ils rencontrent un aventurier du nom d’Allan Quatermain qui part en convoi chercher des chasseurs blancs pour un safari africain. Grâce à Kathleen, celui-ci accepte de les prendre avec lui. Lors d'un bivouac, Kathleen aperçoit un chariot de l'autre côté du fleuve. Une fois sur place, ils découvrent deux personnes, Umbopa l’africain et Sylvestra qui meurt quelques instants après leur avoir révélé l'existence d'une carte indiquant la mine de diamants du roi Salomon. O'Brien trouve la carte et annonce à sa fille qu'il va aller chercher les diamants, il en fait une copie avant de la rendre à Quatermain. Le soir même, il lui annonce qu'il partira seul à leur recherche, et lui demande de veiller sur sa fille. Quatermain qui ne peut le dissuader de partir accepte de protéger Kathleen.
story_text_b: Patsy O'Brien y su hija Kathy están en África en busca de hacer fortuna. En su camino se encuentran con Allan Quatermain, famoso cazador de África Central; a quien solicitan les transporte a su destino. En el camino se cruzan con una carreta en la que venía Umbopa, quien les habla de la existencia de las minas del rey Salomón. Creyendo que así hará su fortuna O'Brien roba el mapa y parte en secreto en su búsqueda. Kathy pide a Quatermain que le ayude a encontrar a su padre. En el transcurso del viaje vivirán todo tipo de peligros y aventuras.

story_text_a:
# I Act
It takes place in the Conway family home in 1919, on the night of the birthday of one of the daughters, Kay. The family consists of Mrs. Conway, her daughters Kay, Hazel, Madge and Carol and her sons Alan and Robin. Three other characters also appear on the scene: Gerald, a lawyer, Joan, a young woman in love with Robin, and Ernest, a young and ambitious entrepreneur, from a lower social class, who intends to attack the Conway family. The family celebrates the end of World War I, and holds out hope for a bright future of fulfilled dreams. At some point, Kay falls into a dream state and has a vision of the future.
# Act two
The second act takes place in the same room and plunges us into the shattered lives of the Conways exactly eighteen years later. Reunited, it shows how the lives of the Conways have failed in different ways. Robin has become a traveller, estranged from his wife Joan, Madge has failed to realize her socialist dreams, Carol has died, Hazel is married to the rich but sadistic Ernest. Kay has succeeded to some extent as an independent woman, but has not realized her dream of writing a novel. Worst of all, Mrs. Conway's fortune has been squandered, the family home is up for sale, and the children's inheritance is gone. As the action progresses, resentments and tensions flare up and the Conways are torn apart by misery and grief. Only Alan, the quietest of the family, seems to keep his cool. In the final scene, Kay confesses her hopelessness to Alan who suggests that the secret of life is understanding its true reality: the premise that the perception that time is linear and that we should seize and take what we can before we die is false. If we are able to see time as eternally present, that at any given moment we are seeing only "a cross-section of ourselves", then we can transcend suffering without needing to hurt or collide with other people.
# Act three
The third act takes us back to 1919 and we see how the seeds of the downfall of the Conways are being sown, even then. Ernest is rejected by Hazel and Mrs. Conway, Gerald's budding love for Madge is destroyed by Mrs. Conway's snobbery in another moment of social hubris, Alan is rejected by Joan who becomes Robin's fiancée. As the children gather at the end of Mrs. Conway's play, Kay has a moment of recollection of the vision of the second act. Concerned, she leaves the party and the play ends with Alan promising that he will be able to tell her something in the future that will help her.
story_text_b:
In 1961, 11-year-old Beverly "Bev" Donofrio is in a car with her father, Leonard, at the Christmas tree lot. When she reveals that she wants a bra for Christmas to attract the attention of a boy she likes, Leonard tells her that she is too young to think about boys and that she should focus on books instead.
In 1965, Bev is an intelligent but naive 15-year-old. Her dream is to go to college in New York and become a writer. She and her friends, Fay and Tina, are going to a party. Fay meets her boyfriend Bobby, who is about to be sent to the front in Vietnam, while Bev delivers a love letter to a popular boy named Sky. When Sky reads the letter aloud, Bev runs to the bathroom. She is consoled by Ray, a stranger, who then defends Bev's honor and fights Sky. Bev and Ray, along with Fay and Bobby, run away from the party. The four of them go to a lookout, where Bobby and Fay have sex. Bev is overwhelmed by Ray's kindness, and they have sex, too. Leonard, who's on duty, takes them to the police station, where Bev claims they just kissed.
Bev finds out that she's pregnant. After communicating this to Ray, he proposes to marry her but Bev initially refuses. He appeases the anger of his shocked parents by agreeing to a hasty marriage. At the reception, everyone avoids Bev, so Fay announces publicly that she is also pregnant. Fay confides to Bev that her father wanted her to put the baby up for adoption, but she and Bobby are getting married instead. The two girls finally celebrate the fact that they're going to be mothers together.
In the months that followed, the girls complained that they had missed three things: their childhood, their high school prom, and an education. Bev gives birth to son Jason (which makes her angry because she wanted a girl), while Fay gives birth to daughter Amelia. Bev continues to pursue her education. When Jason is three, she has a chance to win a college scholarship. Unfortunately, Bev's interview goes bad when she's forced to bring Jason along. Although the interviewer praises Bev's writing, he says she has too many distractions. Later, Fay reveals that she and Bobby are divorcing, because he met someone else while stationed in Hawaii. Bev tells Fay that she's not sure she loves Jason, because his birth cost her so much. When Jason threatens to drown in Fay's pool, Bev vows to be more careful.
On Jason's seventh birthday, several people from Bev's high school show up at his party: old friend Tina is now engaged and going to New York University; and Tommy, who had a crush on Bev, just graduated from Berkeley. He suggests that Bev move her family to California and pursue her education there, as the state offers financial aid. Ray agrees to the plan, but on the day they are supposed to leave he confesses to being a heroin addict and to having spent their life savings on drugs. Bev's helping him get clean, but Ray's sneaking out to get more drugs. When he tells Bev that it's impossible for him to quit, she tells him that he should leave instead. Ray agrees, but young Jason chases after him in tears, then tells Bev that he hates her for letting Ray go.
Two years later, Bev still craves California. She and Fay help Lizard dry marijuana in Bev's oven. Jason, still bitter, tells grandfather Leonard, who arrests the mothers (Lizard had escaped). Fay's brother pays the bail, using their savings, on the condition that Fay and Amelia move away with him and cut off contact with Bev. Bev tells complacent Jason harshly that he ruined their lives. He claims it's his fault Amelia moved away.
In 1985, Bev and Jason are driving to see Ray. She managed to graduate and write her memoir, but she needs Ray to sign a waiver, or her book won't be published. During the drive, Jason tells Bev that he wants to transfer from New York University to Indiana University, but Bev refuses, saying that he is receiving the education she was never able to receive. Jason calls his girlfriend Amelia and tells her the bad news. Amelia is devastated but assures him that she is not angry. Upon arriving at Ray's trailer, Bev explains why they are there. When Ray's wife, Shirley, asks for $100,000, Bev yells at Ray and leaves. Jason follows her and calls her selfish because she only cares about her book when she finally gets to see her father again. You accuse her of being a bad mother, and she walks away.
Ray goes out and talks to Jason, stating that leaving was the best thing he could have done for Jason and believes it's the only reason Jason has grown so well. He's smuggling signed documents to Jason. Jason finds Bev, who insists she was a great mother who sacrificed everything for him. Jason reveals he's moving in with Amelia and apologizes to Bev for ruining her life. Bev mellows and tells Jason that she's proud of him and thinks of him as the best thing in her life. She also tells him that she feels responsible for his various mistakes and wrong choices, and that she never intended to blame him for them. She gives him her car to drive to Indiana.
Beverly is forced to call Leonard for a ride. She complains to him about how Jason blames her for everything that's wrong in his life. Then she realizes she did the same thing to her father. Together, they sing a song of his childhood as they walk away.

story_text_a:
In the year 2047, a broadcast reveals the unexpected reappearance of the spaceship Event Horizon, officially destroyed in an accident seven years earlier. She is sent to investigate the rescue ship Lewis and Clark, with its crew consisting of Captain Miller, Lieutenant Starck, Pilot Smith, Medical Officer Peters, Engineer Justin, Dr. D.J., Rescue Technician Cooper and, finally, Dr. William Weir, a guest.
After the long journey to the planet Neptune, in whose orbit the Event Horizon has reappeared, Dr. Weir reveals to the rest of the team that he is the builder of the spacecraft and that the latter, in fact, was the result of a secret project with the aim of creating a vehicle capable of exceeding the speed of light. Weir explains that he has equipped the Event Horizon with a gravitational transporter: the latter is able to generate an artificial black hole, whose gravity is used to curve space-time and thus allow the spacecraft to jump to any point in the universe. However, after reaching the safe distance and opening a dimensional entrance to Proxima Centauri, the Event Horizon disappeared without a trace.
The only transmission received after the return of the spacecraft is a confused audio in which there are terrifying cries and a voice that, according to D.J., pronounces the Latin phrase liberate me ("save me"). Aboard the Event Horizon, members of the rescue team find obvious signs of a massacre and strange readings indicating vague and widespread life forms throughout the ship. Justin enters the engine room, where the gravitational transducer reactivates itself by sucking it into the resulting dimensional entrance. Immediately afterwards, a violent shock wave leaks out of the transporter severely damaging the Lewis and Clark and forcing its crew to take refuge on the Event Horizon.
Meanwhile, Justin re-emerges from the dimensional entrance in a catatonic state and is taken to the infirmary. On the spacecraft, however, oxygen is running low and the team has very little time to repair the Lewis and Clark. Recovered, Justin attempts suicide by jumping into space, terrified by what he saw on the other side of the dimensional entrance. He is, however, rescued by Captain Miller and, badly wounded, placed in stasis. Meanwhile, each member of the team begins to see their own fears and demons materialize in the form of hallucinations: Miller sees Corrick again, a man he was forced to abandon leaving him to die by being burned alive, Peters has visions of his son with his legs heavily injured, while Weir is haunted by the figure of his eyeless wife, who committed suicide because of her husband's prolonged absence when he was busy designing the spaceship.
Soon the rescuers find the footage of the logbook, where the original crew of the Event Horizon prepares for the test jump to Proxima Centauri and, immediately after, we see him engaged in acts of torture, cannibalism and all kinds of nefarious practices; at the end of the recording, the captain launches a warning showing the eyes that he apparently has extinguished: liberate tutemet ex inferis ("save yourselves from hell"). According to D.J., the gravitational transporter took the spacecraft beyond the boundaries of the universe known to science, leading it into a dimension of darkness and doom, only to return changed. Starck senses that the detected life signs are an indication that the spaceship is somehow alive and sentient, intent on exterminating the new crew as well by returning them to the alternate dimension.
Miller then decides to destroy the Event Horizon, but Weir is invaded by the evil presence and, after having his eyes gouged out during a new vision of his wife's suicide, he blows up the Lewis and Clark with an explosive device taken from the central corridor of the Event Horizon. In the explosion, Smith is killed and Cooper is thrown into space; Peters is also a victim of the spaceship, driven into a deep limbo by his son's hallucination. Weir kills D.J. by vivisecting him, and kidnaps Starck by leading her to the command deck. Miller confronts Weir face-to-face, and in the encounter, Weir accidentally breaks the hall window and is sucked into space. Escaping safely, Miller and Starck find Cooper, who has managed to return by detonating the suit's oxygen tank. To their horror, they also discover that Weir has activated the gravitational transducer and that the spacecraft will cross the dimensional entrance again in less than ten minutes. Miller decides to detonate the Event Horizon corridor to separate the remaining bridges from the transporter room.
Starck and Cooper reach the bow of the ship, where Justin is also in stasis, sending a distress signal, while Miller is forced to flee, detonator in hand, into the engine room from Corrick's apparition. The latter transforms into a horribly mutilated Weir, who begins to show Miller the atrocities to which they will be destined once they reach the infernal dimension. The dimensional entrance opens wide and Miller, in a last desperate gesture, activates the detonator destroying the central corridor. The Event Horizon's bow moves away with Starck, Cooper and Justin aboard, while the remaining decks explode and Miller with the stern of the spaceship enters the gravitational hole towards the demonic dimension.
Several days later, Starck is brought out of stasis by a rescue team, sent in after receiving their signal, but one of the rescuers uncovers his own face revealing himself to be Weir. In a panic, Starck wakes up from what was a nightmare in the presence of Cooper, Justin, and the real rescue team. The film ends with the doors of the stasis chamber closing on the scene, leaving the ominous premonition that the diabolical presence on the spaceship is still alive.
story_text_b:
May the 10th, 1916. British spy Edgar Brodie is dead, according to the press. In fact, he's assuming a different identity, as he's to be deployed as a secret agent in Switzerland. As Richard Ashenden, he's there to kill an unknown spy before he can deploy into enemy territory. This was necessary to safeguard British interests in a Middle East crisis. A colleague from Mexico, known as "the General", is to accompany Ashenden.
In his hotel room, Ashenden meets with the spy disguised as his wife Elsa, who is being visited by her admirer Marvin. Elsa is initially fire and flame for the assassination mission and thinks the whole thing is a great adventure.
When Ashenden and the General find one of their informants murdered in a church, a jacket button in the dead man's hand leads them to a clue. The agents identify the alleged owner of the button (an Englishman with a German wife). They're trying to lure him into a trap. To this end, the espionage-driven "couple" seeks to get acquainted with the already elderly English-German couple. In the meantime, Mrs. Ashenden frequents Marvin, but rejects his advances.
Meanwhile, Elsa has scruples about her assignment, as she becomes more and more convinced that even a political murder is morally reprehensible. Adding to her changed attitude is her burgeoning love for Edgar/Richard. "The General", on the other hand, is increasingly turning out to be a murderous driving force on behalf of the British government.
The elimination of the enemy by the General and Ashenden, whose sense of duty to his country compels him to act as the "ultimate" espionage mission, is now to be accomplished on a mountain hike. Eventually, Ashenden shuns direct involvement and leaves it to the "General" to throw the old man into the deep while Ashenden watches with a telescope.
Tragically, however, it turns out that the victim was merely a harmless tourist. Horrified by the senseless murder, Elsa and Ashenden decide to abort the mission.
However, a new clue shakes Ashenden's resolve again: through an acquaintance, the General has found out that a nearby chocolate factory is used by the German opponents as a conspiratorial cell. The two men spy on the scene, but then have to flee from the police. But they were able to find out that Marvin is the man they're looking for.
Believing that Elsa, who is really clinging to Marvin out of disappointment in her lover, would have also exposed him, they catch the train that Marvin wants to get off on at the last minute. Marvin reveals his identity to Elsa, but at the same time, he sees through her disguise. Ashenden and his Mexican colleague find the two and set out to liquidate Marvin. Elsa, however, foils the act at gunpoint, and responds to Ashenden's patriotic warnings with a reference to the primacy of their moral integrity.
At this very moment, the train is derailed by an air attack by British pilots. Marvin is mortally pinned, but just before he dies, he still manages to shoot the murderous "General". Elsa and Ashenden sink into each other's arms, free from the ultimately unbearable decisions of life and death. Back in England, they both quit the service.

story_text_a:
David Lewis is so affected by the death of his beautiful wife, Gillian, who fell from the mast of their yacht on a sailing trip, that he turns their summer cottage in Nantucket, Massachusetts into a permanent home and spends most of his time on the beach there, communicating with Gillian's spirit and unwittingly neglecting his daughter, Rachel.
On the second anniversary of Gillian's death, David invites her sister, Esther Wheeler, and Esther's husband, Paul, to stay for the weekend. She insists on bringing a friend named Kevin Dollof, who she hopes David will become romantically interested in. He, however, ignores her in proceeding with a ritualistic celebration of Gillian's birthday.
The events of the weekend cause the adults to re-examine their relationships; Esther and Paul have to deal with the problem posed to their marriage by Rachel's provocative friend, Cindy, while David comes to realize that he can be a loving and attentive father to Rachel without betraying the memory of Gillian.
story_text_b: David Lewis has been so affected by the death of his wife Gillian, who drowned two years ago, that he spends most of his time on the beach in Nantucket communicating with Gillian's spirit and neglecting his daughter Rachel. David has invited his sister-in-law Esther and her husband for the weekend. The couple comes with a friend, hoping that David will take an interest in her while Rachel invites her girlfriend.

story_text_a:
A rich novelist, Stephen Byrne, who lives and works by a river, accidentally kills his attractive maid after she begins screaming when he makes a drunken pass.  The writer manipulates his brother, John, who is physically impaired with a limp, to help him dispose of the body. Making use of a sack, which Stephen has borrowed from John for carrying firewood, they stuff the maid inside and dump her into the river. Days later, the sack and body float up and pass Stephen's house.  He goes onto the water and desperately tries to retrieve it, but fails. The police recover the bundle and, because John's initials have been stencilled on the sack, it is all traceable to him.
An inquest is held and, to Stephen's great pleasure, a cloud of suspicion hangs over John, who is tortured by his role in the situation and contemplates suicide. He and Stephen's wife, Marjorie, harbour feelings for each other. Stephen, meanwhile, has used the maid's disappearance and death as publicity for his books. Looking to reap great financial gain, he begins writing a novel specifically about the crime; in it he implicates himself.
The circumstances are resolved after Stephen resorts to deliberate attempts at murder.
story_text_b:
Lo scrittore Stephen Byrne vive in una bella casa vittoriana di stile rococò sulla riva di un fiume.
La corrente limacciosa trasporta ogni genere di relitti: un'inquadratura mostra il primo piano della carcassa di una mucca gonfia d'acqua. La vicina di casa, Mrs Ambrose, è una donna curiosa e pettegola, sempre pronta a fare domande e a lanciare sguardi indiscreti, ma sta a lei esprimere il disgusto per lo spettacolo dei rifiuti gettati nell'acqua   "Odio questo fiume!".
Stephen non sta passando un periodo fortunato nel suo lavoro: gli manca l'ispirazione e spesso l'editore è insoddisfatto dei suoi manoscritti e glieli respinge. Una sera d'estate scrive all'aperto, nel giardino, sotto il gazebo. La moglie Marjorie è andata da dei parenti, in campagna, ed è rimasto solo in casa con la giovane cameriera, Emily.
La ragazza gli chiede il permesso di fare il bagno al piano superiore, essendosi guastato quello di servizio nel seminterrato. Si ode lo scrosciare l'acqua, la finestra è illuminata: verso di essa lui alza gli occhi di tanto in tanto. La giovane guarda compiaciuta il suo bel viso prender forma sullo specchio appannato e si profuma come fa la sua padrona.  L'uomo si accende di desiderio. Entra in casa e nel buio del vano delle scale la aspetta. Mentre Emily scende le scale se ne intravedono le belle gambe, lasciate scoperte dall'accappatoio allentato. Stephen tenta di abbracciarla, ma incontra la sua imprevista resistenza. Lei grida e lui, contrariato e preoccupato di richiamare l'attenzione della vicina che è fuori in giardino, le mette una mano sulla bocca e la strangola con tale violenza che la ragazza soffoca e si affloscia esanime.
Proprio in questo frangente arriva il fratello John. Stephen non può fare a meno di raccontargli il fatto e John gli consiglia di consegnarsi alla polizia. L'uomo, non sposato, conduce una piccola ditta e tra l'altro è storpio, inizialmente rifiuta di aiutare il fratello, egli lo ha tirato fuori d'impaccio numerose volte, ma stavolta si tratta di omicidio.
Adducendo il pretesto (falso) che Marjorie è incinta e non potrebbe affrontare un tale scandalo, Stephen costringe il fratello, che ha una grande simpatia e stima della moglie, ad aiutarlo.
I due portano il corpo, infilato e chiuso in un sacco di iuta, nel fiume, dove al largo lo gettano appesantito da un'ancora. Stephen inscena poi la finzione della fuga della ragazza. Fa sparire dall'armadio i suoi abiti e sottrae un paio di orecchini di opale dallo scrigno di sua moglie Marjorie, per attribuirle il movente del furto.
La sparizione di Emily diventa un giallo misterioso e dà notorietà allo scrittore che ne trae beneficio: le sue opere godono di una pubblicità insperata e lui inizia a scrivere un romanzo che adombra la sua ultima esperienza, inoltre, sprezzante per la fine della povera ragazza, non perde occasione per denigrarla e accusare di ogni comportamento immorale in pubblico. Ciò manda su tutte le furie il fratello, che all'ennesimo sproloquio di Flora Bantam, sua governante, sulla ragazza, dà in escandescenze licenziandola.
Ma la marea muta e il sacco torna in superficie. Sulla iuta è stampato il nome di John Byrne, in quanto di proprietà della ditta, egli lo aveva prestato al fratello per far raccogliere della legna alla sua domestica. I sospetti si concentrano quindi su John. Inoltre, durante il processo, viene accusato dalla sua governante, donna gelosa e possessiva che essendo stata appena licenziata, nutre risentimenti verso l'uomo. Soltanto la vicina depone favorevolmente per lui. Stephen fa ben poco per scagionarlo. Il giudice tuttavia conclude con un non luogo a procedere.
John è tormentato dal rimorso di avere aiutato a nascondere un delitto, inoltre essendo ritenuto nel villaggio responsabile della morte di Emily, riceve continue lettere di minacce ed è malvisto dai vicini e dai clienti della ditta. Gli fa visita Marjorie, affranta per il comportamento del marito che da un po' di tempo è irascibile e nervoso, la donna trova John profondamente depresso e temendo possa commettere qualcosa di irreparabile, tornata in casa, supplica il marito di raggiungere il fratello e confortarlo.
Ma Stephen ha ben altre intenzioni, recupera gli orecchini di Emily, che aveva nascosto in casa e di sera, assicuratosi dell'assenza del fratello va a nasconderli nella sua abitazione, dopodiché lo trova assorto mentre passeggia sulla sponda del fiume. John, stufo della situazione e irritato dal comportamento di Stephen, gli manifesta la sua intenzione di confessare tutto alla polizia.
Stephen attua quindi il suo piano, lo colpisce con una catena, stordendolo e lo fa getta nel fiume.
La moglie Marjorie, resasi conto nel corso del processo, della meschinità del comportamento del marito nei confronti del fratello,  inizia a nutrire dei sospetti sulla sua colpevolezza e quando legge la bozza del romanzo che sta scrivendo ne ha la certezza.
Tornato in casa visibilmente stravolto, Stephen ha una discussione con la moglie, la quale rivelandogli sinceramente quello che pensa, provoca la collera incontenibile dell'uomo che tenta di strangolarla, ma imprevedibilmente appare John, fradicio e ferito che è riuscito a risalire la sponda del fiume, facendo desistere Stephen dalla sua azione.
Il destino ha preparato allo scrittore una condanna inappellabile. Fuori di sé e in fuga, in una tenda che svolazza nel corridoio della casa gli pare di vedere il fantasma di Emily, inciampa, scivola, la tenda gli si avvolge attorno al collo, nel tentativo di districarsi precipita nel vano delle scale e si schianta al suolo.

story_text_a:
The film tells the story of Apollo 13, the seventh manned American space mission to the Moon of the Apollo program, which included astronaut James Lovell (NASA's most experienced), Fred Haise, and Jack Swigert.
The launch took place on April 11, 1970 at the Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center in Houston at exactly 1:13 p.m. The take-off was a success, despite a shutdown of the No. 5 rocket engine.
But at 9:07 p.m. on April 13, 1970, astronaut Jack Swigert alerted NASA's command center that an explosion aboard their craft had destroyed one oxygen tank and damaged the other tank, as well as several of the spacecraft's fuel cells. The main engine of the service module (CSM) may also be damaged, making the planned lunar mission impossible and forcing Houston Mission Control to maintain a lunar orbit trajectory for the Apollo 13 crew's return to Earth.
The loss of power caused by the failure will then force the astronauts to cut off all non-essential devices on board, leaving them with no help to guide their craft when they return to Earth.
story_text_b: The Griswolds win a European vacation tour where the usual chaos ensues.

story_text_a:
The Number One, a famous nightclub in Rome, was at the centre of a major scandal in 1971: a cocaine trafficking that involved international jet set names.
At "Number One", the playboys Benni (Chris Avram) and Leo (Venantino Venantini) rule the nightlife. In a Roman villa, Teddy Garner Jr. (Paolo Malco) mourns the sudden death of his wife Deborah. Two doctors have just found her dead and are taking her body away. His friends Massimo (Guido Mannari) and Dino (Howard Ross) reassure him. They now ask him to leave Rome quickly. The first result is a suicide, but Commissioner Vinci (Renzo Montagnani) doubts and begins his investigation. Teddy Garner left the country in a hurry to escape prosecution. Links are quickly made with the organized art theft, in which Massimo and Dino are active and do not hesitate to commit murders. Vinci now works in collaboration with the "Capitano" (Luigi Pistilli), the commander of the carabinieri. Sylvie Boisset (Claude Jade), a French actress who is a friend of playboy Benni, is the only one to attend Deborah's funeral. She informs the carabinieri of the hiding place of the stolen paintings in a convent. Later, Sylvie visits her friend Massimo, played by Guido Mannari. She learns terrible things from him. Meanwhile, the police searched the convent and found the paintings. Sylvie goes back to the carabinieri and makes a statement to the captain about Deborah's death: When Tony arrived with his friends Massimo and Dino in Deborah's house, she was lying on the bed, naked and rolling, foam on her lips. Dino reassured his friends by telling them to wait for Deborah's agony. While the men played cards, Deborah died after a long agony. Only then do they call the doctor. And Tony is leaving Italy in a hurry. Sylvie tells the captain she's worried about Massimo, who's been missing for four days. Sylvie's testimony led to a new autopsy of Deborah's body. But investigators can't find a culprit, because suspects or even witnesses regularly disappear...
story_text_b:
The Los Angeles of today: Successful oncologist Michael Reynolds, an overachiever who flew with his
$176,000 Porsche 911 Turbo comes to work (digestive music at this point: What a Difference a Day Makes, Esther Phillips) examines a tumor in a 16-year-old felon named Brandon Blue Monroe. Monroe's doing time for murdering his stepfather and for armed robbery. There's no hope of recovery. On the contrary, the CT shows a terminal peritoneal sarcoma. He's bald from the chemo, and he's still smoking in front of the doctors. Reynolds is shocked by Monroe's ordinary manner and doesn't quite know how to deal with the antisocial boy. Suddenly, he's taken hostage in his own hospital despite guards and security measures, thanks to a smuggled firearm. The breakout was prepared long in advance.
Monroe, who has only weeks to live, drags the terrified doctor out onto the street and trades a gang member's sports car for a hastily painted car that turns out to be roadworthy. Monroe seems to be following a definite plan, moving with purpose and speed. At gunpoint, he forces Dr. Reynolds to race out of L.A.
In the beginning, Monroe was seen with his favorite mystical book "The Man Who Travels" in the prisoner transport "more like a penny notebook". He's half Navajo on his father's side, and he knows stories about a healing sacred mountain of his ancestors in Arizona, which he must reach alive at all costs. That's what he learned from that story. Under normal circumstances, the rather shallow and self-centered Dr. Reynolds doesn't think much of natural religions and esotericism. First, they have to find the medicine man Skyhorse on the reservation, who Monroe used to know, and who knows about the rite.
Patrol cars are on their tail, and Monroe's got Reynolds on full throttle. Intervals follow: an explosive confrontation with a biker gang, a slightly surreal one with an elderly, spiritually receptive hippie lady living in the wilderness, and an encounter with gospel-singing churchgoers. To make matters worse, Reynolds is bitten by a rattlesnake in the desert before they even reach Flagstaff. Monroe manages to neutralize the snake venom with an electric shock from the car battery. From then on, Monroe's health deteriorated rapidly; at the same time, the mood among the unequal men somewhat normalized. A prayer from "The Man Who Travels" must comfort Monroe more and more. Despite the hopelessness of the whole enterprise, and although the police are to be expected, the boy does not deviate from his plan and his obscure belief. Then they meet Skyhorse's granddaughter and finally him, who leads them.
Monroe would actually release Reynolds now, but near Shiprock, he's in dire need of antibiotics, and Reynolds breaks into a hospital for him. As a result, Reynolds decides to stay with him. From there, they will ascend the Holy Mountain.
A police helicopter is picking up the fugitives. Monroe's face has literally lost all color, he's sweating and shaking all over his body. Kidnapping has turned into a death escort. But Dr. Reynolds' worldview and self-image have changed for the better. The experience brought back memories of the last days of his brother, who died similarly. At the end of the long chase and the climb of the mountain range, Reynolds has to carry it, so to speak, they reach the Holy Mountain and the magic lake on its summit. With a joyous May perfection be before me. May perfection be behind me. May perfection be upon me. May there be perfection under me. May perfection be all around me. (Original: beauty, beauty) Monroe disappears over the water, in the noise and wind of the helicopter. He becomes one with the landscape.

story_text_a:
Un uomo cammina per le strade di una Londra deserta ed assolata, si tratta del giornalista Peter Stenning, che sta recandosi nella sede del Daily Express, il quotidiano per il quale lavora. 
Qui giunto inizia a dettare un articolo.
Con un flashback si torna indietro di alcuni mesi all'inizio della vicenda.
Peter sta passando un brutto periodo, ha divorziato da poco perdendo l'affidamento del figlioletto che può vedere raramente, trascura il lavoro ed ha iniziato a bere.
Il suo amico ed esperto collega Bill Maguire gli dà tutto il sostegno possibile coprendo le sue frequenti assenze al giornale e scrivendo articoli in suo nome.
Intanto strani eventi climatici avvengono in tutto il pianeta: inondazioni e violenti nubifragi da una parte, siccità e temperature molto elevate dall'altra.
Incaricato di chiedere informazioni al riguardo al centro meteorologico nazionale, Peter si reca sul posto, ma non ha fortuna perché gli esperti lo cacciano via in malo modo, facendo venire al giornalista dei sospetti sul fatto che stiano nascondendo qualcosa. 
Iniziano a trapelare voci secondo le quali tutto è stato causato da esperimenti svolti nella zona artica da statunitensi e sovietici, infatti, gli uni all'insaputa degli altri, hanno fatto esplodere in contemporanea delle potenti testate nucleari.
Peter inizia una relazione sentimentale con Jeanie, una ragazza che lavora al centro meteorologico, e grazie al suo aiuto il giornalista riuscirà ad uscire dal suo periodo nero e a smetterla con l'alcool.
L'intera condizione climatica mondiale intanto sta peggiorando e l'Inghilterra è investita da un'ondata di calore senza precedenti. 
Jeanie rivela a Peter una scoperta fatta dai suoi superiori: gli esperimenti nucleari hanno spostato l'asse terrestre di alcuni gradi modificando le zone climatiche del pianeta.
Peter ha ormai ripreso in mano anche la sua carriera, infatti, sono i suoi articoli che informano la popolazione sul susseguirsi dei fatti.
La situazione precipita quando gli scienziati sovietici rivelano che oltre l'asse anche l'orbita della Terra è stata modificata, il pianeta si sta avvicinando sempre più al sole e continuando così la razza umana si estinguerà per il troppo calore. 
Il governo britannico decide a causa della forte siccità di razionare l'acqua e a breve iniziano i primi disordini in tutta Londra, dove i cittadini compiono atti vandalici e di sciacallaggio.
Di comune accordo, le potenze mondiali decidono di tentare una disperata soluzione, fare esplodere diverse testate nucleari in un punto preciso della Siberia, cercando di rimettere la Terra nella sua orbita originaria.
Il conto alla rovescia per l'esplosione è trasmesso in diretta via radio, mentre tutto il mondo attende con trepidazione di sapere se l'operazione ha avuto successo.
Si ritorna alla sequenza iniziale con Peter che detta un articolo in cui ricorda gli errori commessi dalla razza umana e auspica un futuro migliore per la Terra.
Intanto, si vedono le due diverse bozze, pronte per la prima pagina del quotidiano: una dice “la Terra è salva”, mentre l'altra “la Terra è condannata”.
story_text_b:
The journalist Peter Stenning walks through the orphaned streets of London. Exhausted, he reaches his newspaper office and tries to type an editorial on the typewriter. Because of the heat, the roller is useless, so he telephones the printer with the article. Stenning begins the article by saying that 30 minutes have passed since the detonation of the "correction bombs" and the world will know within the next few hours whether this is the end or a new beginning.
The film then flashes back 90 days as reporters from London's Daily Express newspaper report in confusion on abnormal weather events around the world. Reports of plane crashes caused by sunspots are piling up. New York is battered by blizzards, the Soviet Union is ravaged by devastating tornadoes, and Londoners are suffering from a severe heat wave. Since there are no official statements on the situation, the media indulge in speculation.
Two employees of the newspaper, veteran reporter Stenning and science editor Bill Maguire, discover the cause of the weather disturbances: the Americans and Soviets have conducted a nuclear test simultaneously, the Americans at the North Pole, the Soviets at the South Pole. Stenning makes contact with Jeanie Craig, who works as a telephone operator at the Met Office. Through it, he learns that the nutation, or tilt, of the earth has changed by 11 degrees. In an editorial conference, the College later learns through the editor Arthur Christiansen (who in real life was actually the editor of the Daily Express and plays himself) of a press conference of Soviet scientists in Moscow: Due to the explosions, the Earth has left its orbit and is drifting towards the sun. The newspaper publishes this news and causes a panic among the population. According to Maguire, mankind has only four months left to live because of the steady rise in temperatures, which are already reaching over 100 degrees Fahrenheit [40°C] in London and over 100 degrees Fahrenheit [60°C] in Mexico City.
In order to control the panic, governments take security measures. Cities are being evacuated, food and water are being rationed. Even so, there are looting and demonstrations. Scientists from several countries are working on a plan to detonate four large atomic bombs in western Siberia in order to return to its original orbit. On the day of the planned detonation, people will seek shelter in air raid shelters and basements. As police cars drive through the streets, counting the remaining time until the ignition, Stenning, Craig and Maguire head to their regular bar, where they toast each other just before the end of the countdown. The detonation of the "correction bombs" is apparently so strong that the effects are still felt in London: the pub is shaken slightly, the dust comes down from the ceiling. Shortly after, Stenning goes to the editorial office, where he wants to wait for the effect of the explosions and passes his text to the printing press. At the same time, the newspaper's editors have prepared two headlines for selection in the next issue. One is: "The world is saved". A nation is praying. A nation prays), the other: Doomsday. Now the nation prays. Now nation prays).
The camera then swings over the houses of London to St Paul's Cathedral, under the closing lines of Stenning's editorial: "And if there is still a new future for man, then it is time for him to forget his ruthless pride and his quest for power. Then he must replace all that with love. Maybe one day he'll be able to say, "How beautiful the light is". And raise his eyes to the sun. The movie ends with bells ringing.

story_text_a: L'héritier d'un meurtrier est possédé par l'esprit de celui-ci : investissant le manoir familial, d'étranges visions, lourdes de menaces, commencent très vite à le hanter. En parallèle, quelques membres du voisinage, visiblement intéressés, mettent tout en œuvre pour attirer son amitié. D'abord courtois et indécis, le héros se prête au jeu, mais comme happé par le passé qui resurgit, il ne tarde pas à perdre pied, voire à sombrer dangereusement dans la démence...
story_text_b: The heir of a murderer is possessed by the spirit of the murderer: invading the family mansion, strange visions, heavy with threats, soon begin to haunt him. At the same time, some interested neighbors try their best to befriend him. Initially courteous and indecisive, the hero lends himself to the game, but as caught by the past that resurfaces, he soon loses his footing, even sinking dangerously into madness...

story_text_a: Der Künstler Anthony McCoy zieht mit seiner Freundin Brianna Cartwright in eine Luxuswohnung im neu gentrifizierten Stadtteil Cabrini-Green in Chicago. In der Nachbarschaft erzählt man sich die Geschichte des „Candyman“, eines Killers aus der Vergangenheit mit einem Haken in der Hand, der herbeigerufen wird, wenn man es wagt, seinen Namen fünfmal zu wiederholen, und dabei in einen Spiegel schaut. Zunächst nutzt Anthony diese Legende als Inspiration in seinen Bildern. Es kommt zu bestialischen Morden in der Kunstwelt und Anthony wird plötzlich medial beachtet. Er malt immer wahnhafter und seine Haut verändert sich nach einem Bienenstich krankhaft. Als Brianna der Sache auf den Grund gehen will, wird sie kurzerhand entführt und wohnt so einer Zeremonie bei, bei der Anthony die Hand abgeschlagen wird und einen Haken erhält und somit die Candyman-Rache-Saga weiterführen soll. Er wird jedoch von einem herbeieilenden Polizisten erschossen. Als Brianna selbst von der Polizei abgeführt wird und zu polizeifreundlichen Aussagen genötigt wird, nutzt sie selbst die Candyman-Beschwörung, um Rachetaten auszuführen.
story_text_b:
In 1977, in Chicago's Cabrini-Green housing projects, a child witnesses the murder of Sherman Fields, a homeless African-American man with a hook for a hand. Suspected of giving a white child a razor blade in a candy, Sherman is beaten to death by the police, but is later proven innocent.
Thirty years after the events of the first film, visual artist Anthony McCoy lives in Chicago with his girlfriend, art gallery director Brianna Cartwright. Brianna's brother, Troy, tells her the urban legend of Helen Lyle, a graduate student who committed a massacre in the early 1990s. Her rampage culminated in a bonfire outside Cabrini-Green's social housing project when she attempted to sacrifice a baby. Residents were able to rescue the boy before Helen perished in the fire in an apparent act of self-immolation.
Desperate to find a creative spark to turn his career around, Anthony scours the renovated Cabrini-Green for inspiration. He finally meets William Burke, owner of a laundry, who introduces him to Candyman's story. When Burke was young, he had a terrifying encounter with Sherman Fields, a hook-handed man whom the police believed was responsible for putting a razor blade in a candy that caused a girl's death. Burke inadvertently alerted the police to Sherman's presence within the walls of one of the apartment blocks, leading them to beat Sherman to death. When the children continued to receive candy with razor blades inside, Sherman was exonerated, and legend implies that if someone says "Candyman" five times to a mirror, Sherman's spirit will appear and kill the summoner.
Inspired, Anthony develops an art exhibition based on the Candyman legend and exhibits it at Brianna's art gallery. However, he is dismayed when he does not get a positive reaction. That night, one of Brianna's co-workers and her girlfriend are killed by the Candyman after saying their name five times in front of a piece of Anthony's exhibit consisting of a mirror, and the next morning a horrified Brianna discovers their bodies. The legend spreads and more people are killed after repeating the Candyman's name, including an art critic and his girlfriend, and even a group of high school girls, triggering a police investigation looking for a killer who calls himself "Say My Name".
Anthony begins to undergo a physical transformation, stemming from a bee sting he received on his hand at Cabrini-Green that turns into a huge crust that begins to spread throughout his body. Besides, he's slowly becoming obsessed with the legend. Subsequently, Anthony, in search of answers, meets again with Burke, who reveals to him that "Candyman is not a he, it is a whole hive" and tells him of the different versions that exist of the legend, such as William Bell, Samuel Evans and the original entity: Daniel Robitaille. That same night, Anthony has a heated argument with Brianna, who ends up abandoning him.
The next night, Anthony goes to a hospital, where he learns that his mother, Anne-Marie, lied about his birth and, when confronted, reluctantly reveals that he was the baby Helen rescued from the fire the night she died. Although Helen saved him from Robitaille himself, the first Candyman who kidnapped him and planned to sacrifice him in the fire, Anne-Marie never told him because she wanted Anthony to have a normal life. The community had sworn never to repeat the legend of the Candyman after that night, and she fears what might happen now that someone has broken the pact. Anthony leaves, resigned to his fate, and wanders the modern Cabrini-Green townhouses.
Concerned about Anthony, Brianna realizes that Burke told her about the Candyman first and goes to Cabrini-Green to look for them. In the laundry, she is attacked by Burke, who takes her to an abandoned church where Anthony, whose body continues to deteriorate, awaits her. Anthony enters a dissociated state and attempts to save her as Burke reveals that he not only witnessed Sherman's death, but also saw Sherman's spirit return as the Candyman, and witnessed how he killed his older sister and a friend who summoned him. Above all, Burke knew that Anthony was the baby who was kidnapped by the Candyman and plans to have the police shoot Anthony to create a new legend with the Candyman as an instrument of revenge and not as a symbol of the pain and suffering of African Americans. To complete Anthony's transformation into the Candyman, Burke cuts off his right hand and replaces it with a hook.
Brianna manages to escape from the church and is pursued by Burke through Cabrini-Green, whom she cruelly stabs to death. Anthony appears and collapses in her arms as the police, lured by Burke, appear and shoot Anthony to death. Brianna is arrested and handcuffed, and while an officer tries to intimidate her into accepting that Anthony provoked the police into shooting her, Brianna uses the rearview mirror of the police car to summon the Candyman. This one shows up, now in the guise of Anthony, and ends up massacring the police. As more police arrive on the scene, Anthony assumes the appearance of Robitaille (it is revealed that he has been taking the forms of Sherman and Anthony due to their tragic deaths) and approaches Brianna with a mass of bees on the upper torso, ordering her to "tell everyone".
The film's end credits include an animated shadow puppet assembly of various Candyman members such as Robitaille, Sherman, Anthony Crawford, James Byrd Jr., George Stinney and lastly, Anthony himself.

story_text_a: In 1971, David Bowie was at a turning point in his career. While making his first trip to the United States, he met his publicist for Mercury Records, Ron Oberman. The latter urges him to imagine a character. It will therefore be Ziggy Stardust, which the singer uses notably for the album The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars.
story_text_b: Barney Lincoln is a compulsive gambler who organizes a scam to make his life easier: he breaks into a printing plant and marks the clichés of playing cards to make them recognizable and wins a lot of money. Shortly afterwards, he goes to Scotland Yard on the report of Angela McGinnis, the daughter of a police inspector who, having learned of the scam, convinces Barry to keep it quiet on the condition that he lose an equally large sum.

story_text_a: Gerald (Edward de Souza) and Marianne Harcourt (Jennifer Daniel), are a newlywed couple in early 20th-century Bavaria who find themselves trapped by a vampire cult led by Dr. Ravna (Noel Willman) and their children Carl (Barry Warren) and Sabena (Jacquie Wallis).
story_text_b:
The unconventional Father Charles "Chuck" O'Malley (Bing Crosby) is assigned to St. Mary's parish, which includes a run-down inner-city school building on the verge of being condemned. O'Malley is to recommend whether or not the school should be closed and the children sent to another school with modern facilities; but the sisters feel that God will provide for them.
They put their hopes in Horace P. Bogardus (Henry Travers), a businessman who has constructed a modern building next door to the school which they hope he will donate to them. Father O'Malley and the dedicated but stubborn Sister Superior, Mary Benedict (Ingrid Bergman), both wish to save the school, but their different views and methods often lead to disagreements. One such involves student Eddie (Dickie Tyler), who is being bullied by another. A more serious one regards the promotion of an eighth-grade student, Patsy (Joan Carroll) of Syracuse, New York, whom the parish has taken in while her mother attempts to get back on her feet.
Sister Benedict contracts tuberculosis and the physician recommends to Father O'Malley that she be transferred to a dry climate with non-parochial duties, but without telling her the reason. She assumes the transfer is because of her disagreements with O'Malley and struggles to understand the reasons for the path set out for her. Just before Sister Benedict departs, Father O'Malley reveals the true reason for her temporary transfer, and she then leaves happily, looking forward to her return.

story_text_a:
Adrián (Quim Gutierrez), a young orchestra conductor is viewing a recorded video of his girlfriend Belén (Clara Lago) informing him of leaving him. Adrián becomes distraught. While drinking away his sorrows at a bar, he meets Fabiana (Martina Garcia) and they develop a relationship. Fabiana moves into the house that Adrián was sharing with Belén.  Strange things begin to occur in the bathroom, with Fabiana observing strange noises coming from the sink and bathtub, and being scalded by an abruptly hot shower.
Adrián becomes a suspect in the disappearance of Belén; however, the investigators can find no evidence of Adrián's involvement in Belén's disappearance. One of the police investigators, apparently a former boyfriend of Fabiana, warns Adrián that if anything happens to Fabiana he will kill Adrián.
The house belongs to Emma, a German woman, who reveals a soundproof secret room intended for her former Nazi officer husband. Belén, driven by jealousy over Adrián's connection with violinist Verónica, follows Emma's suggestion to pretend she's leaving him. She records a breakup video and hides in the secret room, equipped with one-way mirrors to spy on Adrián's reaction. Belén plans to end the ruse, but loses the key, trapping herself without a way to contact Adrián.
Fabiana finds the key to the secret room, but she does not know what it is used for. Fabiana eventually figures out that Belén is trapped in the house because Belén is able to communicate through tapping on the pipes in the secret room, creating ripples in the full bathroom sink. As Fabiana is ready to open the door, she pauses and decides not to rescue Belén because she might lose Adrián.
Despite her inner turmoil, Fabiana opens the secret room's door to check on the unresponsive Belén. Jealousy stoked by an investigator's pictures of Adrián and Verónica influences Fabiana's decision. Inside the room, she finds Belén lying on a bed. Unexpectedly, Belén knocks Fabiana out, rendering her unconscious, and locks her in. Belén leaves the house, placing the secret room's key on a bed for Adrián and attaching a photo of them to the mirrored door. The film ends with Belén alone on the beach, and Fabiana trapped, awaiting rescue.
story_text_b: Adrián, un jeune et brillant chef d'orchestre espagnol, s'est installé dans une immense maison en Colombie depuis peu où il dirige le  philharmonique de Bogota. Mais Belén, sa fiancée avec qui il file le parfait amour, ne tarde pas à le quitter sans raison avant de demeurer totalement introuvable. Un soir, alors qu'il va se saouler dans un bar pour oublier son chagrin, le jeune homme fait la connaissance de la belle Fabiana. Une histoire démarre rapidement entre eux, et celle-ci vient s'installer dans la maison d'Adrián. Les enquêteurs commencent alors à s'intéresser à la disparition subite et inexpliquée de Belén, suspectant Adrián d'avoir commis le pire. Quant à elle, Fabiana est témoin de phénomènes étranges, se sent observée, et en vient à avoir peur de la demeure. Mais Belén n'est pas partie bien loin...

story_text_a:
Bu lives in a small fishing village in Taiwan. When she fishes a bottle post from the sea and in it the message "I am alone. How about you? When she finds a Hong Konger's address, she sets off to find her so-called prince charming.
It meets the sender. Since this one is homosexual, only a friendship develops. But she's meeting the millionaire Chan. The two have a good time together, but when Chan is more involved in business and also has to deal with envy, he neglects Bu, who returns disappointed to her home village. Only now does the millionaire realize how much she meant to him. He tracks her down and eventually manages to win her heart.
story_text_b: Upon the death of her parents, young Mary Lennox, a lonely child with an exuberant imagination, left India to join the British countryside. Exiled to her uncle Archibal's mansion, she meets her cousin Colin, a young boy named Dickon, the adorable dog Fozzie, and an ingenious redhead. Together they will share the discovery of a magical and wonderful garden that will mark the beginning of an extraordinary adventure and friendship.

story_text_a: Georgia Byrd est une employée d'un magasin à rayons multiples qui a toujours vécu sa vie sans faire de vagues. Le jour où elle apprend qu'elle est atteinte d'une maladie incurable en phase terminale, elle décide de retirer toutes ses économies pour se payer les dernières vacances de sa vie dans la luxueuse ville d'eau tchèque de Karlovy Vary où elle se permettra tout ce qu'elle s'était toujours refusée.
story_text_b:
Georgia Byrd (Queen Latifah), an employee in the cookware department at Kragen's store in New Orleans, is a shy, unassuming woman who longs to cook professionally and who records her dreams of a better life in a diary titled "Possibilities". It's the holiday season. While flirting with a co-worker Sean Williams (LL Cool J), she hits her head on a cabinet door and is taken to the store's health center for a CT scan. There he is told by his physician, Dr. Gupta (Ranjit Chowdhry), who has several brain tumors resulting from a rare neurological disorder called Lampington's Disease. Since her medical insurance won't cover the exorbitant cost of an operation, Georgia resigns herself to the fact that she has only a few weeks to live, quits her job, liquidates her assets, and heads for a dream vacation in the spa town of Karlovy Vary in the Czech Republic, more precisely at the luxurious Grandhotel Pupp.
Free of inhibitions and determined to live life to the fullest, Georgia checks into the Presidential Suite, buys a designer wardrobe from expensive boutiques, makes extensive use of the hotel's spa facilities, attempts snowboarding and BASE jumping off a dam, enjoys succulent meals prepared by the famous chef Didier (Gérard Depardieu), and wins a small fortune playing roulette in the casino. She impresses the hotel staff, with the exception of the guest services manager, Ms. Gunther (Susan Kellermann), with his naive manner and outspoken kindness, and mingles with some of the other guests, including Matthew Kragen (Timothy Hutton), a self-help guru and casually the owner of the shop where he works; his assistant/Mrs. Burns (Alicia Witt); loving Senator Dillings (Giancarlo Esposito) from his home state of Louisiana; and prominent Congressman Stewart (Michael Nouri). Kragen is skeptical about Georgia's origins and suspects that she is trying to sabotage his business, but the rest are charmed by her free spirit.
When Kragen is bribing Miss. Gunther to unearth information about Georgia's background, finds a letter that Georgia has written to give instructions on how to dispose of her remains after her death.
