Disguised as a bounty hunter, Princess Leia infiltrates the palace under the pretense of having captured Chewbacca and unfreezes Han, but is caught and enslaved. Luke soon arrives to bargain for his friends' release, but Jabba drops him through a trapdoor to be eaten by a rancor. After Luke kills it, Jabba sentences him, Han, and Chewbacca to death by being fed to the sarlacc, a deadly beast entombed in the desert floor. Having hidden his new green lightsaber inside R2-D2, Luke frees himself and his friends. The group battle Jabba's men aboard his sail barge. During the chaos, Boba Fett falls into the sarlacc after Han inadvertently damages his jet pack. Meanwhile, Leia strangles Jabba to death with her chains. After destroying Jabba's sail barge, the group escapes.
As the others rendezvous with the Rebel Alliance, Luke returns to Dagobah to complete his Jedi training with Yoda, whom he discovers is dying. Yoda confirms that Darth Vader is Luke's father, the former Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker, and reveals that there is another Skywalker, before passing away and becoming one with the Force. Obi-Wan Kenobi's Force spirit tells Luke the truth about Anakin's fall to the dark side, that Leia is his twin sister, and that he must face Vader again to finish his training and defeat the Empire.
The Alliance learns that the Empire has been constructing a second Death Star under the supervision of the Emperor. The station is protected by an energy shield on the forest moon of Endor. To destroy its generator, Han leads a strike team which includes Luke, Leia and Chewbacca. Using a stolen Imperial shuttle to arrive undetected, the team encounters a tribe of Ewoks, gaining their trust after an initial conflict. Later, Luke tells Leia that she is his sister and Vader is their father. Surrendering to Imperial troops, he is brought before Vader, and fails to convince him to reject the dark side of the Force.
Luke is brought to the Emperor, who intends to turn him to the dark side, and reveals that his friends and the Rebel fleet are headed into a trap. On Endor, Han's team is captured by Imperial forces, but a counterattack by the Ewoks allows the Rebels to infiltrate the shield generator. Meanwhile, Lando Calrissian and Admiral Ackbar lead the Rebel assault on the Death Star, finding its shield still active and the Imperial fleet waiting for them.
The Emperor reveals to Luke that the Death Star is fully operational and orders the firing of its superlaser, destroying a Rebel starship. He tempts Luke to give in to his anger. Luke attempts to attack him, but Vader intervenes and the two engage in a lightsaber duel. Vader senses that Luke has a sister and threatens to turn her to the dark side if Luke does not. In retaliation, Luke defeats Vader, severing his prosthetic hand. The Emperor betrays Vader by ordering Luke to take Vader's place, but Luke refuses, declaring himself to be a Jedi, like his father before him. Enraged, the Emperor starts torturing Luke with Force lightning. Unwilling to let his son die, Vader betrays the Emperor by throwing him down a reactor shaft to his death, but he is mortally electrocuted in the process. Vader's final request is that Luke remove his mask so he can see his son with his own eyes, which he does. Redeemed, Anakin Skywalker dies.
After the strike team destroys the shield generator, Lando leads Rebel fighters into the Death Star's core. While the Rebel fleet destroys the Imperial command ship, Lando and X-wing fighter pilot Wedge Antilles destroy the Death Star's main reactor and escape before the station explodes. Meanwhile, Luke escapes in a shuttle. On Endor, Luke cremates his father's body on a pyre and reunites with his friends. As the Rebels celebrate their victory, Luke notices the Force spirits of Obi-Wan, Yoda, and Anakin watching nearby.
story_text_b:
Der in Karbonit tiefgefrorene Körper von Han Solo befindet sich nun im Besitz von Jabba, der ihn in seiner Wüstenfestung auf Tatooine als bizarren Wandschmuck aufgestellt hat. Bei dem Versuch, Han zu retten, wird Prinzessin Leia gefasst und als persönliche Sklavin von Jabba gehalten. In einer Rettungsaktion gelingt es jedoch Luke Skywalker, seine beiden Freunde zu befreien. Luke macht sich danach auf ins Dagobah-System, um seine Ausbildung beim alten Jedi-Meister Yoda zu beenden. Yoda aber erklärt Luke, dass er keiner weiteren Ausbildung bedürfe, um Vader gegenüberzutreten und ihn zu besiegen. Ein Sieg über Vader würde Luke zu einem Jedi-Ritter machen. Außerdem bestätigt Yoda, dass Vader Lukes Vater ist und früher einmal der Schüler von Obi-Wan Kenobi war. Kurz danach stirbt Yoda friedlich an Altersschwäche und wird eins mit der Macht. Nach Yodas Tod erfährt Luke durch den Machtgeist von Obi-Wan Kenobi, der ihm auf Dagobah erscheint, dass Leia seine Zwillingsschwester ist.
Währenddessen sammelt sich die Rebellenflotte, um Vorbereitungen für die entscheidende Schlacht gegen die Streitkräfte des Imperiums zu treffen. Das Imperium steht kurz vor der Vollendung eines neuen, mächtigeren Todessterns, dessen Bau der Imperator persönlich beaufsichtigt.
Eine kleine Kommandoeinheit der Rebellen unter der Leitung von Han, Luke und Leia begibt sich auf den Waldmond Endor, um den Generator des Schutzschildes zu zerstören, welcher den Todesstern umgibt. Dabei trifft der Stoßtrupp jedoch auf eine imperiale Patrouille mit Düsenschlitten. Luke und Leia verfolgen die Soldaten, werden dabei jedoch getrennt. Nach Leia stoßen auch die sie suchenden Han, Chewbacca und Luke auf die primitiven Ureinwohner des Mondes, die Ewoks. Diese halten C-3PO aufgrund seiner goldfarbenen Metallhülle für eine Gottheit. Der Droide erwirkt auf Anweisung Lukes, dass sie sich mit den Rebellen verbünden.
Luke plant indes, sich seinem Vater Darth Vader erneut in einem Zweikampf zu stellen und ihn von der dunklen Seite der Macht zurückholen. Zu diesem Zweck lässt er sich freiwillig gefangen nehmen. Er wird von Darth Vader auf den Todesstern gebracht, wo ihn der Imperator bereits erwartet, der Luke auf die dunkle Seite der Macht ziehen will. Als die Rebellenflotte eintrifft, ist der Schild des Todessterns noch aktiv und die Imperiale Armada verwickelt sie in eine aussichtslos scheinende Schlacht. Angesichts der Lage der Rebellen greift der verzweifelte Luke den Imperator mit seinem Lichtschwert an, wird jedoch von Vader aufgehalten; zwischen beiden beginnt ein Duell. Die Ewoks greifen im Verbund mit den Rebellen den Schildgenerator auf Endor an. Zusammen können sie die imperialen Truppen schlagen und den Generator sprengen.
Der Angriff auf den Todesstern beginnt, während Luke weiterhin gegen Darth Vader kämpft. Luke weiß, dass er der dunklen Seite der Macht verfallen würde, wenn er auf Wunsch des Imperators seinem Hass nachgibt und Vader tötet. Immer wieder versucht er, sich zurückzuhalten. Als Vader jedoch Lukes Gefühle durch die Macht erspürt, somit Leias wahre Herkunft erkennt und androht, sie bekehren zu wollen, gibt Luke seinem Hass nach: Er schlägt wild auf ihn ein und kann ihm die rechte Hand abtrennen, in der er sein Lichtschwert hält. Als Vader wehrlos zu Lukes Füßen liegt, fordert der Imperator ihn auf, Vader zu töten. Luke jedoch wirft sein Lichtschwert fort und weigert sich. Als ihn der Imperator daraufhin mit Machtblitzen töten will, ergreift Vader schließlich Partei für seinen Sohn Luke, der ihn unter Schmerzen um Hilfe bittet. Vader packt seinen Meister und schleudert ihn in einen Reaktorschacht des Todessterns, wo er augenscheinlich zu Tode kommt. Auch Darth Vader, den das Ausströmen der dunklen Macht aus dem Imperator schwer verletzt hat, bricht zusammen. Aber noch bevor er stirbt, lässt er sich von seinem Sohn die schwarze Atemmaske abnehmen, um ihn einmal noch mit seinen eigenen Augen sehen zu können. Luke kann nur noch mit Vaders Leichnam vom Todesstern entkommen.
Der Angriff der Rebellen führt kurze Zeit später auch zum Erfolg, und der zweite Todesstern wird in einer gewaltigen Explosion vernichtet.
Bei der Siegesfeier auf dem Waldmond trifft Luke wieder mit seinen Freunden zusammen. Während der Siegesfeier erscheinen die Machtgeister von Obi-Wan, Yoda und Anakin Skywalker, wobei Anakin in seiner jungen Gestalt erscheint. Mit einem rauschenden Fest feiern viele Planeten in der Galaxis ihre Befreiung von der Terrorherrschaft des Imperiums.

story_text_a:
Der ehemalige Tierarzt Amandus Rosenbach leidet zunehmend unter Alzheimer. Als er auf der Beerdigung seiner Frau Margarethe eine verwirrte Rede hält, bekommt der Zuschauer einen ersten Eindruck von seinem geistigen Zustand.
Auf Drängen seines Sohnes Niko zieht Amandus in dessen Haus nahe Hamburg. Nikos Ehe mit seiner Frau Sarah steht auf der Kippe, nachdem Niko erfahren hat, dass Sarah eine Affäre mit ihrem Chef Serge hatte. Schnell kommt es wegen Amandus’ geistigem Zustand zu mehreren kritischen Situationen; u. a. will er einen Kuchen backen und verursacht dabei beinahe einen Küchenbrand, den Sarah in letzter Sekunde verhindern kann.
Als Amandus’ geistiger und motorischer Verfall immer weiter voranschreitet und das Sommerfest von Niko und Sarah in einem Fiasko endet, sieht sich Niko gezwungen, ihn in eine betreuende Einrichtung zu geben, was Nicos elfjährige Tochter Tilda allerdings nicht hinnehmen will. Und so begibt sie sich mit ihrem Großvater auf eine Reise nach Venedig, wo Amandus seinerzeit mit seiner Frau die Flitterwochen verbracht hat. Von ihrem Kinderarzt Dr. Ehlers hat Tilda erfahren, dass es für Alzheimer-Patienten hilfreich sein kann, altbekannte Orte wiederzusehen.
Der Reisebeginn per Auto endet nach wenigen Kilometern mit einem glimpflich verlaufenden Unfall, als Amandus eine rote Ampel ignoriert. Per Zug geht es bis Bozen, dort verlässt Amandus auf der Suche nach einer Toilette versehentlich den Zug. Seine Enkelin zieht die Notbremse und versteckt sich mit Amandus auf der Bahnhofstoilette, bis die sie verfolgenden Polizisten die Suche aufgegeben haben. Abends werden sie von der Reinigungskraft Erdal gefunden, er vermittelt den beiden eine Weiterfahrt nach Venedig per Schaftransporter. Als dieser von der Polizei angehalten wird, können Amandus und Tilda noch rechtzeitig vor ihrer Entdeckung von der Ladefläche fliehen. Sie finden Unterschlupf in einem Kloster. Die Oberin ist von der Geschichte der beiden so gerührt, dass sie Amandus und Tilda bis nach Venedig fährt. Dort sind Niko und Sarah inzwischen per Flugzeug eingetroffen und checken im selben Hotel wie Amandus und Tilda ein.
In der folgenden Nacht verlässt Amandus, von Tilda unbemerkt, das Hotel. Tilda findet ihn am nächsten Morgen auf der Bank wieder, auf der Amandus vor vielen Jahren mit seiner Frau Margarethe gesessen hat. Seine Krankheit ist nun so weit fortgeschritten, dass er Tilda nicht mehr als seine Enkelin und „kleine Prinzessin“ erkennt. In diesem Moment werden die beiden von Niko und Sarah gefunden. Zu viert tritt man die Heimreise nach Hamburg an.
Sarah beschließt, ihren Job aufzugeben, um mehr Zeit für die Pflege von Amandus zu haben. Die zerrüttete Ehe von Niko und Sarah ist endgültig gerettet, als Sarah neun Monate nach dem Venedigbesuch Mutter eines Jungen wird, der nach seinem kranken Großvater benannt wird. Amandus erfährt noch eine glückliche Zeit mit seiner Familie, bis er in Tildas Beisein an Herzversagen stirbt. Bei der Beerdigung liegt Tilda im Gras und sieht von dort in den Himmel, von wo aus sie nun von Amandus beschützt wird, wie er es ihr zu Lebzeiten versprochen hat.
story_text_b: Amadeus is an elderly gentleman who suffers from Alzheimer's. Mick, son of Amadeus and father of a little girl named Tilda, brings Amadeus to the clinic against his will. Tilda herself must have smuggled her grandfather away to take him on a long trip to Venice.

story_text_a:
Due to countless cataclysms, mankind is forced to abandon Earth, attempting to settle on a new planet far from the solar system: Nova Prime.
But an alien civilization attacks humans with the Ursa, monsters with six legs and an insect-like body, completely blind, trained to sense the pheromones emanating from a body when it feels fear. Because of these monsters, the human race now faces a new extinction. For this purpose, General Cypher Raige trains a group of Rangers who are able to feel no fear, i.e. to "ghost", making themselves invisible to the attacks of the Bears.
In the past, due to an attack by such monsters, the same general had lost his firstborn, Senshi. In fact, she, being alone in the house with her little brother Kitai, had locked him inside a glass dome to prevent the Bear from smelling him, while she had sacrificed herself in his place, dying under the frightened gaze of her brother.
Kitai, growing up, decides to train to become a Ranger, like his father, but on the very day Cypher returns from a long mission, he fails the exam. Cypher, to rekindle his relationship with his son decides to abandon the Ranger body, so he decides to take him with him on his last mission: transporting a Bear to a training camp on a distant moon.
During the journey, an asteroid severely damages the spacecraft, which crashes on an unknown planet. Cypher and Kitai soon realize that they are the only survivors, and that they have landed right on Earth, which has now become an inhospitable jungle with an unbreathable atmosphere. Cypher, severely injured in one leg, cannot move, so the young Kitai supported tactically by his father will have to cross a threatening and unknown territory to recover an emergency signaling device (which is the only hope for the two protagonists to be traced and saved) that is located in the tail of the spaceship, broken into two trunks during the crash. Immediately after Kitai's departure, his father begins remotely combing the tail crash area, looking for the dangerous Bear they were transporting.
Kitai after a few days of walking and after overcoming numerous peripherals finally arrives at the remains of the tail of the spacecraft, about 100 km away from the head section. He is then able to retrieve the signalling device which turns out to be intact but not technically operational in that area. It is therefore necessary for Kitai to climb a mountain in order to reach a station from which the signal can start.
During the climb, however, he must overcome the last obstacle: the attack of the "Ursa" that had survived the crash, also managing to free himself from the cage in which he was imprisoned. After an initial moment of difficulty Kitai manages to spectral and kill the Ursa, finally starting the intergalactic distress signal. The father is rescued and the two, after embracing, confide in each other that they want to work with the mother.
story_text_b:
Remi is a dedicated elementary school teacher in the South Bronx, New York. It's hard for her to find a husband. One reason for this is their great interest in insects. A few years ago, Remi was involved in the breeding of a new species of insect, a genetically modified cross between termites and goddess-worshippers, called the Judas breed. They're supposed to help with the cockroach plague. This breeding had the property of greatly altering their appearance and even imitating humans, which was to the detriment of humans themselves. At the time, they thought they had killed all the insects.
But at least one specimen has survived and evolved. This specimen can imitate human faces in a deceptively real way, and it's after Remi. However, it does not want to kill the teacher, but to mate with her. That's why it doesn't tolerate other men around Remi and kills her dates.
At Remi's school, they come into contact with the giant insect. Remi tries to escape from the school with two of her students and a policeman and at the same time admirers. After a nerve-racking escape across the school, Remi and the two children are able to leave the now completely converted and quarantined building.
Through the gift of adapting his appearance to other creatures, the monster, who disguises himself as Remis lover, the policeman, also escapes from the school. Later, Remi again faces the insect that perfected his adaptability in her apartment. With a trick, she outwits the monster and kills the last of his kind.

story_text_a: In a small, remote town on the American plains, two FBI agents investigate a series of murders by placing the three witnesses - a neurotic cop, a junkie, and a child - in different rooms of the police station. The three of them each give them a different version of the facts, concealing the truth.
story_text_b:
Dr. Richard H. Thorndyke (Mel Brooks), the famous Nobel Prize winner in psychiatry, is appointed director of a Los Angeles mental asylum whose director has mysteriously died. The prominent psychiatrist gradually discovers patients and doctors who seem to be hiding something from him.
Victim of a conspiracy at a convention in San Francisco, Thorndyke will have to deal with his acute anxiety attacks for
to prove his innocence.

story_text_a:
Jill Cheyne espère devenir danseuse au Pleasure Garden. Mais arrivée à Londres, elle s’aperçoit qu'elle a perdu sa lettre de recommandation. Heureusement, Patsy Brand, une danseuse du cabaret, lui offre l'hospitalité pour la nuit.
Le lendemain, Jill qui n’a pas renoncé à son projet, rencontre le patron du Garden et obtient un engagement.
Hugh, le fiancé de Jill, assiste à son triomphe avant de quitter l’Angleterre pour les tropiques. Mais qu’importe, Jill a obtenu ce qu'elle cherchait : la gloire, la vie facile et des admirateurs argentés…
Pendant ce temps, Patsy épouse Levet, un ami de Hugh avant de partir en voyage de noces au lac de Côme.
Pour Patsy, le bonheur semble à portée de main, mais il n'en est rien… et Levet s'envole, lui aussi pour les tropiques… où l'attend une femme… femme qu'il noiera dans une crise de folie avant d'essayer de tuer Patsy, qui, le sachant souffrant, était venue le rejoindre.
story_text_b:
The film tells the story of two couples and how their lives intertwine in different ways. Patsy is a chorus girl who dances at a London variety theatre called The Garden of Delight. One day a country girl named Jill arrives at the theater wanting to make a name for herself as a dancer. Thanks to Patsy, who gives her sanctuary, she'll manage to become a prima ballerina. On the other hand, Jill's boyfriend, Hugh, and a friend of hers, Levett, must leave for the colonies in the Tropics and will be away for two years. Hugh asks Jill to wait for him and she says she will.
Hugh leaves, but Levett stays for another month, during which time he begins a romantic relationship with Patsy and marries her. During that month, Jill begins to lead a life of luxury and flirtation, completely forgetting Hugh and despising even Patsy forgetting what he did for her. Levett finally leaves for the Tropics, to the same fate as Hugh. There he has an affair with an Indian woman. Sometime later, Patsy receives a letter from the colonies, saying that her husband has contracted a fever and is lying down.
Patsy decides to travel to the Tropics and reunite with her husband to care for her. She borrows money from Jill, but she kicks her out of her fancy mansion. She won't even give him Hugh's engagement ring, as she's planning her wedding to a so-called prince. It'll be Patsy's landlords who get her the money for the trip. Once there, she discovers Levett's infidelity and decides to leave him. The man will end up murdering his lover by drowning her in the sea.
At a neighboring cabin, Patsy finds Hugh, also in bed, and decides to care for him until his recovery. Levett, driven mad by fever, jealousy and remorse, will see visions of his lover's ghost, who orders him to murder Patsy, something he will attempt sword in hand...

story_text_a:
In the small village of Ambricourt, the new parish priest keeps a diary, which he can be seen writing in and heard reading from throughout the film. Due to an undiagnosed stomach ailment, he has excluded meat and vegetables from his diet and primarily subsists on cheap wine with sugar and bread added. The locals are mostly either indifferent or hostile to the young priest, whether it be an old man who complains about the fees to bury his wife or the students of the catechism class who play tricks, so, as this is his first appointment, he often consults with the older and more experienced Priest of Torcy, who says he needs to worry about keeping order, rather than being loved.
The only parishioner who attends daily mass is Miss Louise, the young governess at the local manor, who is secretly having an affair with the Count. She complains that her ward, Chantal, mistreats her, so the priest says he will go talk to the Count, who he has been looking for an excuse to see about getting help starting a youth club and sports program. The Count initially approves of the priest's plans, but cools when the priest attempts to broach the subject of the conflict between Chantal and Louise.
When the priest revisits the manor, the Count avoids him, so he is greeted by the Countess, who withdrew from the world when Chantal's younger brother died several years ago, but he soon begins to feel ill and leaves. He goes to see Dr. Delbende, an elderly physician with a struggling practice who, though an atheist, is friends with and was recommended by the Priest of Torcy. The doctor palpates the priest's abdomen at length, but offers no diagnosis.
The priest finds it difficult to pray, even when he is able to find the time to try. One day, he receives an anonymous letter in Louise's handwriting telling him to ask to be transferred to another parish. He becomes convinced that God has abandoned him, and is particularly affected by the death of Dr. Delbende, which is rumored to be a suicide, but decides he has not lost his faith.
Chantal tells the priest that the Count and Louise plan to send her away and the Countess is not trying to stop them. The priest worries Chantal may be suicidal and, on a hunch, asks her to hand over her suicide note, which she produces from her pocket. Concerned, he goes to see the Countess, and, overheard by Chantal, they have a contentious theological conversation, by the end of which the Countess has come to terms with the death of her son and reconciled with God. She dies that night of a heart condition, and Louise leaves the manor shortly thereafter. Chantal lies and says the priest spoke harshly to the Countess and tormented her to death. The Canon (who is the Count's uncle), the Count, and the Priest of Torcy all question the priest's conduct, but he only weakly defends himself and does not mention the letter of thanks the Countess sent him before she died, choosing to let his actions speak for themselves.
After the priest passes out one night and begins to intermittently hemorrhage blood, he decides to go to the city of Lille to see a doctor. Chantal visits him when he is packing and says the whole town thinks he is a drunk and her father is sure to have him transferred, but he maintains his composure.
In Lille, the doctor diagnoses the priest with stomach cancer. He visits Dufrety, a classmate from seminary who took a leave from the ministry after becoming sick and now works selling drugstore supplies and lives with a woman out of wedlock. The priest faints and ends up staying with Dufrety until he dies. Dufrety relates in a letter to the Priest of Torcy that the Priest of Ambricourt asked him for absolution shortly before dying and he complied, though not without communicating that he was not sure if it was appropriate. The priest's response to this were his last words: "What does it matter? All is Grace."
story_text_b: A young priest (Claude Laydu), barely out of the seminary, arrives in Ambricourt (Pas-de-Calais), his new parish, but is not welcome. He begins his ministry by disregarding earthly and material needs, showing a tendency to mysticism, and neglecting health. He suffers from stomach aches, an inheritance from his family of alcoholics that leads him to feed only on sugar, bread and bad wine, the only foods he tolerates. He keeps an intimate diary in which he records the difficulties he encounters in gaining acceptance from his parishioners in the Artois countryside. The girls in the catechism class laugh at him and make fun of him. His colleagues criticize his bread-and-wine diet and ascetic life. He entrusts his problems to another priest of strong personality, the abbot of Torcy (Armand Guibert), who sends him to Dr. Delbende (Antoine Balpêtré) and advises him to proceed with prudence to win the confidence of the parishioners. Shortly after, Dr. Delbende dies in what appears to be a suicide. The young priest does not follow the abbot's advice and clashes with the Count (Jean Riveyre), who he knows is the lover of the governess (Nicole Maurey) of his daughter Chantal (Nicole Ladmiral), a teenager who hates her mother (Rachel Berendt), a troubled woman who lost her faith because of the death of her infant son. Concerned for Chantal, the priest visits the countess at the family castle, and is adamant in getting her back to religion until he succeeds, but she dies of a heart attack the following night. Chantal spreads false rumors that the priest's bitter words had led to her mother's death. Previously, Chantal had revealed her hatred for her parents to the priest. As a result of this situation, and convinced that he has failed in his mission, the priest suffers a great crisis of faith. When his health deteriorates, he goes to Lille to consult a doctor and learns that he suffers from stomach cancer. At the home of Dufrety (Bernard Hubrenne), a fellow seminarian and secularized priest who lives with a woman, he dies stating that "Everything is grace".[1]

story_text_a: David Lewis has been so affected by the death of his wife Gillian, who drowned two years ago, that he spends most of his time on the beach in Nantucket communicating with Gillian's spirit and neglecting his daughter Rachel. David has invited his sister-in-law Esther and her husband for the weekend. The couple comes with a friend, hoping that David will take an interest in her while Rachel invites her girlfriend.
story_text_b:
# Theatrical release
Michael and Jenna seem like the perfect couple: they've been together for three years, and now that Jenna's pregnant, they're planning to move into a house of their own. Furthermore, Jenna's parents would like very much for the two of them to get married. When asked, however, Michael puts forward his enormous workload and Jenna's dissertation as reasons why the wedding would have to be postponed for a while. In reality, however, he has fallen into a mental crisis because he believes that he can see the rest of his life ahead of him: boring, tedious, and without any surprises.
At a friend's wedding, Michael meets the younger Kim, to whom he confides his doubts. Believing that he is about to break up with his girlfriend, she begins flirting with him. Although he is fascinated by her, he does not succumb to temptation. Kim leaves the wedding a little later, but not without telling him where she goes to college and usually spends her free time.
Some time later, Michael actually visits her and pretends to have been in the area "by chance". Kim notices his interest in her and invites him to a party. Michael accepts this invitation and asks his office colleague and friend Chris to lie for him so that Jenna does not find out about the date  without telling him the real reason for this request. Chris immediately suspects a woman is behind it and asks Michael not to be dragged into the matter. However, Michael denies that another woman is involved, and pretends to want to meet up with an old college friend, which Chris still doesn't believe.
After the party, Michael and Kim kiss. She then invites him to spend the night with her if her roommate is absent for the night. Michael, plagued by remorse at the prospect of being sidelined, declines the offer. At the same time, Izzy's father, a friend of Michael and Jenna, dies. Several friends and acquaintances visit Izzy's home to offer support and comfort to the family in this situation. This is where Jenna meets Chris, who is unable to convincingly convey the lie Michael requested. With Michael's phone off all night, Chris can't warn him that Jenna's on to him. When he finally gets home and Jenna asks him where he's been, the first thing he says is that he spent the night with Chris. It's only now that he learns that Izzy's father has passed away, so Jenna has already met Chris at Izzy's and the lie has been exposed. Now he is forced to come forward with the truth, assuring her that the meeting meant nothing and that he did not sleep with Kim, but merely kissed her. Angry Jenna kicks him out of the house anyway.
When Michael is alone, he gets a call from Kim asking him if he wants to come over again just to talk a little bit. Michael finally agrees, drives to her house, and shortly after, the two sleep together. The next morning, Michael tries to sneak away, but leaves his keys behind. When he returns, Kim is already awake and asks him why he didn't say goodbye. He tells her that he didn't want to wake her because he has to go to work early and leaves the apartment.
At the office, Michael decides to take some time off and visit Jenna. At this moment, Kim surprisingly bursts through the door to give him a self-composed CD. Michael confesses to her that he is still in love with Jenna, who is also pregnant with his child. He apologizes to Kim for not telling her about it and leaves the office building.
Michael goes to Jenna's parents, where her father Stephen has a long talk with him. He urges Michael to always be honest with Jenna and explains to him what love really means. Then Michael goes to Jenna's room to talk to her. After the alleged reconciliation, he finally confesses to her that he was still at Kim's house on the night of the argument and had slept with her there. Jenna can't believe what she's hearing and runs away from her parents' house. She gets in her car and drives back to their apartment. Michael chases after her, and since she refuses to talk to him, he intends to wait outside the door until she changes her mind. He has no choice but to stay put for days as Jenna sticks to her guns. One evening, however, she begins to talk to him through the closed door. She says the end of a partnership is like the death of a person, finally opens the door and lets Michael back in.
# Alternate ending (only on DVD)
After Jenna opens the door, the film jumps a few years into the future. Off the record, Michael talks about his ongoing relationship with Jenna and how small decisions can have dramatic consequences. In the final scene, Jenna jogs while another man follows her. However, she smiles at him briefly and continues to run at high speed.

story_text_a: Around the 1920s. When the people of the small coastal town of Littlehampton receive scandalous and obscene letters, suspicion immediately falls on the fiery Rose Gooding, who could lose custody of her daughter. A group of women set out to solve the mystery.
story_text_b:
Louden Swain is a wrestler at Thompson High School who has just turned 18 years old. He has decided that he needs to do something truly meaningful in his life. He embarks on a mission or, in a Native American term, a vision quest. His goal is to drop two weight classes to challenge the area's toughest opponent, Brian Shute, a menacing three-time state champion from nearby rival Hoover High School, who has never been defeated in his high school career. In his zeal to drop from 190 pounds (86 kilograms) to 168 pounds (76 kg), against the wishes of his coach and teammates, he disrupts the team around him and creates health problems of his own.
Meanwhile, his father has taken on a boarder named Carla from Trenton, New Jersey, passing through on her way to San Francisco. Louden falls in love with her and begins to lose sight of his goals as a wrestler. Worse, his drastic weight loss culminates in an unhealthy situation, where he gets frequent nosebleeds which, Louden assumes, is due to a lack of iron in his diet (and results in him having to forfeit a match he was winning). The two finally admit their love for each other, but Carla realizes she is distracting him from his goals.
Carla decides to move out and continue on to San Francisco, but not before seeing Louden's big match, in which he makes a comeback from losing and pins Shute in the final seconds with a hip throw. As Louden celebrates his victory, he monologues to the audience, "...I guess that's why we got to love those people who deserve it like there's no tomorrow. 'Cause when you get right down to it—there isn't."

story_text_a:
Under the watchful eye of Father Silvano Bentivoglio (Carmen Argenziano) and Dr. Vittoria Vetra (Ayelet Zurer), the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN) starts the Large Hadron Collider and creates three jars of antimatter particles, larger than those produced before. Almost immediately, Dr. Vetra goes to check the vials when she finds Father Silvano's eyeball, who was murdered for opening the security door with his eye, and one of the antimatter vials is stolen. At the same time, the Catholic Church is mourning the sudden death of Pope Pius XVI in Rome and preparing for the papal conclave to elect the next pope. The camerlengo, Father Patrick McKenna (Ewan McGregor), assumes temporary control of the Holy See and before the conclave goes into seclusion, four of the preferiti (the cardinals favored to be elected pope) are kidnapped by a man claiming to represent the Illuminati. In a video message, he threatens to kill one candidate every hour from 8 p.m. and destroy the entire Vatican City at midnight, using the missing vial of antimatter as a bomb. The Holy See summons symbologist Robert Langdon (Tom Hanks) from Harvard University and Vetra to help them save the four preferiti and locate the jar.
Langdon hears the message from the Illuminati and deduces that the four cardinals will die on the four altars of the "Path of Enlightenment", marked by statues of angels in places relevant to the four classical elements. Over the objections of Major Maximilian Richter (Stellan Skarsgård), head of the Swiss Guard, but with the consent of McKenna, Langdon gains access to the Vatican Secret Archive. Once there, take a few moments to examine Galileo Galilei's forbidden book with Vetra. Following the tracks and accompanied by Inspector General Ernesto Olivetti (Pierfrancesco Favino) and Claudio Vincenzi (David Pasquesi) of the Vatican City Gendarmerie Corps, they arrive at the Chigi Chapel, in the church of Santa Maria del Popolo. There they find Cardinal Ebner (Curt Lowens) dead, suffocated with dirt and marked with an ambigram of the word "earth". They verify that the second location is the busy St. Peter's Square and arrive just as Cardinal Lamassé (Franklin Amobi), bloodied, appears among the crowd with his chest marked with "air". Vetra attempts, unsuccessfully, to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation, only to discover that his lungs have been punctured, while the killer (Nikolaj Lie Kaas) escapes into the crowd.
Vetra studies Silvano's diaries and at the same time, Langdon, Olivetti and Vincenzi locate the third church, Santa Maria della Vittoria, and arrive to see Cardinal Guidera (Bob Yerkes) branded "fire" and suspended over a pile of burning wood. A shootout ensues between the assassin and the officers, with Olivetti and Vincenzi dying in the process, other than Cardinal Guidera who is pierced by a stray bullet. Langdon manages to escape, but not before being discovered by the killer. Langdon convinces two carabinieri officers to take him to the next location and the trio hurry off to the altar of "water", the Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi, just as the killer arrives in a van. The murderer kills the officers and drops Cardinal Baggia (Marco Fiorini) tied to an iron structure into the fountain to drown himself, before saying goodbye to Langdon and leaving. With the help of passersby, Langdon rescues the Cardinal, who tells him that the lair of the Illuminati is the Castle of Sant'Angelo. There, Langdon and Vetra discover a hidden passageway leading to the Vatican, which is used by the assassin as a hideout. There they discover a chest with five iron marks, and they realize that the fifth mark (the Holy See's emblem) is for the Pope (the chamberlain), but they confront the murderer before they can alert McKenna. The killer spares their lives once again, stating that killing them is not part of his mission, unless they come after him. He then cryptically warns them to be careful, as their contractors are "men of God" before they leave. He escapes a car left for him by his employer, but is killed instantly when it explodes on ignition.
Langdon and Vetra hurry back to the Vatican, where they find Major Richter threatening McKenna with a gun and McKenna with the Holy See's emblem branded on his chest with a burning iron. Richter and Archbishop Simeon (Cosimo Fusco) are shot by the guards. When Richter dies in front of Langdon, he opens his hand to reveal a key that Langdon takes. The antimatter jar is found in St. Peter's tomb, underneath the church, but the battery life is too low to risk reconnecting it to a battery. McKenna, being an ex-pilot of the Aeronáutica Militare, takes the vial and uses a helicopter located in St. Peter's Square to fly over the Vatican. At high altitude, he parachutes out when the antimatter bomb explodes high above. McKenna is hailed as a hero and savior, and the cardinals proclaim a motion to elect him pope, despite the reluctance of Cardinal Strauss (Armin Mueller-Stahl), the grand elector of the conclave. Langdon and Vetra use Richter's key to watch a security video that shows McKenna talking to Richter before the attack. The video reveals that it was McKenna himself who masterminded the entire conspiracy. It is also revealed that it was he who murdered the Pope (his own adoptive father) with an overdose of tinzaparin, a drug that was supplied to him due to a thrombophlebitis, because he felt that he had betrayed the Church by trying to close the gap between science and religion by accepting a meeting with Silvanus to embrace the idea of the existence of the "Particle of God" (the antimatter). After McKenna had killed the Pope, he intended to elect himself to the papacy while rallying the more conservative cardinals to his side, using the return of the Illuminati to make them believe that they were at war and that he would be the warrior who could lead them. The recording is shown to the papal conclave and McKenna finally realizes he's been exposed. He flees to the remote recess of St. Peter's tomb in the building, where he commits suicide by self-immolation before the Swiss Guard apprehends him.
The Holy See officially announces that McKenna died due to internal injuries sustained during the parachute landing (even calling for his canonization), and Cardinal Baggia (the only surviving preferiti) is named as Pope Luke I, with Cardinal Strauss as his new chamberlain. Strauss thanks Langdon for his help and gives the Galileo book to Langdon for his research as a gift from himself and Pope Luke, requesting that Langdon's will be returned to the Vatican, and any future references he may make to the Catholic Church in his future publications be made delicately, to which Langdon responds, "I will try". When the film ends, Lucas I shares a grateful nod with Langdon and Vetra, and goes out on the balcony to greet the crowd waiting for him in St. Peter's Square.
story_text_b:
The unnamed narrator of the story goes into the middle of the Arabian Peninsula to seek out and enter a lost city. After hearing a clanging seemingly coming from deep inside the earth, the narrator inspects mysterious carvings and ruins until nightfall. The next day, the narrator discovers a cliff riddled with low-ceilinged buildings, unfit for human use. While he attends to his suddenly nervous camel, the narrator discovers a somewhat larger temple, with altars, painted murals, and a small staircase going down. After he descends, his torch dies, and he crawls on his hands and knees until he enters a hallway with small wooden coffins containing bizarre reptiles inside of them lining the walls.
The narrator notices a large amount of light coming from an unknown source. After crawling to it on his hands and knees, he sees a large brass door with a descent into a misty portal. He then hears moaning coming from the coffin passage, and feels a strong wind coming from the passage, trying to pull him down. Against all odds, he resists, and sees what appear to be reptiles with a body shaped like a cross between a crocodile and a seal with a strange head common to neither of them, involving a protruding forehead, horns, lack of a nose, and an alligator-like jaw crawling behind the lit portal. The wind dies down after the last of it flows down into the light, when suddenly the door closes behind the narrator, leaving him in the dark.

story_text_a: Mary, the wife of a British consul Ralph Sinclair, is detained by Chinese General Hai Lung. He offers to spare her husband from execution if she will become his lover.
story_text_b:
Noah Praetorius is a brilliant gynecologist who teaches at a medical school and runs a private clinic, where he emphasizes human relationships with his patients.
One of them, Deborah Higgins, is a distressed young single mother-to-be, with whom he falls in love (and vice versa). Not only does he marry her, but he takes in her stepfather, Arthur Higgins, a loser who lives in squalor alongside his brother John, a domineering maniac.
Dr. Praetorius is liked by all of his colleagues (including his friend Professor Barker, a physicist and double bass player) and all of his students, except for Professor Ellwell, who is jealous of him and opens an internal investigation aimed at shedding light on the doctor's troubled past and the mystery surrounding the constant presence at his side of the so-called Shunderson. There is evidence that Praetorius once practiced medicine in the back of a butcher shop in a remote province, and that his earnings later enabled him to specialize, and to buy a clinic...

story_text_a: En algún lugar del tiempo, las garras del Infierno se extienden ominosas sobre el castillo de Hrothgar y sus habitantes. Un ejército de fanáticos religiosos ha sitiado el lugar para contener el mal, y nadie puede salir de allí con vida. Pero un misterioso guerrero, Beowulf (Christopher Lambert), llega para ofrecer su ayuda al rey Hrothgar (Oliver Cotton). Con cierto recelo, el rey le pide que cace a la sanguinaria criatura que cada noche atormenta a sus hombres: Grendel (Vincent Hammond).
story_text_b:
One of the first shots shows an industrial-looking castle defending the border of an unnamed kingdom. This castle is haunted by a monster called Grendel. At first, it kills a different inhabitant every night who lives within its walls. Later, when the hero Beowulf, fighting through a siege ring, reaches the castle, the monster kills more erratically and eventually during the day.
The troops besieging the castle believe that evil from the castle is spreading to the countryside, and they're there to prevent that from happening. Beowulf makes the breakthrough and is welcomed by Hrothgar, who rules the castle, as a welcome additional fighter (Hrothgar's quote: "It's not safe with us", Beowulf's quote: "I'll take the risk".). Nevertheless, Beowulf is viewed with a healthy suspicion.
As Beowulf rides into the castle, he is inspected by, among others, the soldier Roland and the king's daughter Kyra. Roland loves these, but Kyra develops a noticeable interest in Beowulf over the course of the film.
In flashbacks, it is shown that the former queen committed suicide and King Hrothgar had an affair with an unknown, young and very attractive woman. This is actually an ancient creature that originally lived on the land where the castle now stands. With her Hrothgar has a descendant, Grendel.
Beowulf and Grendel fight each other, with both being injured, but recovering from those injuries.
Later, Beowulf and Grendel fight again. In the process, the hero manages to sever an arm from the monster, which he presents to the other combatants as a trophy. Then everyone celebrates, believing that Grendel is defeated; in addition, the arm is hung high on a rope in the castle courtyard, whereupon the besiegers of the castle believe that the monster is dead, and leave. Kyra enters Beowulf's room and "rewards" him for his deed. She confesses to him that she killed her ex-husband when he repeatedly intruded under the influence of alcohol. Beowulf tells her that his father is Baal (the god of darkness, the lord of lies), which explains his enormous powers as well as his ability to regenerate quickly.
While Kyra stays with Beowulf, all the other inhabitants of the castle are killed by Grendel's mother (and possibly by Grendel as well). Beowulf first kills Grendel with a sword and then his mother with a torch after she is transformed into a monstrous monster (which may represent the pure form of the ancient being).
Kyra and Beowulf escape the exploding castle and are the only two survivors. In the end, Kyra wants to stay with Beowulf, but Beowulf warns Kyra that "it's not safe with him". To which she replies, "That's a risk I'm willing to take".

story_text_a:
Paul McCartney part à la recherche des bandes de son dernier album qui lui ont été volées. Il a vingt-quatre heures pour les retrouver et empêcher sa maison de disques de faire faillite. Les bandes sont retrouvées; le voleur, qui s'est mis dans une situation compromettante et Paul se retrouvent et éclatent de rire. L'enquête est l'occasion de voir le musicien répéter avec son groupe.
L'argument est inspiré d'un fait réel survenu en 1973, alors que McCartney enregistrait l'album Band On The Run à Lagos (Nigéria) : son épouse et lui ont été agressés dans la rue, se voyant dérober les bandes magnétiques contenant les démos de l'album.
Broad Street se réfère à la gare de Broad Street à Londres, qui est filmée vers la fin.
story_text_b:
Paul è bloccato in un ingorgo nella sua auto con autista mentre si reca a una riunione di lavoro. Nel traffico, immagina di stare guidando in campagna a bordo di una macchina vistosa piena zeppa di tecnologia moderna quando riceve una chiamata da parte di Steve che lo informa di come Harry, un ex criminale "redento", è sparito insieme ai nastri master del suo ultimo album che avrebbero dovuto essere consegnati alla casa discografica il giorno precedente. Paul corre in studio solo per scoprire che la polizia è già lì a indagare sul furto, sospettando che Harry sia tornato alle sue vecchie abitudini criminali e progetti di ricavare un bootleg dai nastri. Le cose peggiorano quando Mr. Rath, a cui lo studio deve denaro, arriva con la notizia che prenderà il controllo della compagnia discografica se i nastri non vengono ritrovati entro mezzanotte.
Dopo l'incontro, il film prosegue nel descrivere un'ordinaria giornata lavorativa di Paul con la moglie Linda e l'amico Ringo Starr, che include le riprese di due video, le prove in un loft e la registrazione di spettacoli per la radio. In mezzo a questo, Paul si chiede cosa potrebbe aver fatto Harry: ha venduto i nastri master per ricavarne denaro, è scappato o è stato ucciso? Durante diverse canzoni, Paul elabora varie fantasie in varie ambientazioni e costumi ispirati alla sua situazione. Quando la giornata volge al termine, Paul esce in giro per Londra mentre i suoi soci si preparano per il cambio di proprietà della compagnia a mezzanotte.
Guidando verso il quartiere di Broad Street, Paul si ricorda che Harry era diretto lì quando l'aveva visto l'ultima volta, e va ad esplorare la stazione. Alla fine, trova la custodia blu contenente i nastri su una panchina della stazione, e Harry in un piccolo edificio di manutenzione nelle vicinanze, dove si è accidentalmente intrappolato mentre cercava un bagno. Ridono entrambi, e mentre scappano, Paul informa Linda, la quale avvisa, appena in tempo, lo studio che i nastri sono stati trovati e l'acquisizione è quindi stata evitata. L'auto di Paul arriva finalmente a destinazione e lui si sveglia dal suo sogno.

story_text_a: Lauri loses his job as a tram driver and the restaurant where his wife Ilona works, Dubrovnik, is bought by a restaurant chain. The film then follows the journey of the couple to support themselves. Each will try to find work in his branch; but Lauri's age will prevent him from finding work in transport, and the catering crisis forces Ilona to work in a small restaurant that is shabby, underpaid and not even declared to the tax authorities. She gets fired after a tax audit. She then meets the former doorman of Dubrovnik, who has become a shoemaker, and they try to get a loan to open a new restaurant, which they are denied. She then meets the former owner of the Dubrovnik, reapplies with the owner as a guarantor, and this time the loan is granted. With the help of her husband and the entire former Dubrovnik team, they opened a new restaurant: the Travail (Työ in Finnish).
story_text_b:
In Hamburg in 1938, Peter Müller and Thomas Berger join their friends Arvid and Otto at a swing club called the Bismarck. They have a good time, dancing and enjoying the music.
Peter goes home to find his mother in an argument with the Nazi Blockleiter (block leader). Herr Knopp, head of the local Gestapo, arrives and curtly dismisses the Blockleiter.  Herr Knopp begins asking Frau Müller questions about some of her late husband's friends. Herr Müller had been accused of being a communist, and his health was irreparably damaged by an interrogation at the hands of Nazi agents.
At Arvid's house, Thomas accidentally ruins one of Arvid's prized records. Upset, Arvid kicks Thomas, Peter and Otto out. To apologize to Arvid, Peter and Thomas steal a radio (which Peter knows was stolen from a ransacked Jewish home) from a bakery. Thomas escapes, but Peter is caught. Herr Knopp, who is attracted to Peter's mother, intercedes for him; in return, Peter must enroll in the Hitlerjugend (Hitler Youth). Thomas also joins, telling Peter that they will be able to enjoy both the privileges of Hitler Youth membership and the pleasures of being Swing Kids.
Arvid is confronted on the street by a group of Hitler Youth, including former friend and fellow Swing Kid Emil. They beat him and break his hand, threatening his work as a jazz musician.
Peter, who has a job delivering books, is asked to spy on his boss, whom the Nazis suspect is working against the Reich. In HJ school, the boys are encouraged to spy on their friends and families. Thomas accuses his father of insulting Hitler, hoping to cause trouble for him, but is unnerved when the Nazis come to his home and take his father away. His subsequent attempts to resume his friendship with Peter and persuade him to collaborate with the Nazis are tinged with fear.
Arvid overcomes his injury and is able to play music again. However, while working at a jazz club, he refuses to play a German song, lashing out at the club's patrons for being blind to the Nazi agenda. Peter is sympathetic but Thomas loudly argues the Nazi side. Peter angrily proclaims Thomas to be a "fucking Nazi" and storms off. Blacklisted from playing in clubs, Arvid realizes there is nothing for him in Germany and dies by suicide.
As Thomas begins to believe fully in Nazi ideology, Peter feels as though there is no hope for him. Peter, disenchanted with how his life is coming apart, dresses up and goes to a swing club which is scheduled to be raided by members of the Hitlerjugend. As Thomas begins assaulting the club's patrons he attacks Peter; however, during the fight Peter is able to reach Thomas. Thomas begs Peter to run away but Peter won't. Willie Müller is there and as Peter is driven away by the police, he loudly screams "Swing Heil!" over and over again, proud that his brother stood up for being a swing kid.

story_text_a: Ray Burke est agent de joueurs de NBA, la ligue américaine de basket-ball. En plein lock-out, il tente de convaincre l'un de ses clients, dont c’est la première saison professionnelle, d’accepter une opportunité commerciale controversée.
story_text_b:
Ray Burke works for a New York sports agency that's in the middle of a lockdown. After his credit card is declined at a restaurant, his boss David Starr tells him that the company is losing customers, and that he may be fired along with other employees. This forces Ray to come up with a plan to save the company from foreclosure and give his client, Erick Scott, new opportunities. He recruits SAM, his former assistant, to help him.
The next day, Ray visits Emera, Jamero Umber's newly enlisted mother, with an offer. She refuses, insisting that she's the only agent and lawyer her son will ever need. Ray's ex-wife, Myra, tells him that the company is closed and he will have to renegotiate terms with agents and players. However, they will have to wait more than a month to settle down, as the team's owners are at an impasse with the TV networks for millions of dollars. Ray asks her to cancel the deal, convinced that the players won't be paid well during the lockout, which could last up to six months. Meanwhile, future teammates Erick Scott and Jamero Umber have a widely publicized Twitter feud.
Ray goes to Back Court Day, an annual event at a community center with a basketball court where he meets local kids and famous athletes. While Erick is signing autographs and answering questions, Jamero arrives with his mother in tow. Erick and Jamero confront each other over their Twitter discussion; tensions rise as they exchange insults. They end up playing a one-on-one basketball game, which is recorded by the kids on their phones. A video is posted on social media and goes viral, garnering millions of views. Ray has the idea of replaying the matches on streaming services and social media sites such as Snapchat, YouTube and Netflix, thus allowing players to make money during the lockdown. Erick's not convinced, but he accepts.
The next day Sam meets Ray to discuss their future careers. Sam tells Ray that Erick might fire him. Erick fires Ray for lying to him that it was all about the money. However, Ray's plan succeeds and the players who signed with the company remain under contract, meaning that Erick has never been in danger and will be able to play in the league once the lockout is over. Ray reveals to Starr that the entire plan to get players on pay-per-view and streaming platforms was a ploy to force an end to the blockade. Sam then goes to work for the players' association, while she and Erick start a relationship.

story_text_a:
The story is set in the Bosnian War, and is considered by many of Theo's fans to be his best film.
A Greek filmmaker returns to his hometown to embark on a journey in search of three undisclosed reels that contain the innocent look of the pioneers of Greek cinema, the first look. It is a journey to the origins of cinema. During the journey Theo poetically portrays old Europe, freezing it with concrete symbols of its present dismemberment. Specific references to Homer's Odyssey appear in the film.[2] For example, in the film a voice asks who is it? and from the ship in which a statue of Lenin travels, they answer "nobody". In song IX of Odyssey 364 we can read "Cyclops! You ask what my illustrious name is and I'll tell you but give me the gift of hospitality you promised me. My name is Nobody; and Nobody calls me my mother, my father and my companions all".[3] or by Theo Angelopoulos, arrives in his hometown after having spent time in exile. His latest film is projected onto the facades of buildings and that has divided the city. But that city is not the Ithaca Angelopoulos is looking for. In this tale, Ithaca is represented by three reels of yet-to-be-revealed negative that the protagonist will search for throughout the film's footage. Giving birth to that first glimpse of Greek cinema is the goal of the protagonist; but, as in Homer's Odyssey, even more important than reaching Ithaca (revealing the three reels) is the journey that entails. Angelopoulos seeks that first glimpse into the territories of ancient Greece, showing the dismemberment and conflicts of Eastern Europe throughout the 1990s.
In this free reconstruction of the Odyssey, we must pay attention to the role played by women. In Angelopoulos' film, Penelope, Circe, Calypso and Nausicaa are portrayed by the same actress (Maïa Morgenstein). Another very clear reference to Homer's epic poem is the use of fog. Homer uses the fog so that when he reaches Ithaca, Ulysses cannot recognize the city where he was born. In The Look of Ulysses, the fog also appears just before the chemists reveal the negative of all three reels.
Another visible reference in the film is to James Joyce's Ulysses.
story_text_b:
In her teens, Emily Dickinson befriends Susan Gilbert during a recitation of the Amherst's Shakespeare Society, and during a scene in which they play lovers, a romance blossoms. On a stroll afterward, they kiss. Emily's family leaves for a month long trip, and Susan stays with Emily for the duration. They continue to spend time together, concealing their romantic relationship from others.
Susan gets a teaching job out west, and they write countless love letters to each other's while she is away. When she returns, Emily is surprised to learn that Susan has been betrothed to Emily's brother Austin, which Susan had kept secret from her. Susan apologizes to Emily and explains that it's all part of a greater scheme: Susan cannot financially support herself without getting married, and by marrying Austin they can build a house right next door to Emily and no one will suspect their romance.
Twenty years later, Emily and Susan live next door to each other, and Susan's children deliver their countless notes back and forth between the two houses. Emily shows Susan the poems she has written, some of which are written on scraps of paper and in the margins of recipes, and many of which mention Susan by name. Emily also likes to garden and bake bread for the neighborhood children.
During a period when Susan is too busy to speak to Emily, a recently widowed Kate Scott Turner travels to stay with Susan. But Kate turns out to be more interested in Emily, and ends up staying at her place instead. Kate leaves suddenly, and Emily tells Susan she wishes she'd had a chance to say goodbye and give Kate the pair of garters she sewed for her. Susan is jealous because Emily never made garters for her.
Emily receives the company of Judge Otis Phillips Lords, an old man who confuses the Brontë sisters (describing the book “Wuthering Jane”), falls asleep mid conversation, and calls Emily "plain". While on his way out he stumbles, and as the same moment Emily reaches out to help him, Susan walks in, catching them mid-embrace.
Thomas Wentworth Higginson also visits Emily after she writes about publishing her poems. During their meeting he corrects her on what the meaning of poetry is, describes how women's writing is different than men's writing, and even copy-edits one of her poems right in front of her. He tells her the poems are not ready for publication.
Mabel Todd first comes to Emily's house on an invitation to play the piano for Emily, but is surprised when the maid tells her that she will play alone in the drawing room, and that Emily will remain upstairs to listen to the music while she writes. Mabel meets Austin after moving to Amherst, and they began an affair. They have little shame about it, and frequently appear in public together. They often go to Emily's house to have sex, which Emily avoids by staying in her room. Mabel suggests to Austin that they publish their love letters, but Austin finds that idea too scandalous and tells her to seek for a creative outlet elsewhere.
Emily suddenly becomes ill and passes away. Her sister Lavinia asks Susan to wash the body for burial. After her death, Mabel discovers a chest full of Emily's poems and letters, but she realizes that many of the best ones are addressed to Susan. She enlists the help of Austin to erase all the instances of "Susan" and replace them with men's names instead.
Years later after Emily's work has become successful, Mabel gives a talk to a large group of society women. She tells them that because Emily was such an eccentric recluse, she only saw her face once: in the casket of her funeral. She explains that her poems must have been directed to Judge Otis, and that she added titles to all the poems so that audiences would know exactly what they were about. Emily's niece also gives a lecture about how her aunt and mother were secret lovers, but only three people attend.
The film ends with titles explaining that recent technology has revealed Mabel's erasures and shown that the love letters were indeed written to Susan.

story_text_a:
The film opens with the assassination of Abraham Lincoln by John Wilkes Booth during a theatrical performance. Flashback, Kentucky, mid-19th century: The black, kind-hearted slave Tom, affectionately called "Uncle Tom" by all, lives with other blacks at the Shelby family in the South. One day old Mr. Shelby has to sell some of his protege out of financial need, because a certain Simon Legree demands payment of a change due. This brutal, unscrupulous, and business-minded slave-owner sees the serfs as nothing more than commodities - dumb niggers - that he can buy and resell at will. The disfigured Legree demands a total of ten of his slaves, including Uncle Tom, from the heavily indebted Shelby to settle the exchange. Also, Legree has fallen in love with the Shelby's attractive maid, Eliza. She's to become one of the ten new Legree slaves. Since the agreement stipulates that he can only choose male slaves, Legree decides to take her two-year-old son with the other nine, because he knows that Eliza would never let her son go alone. Since Eliza is married to Harris, another slave laboring on another plantation, Legree decides to buy him as well.
Young George Shelby is disgusted by Legree's bad character and lets him feel his rejection. The next day, when Legree wants to take his ten slaves with him, Eliza and her son are missing. Emilie Shelby, George's mother, set them free to spare the colored girl the torture of becoming Legree's sex slave. Eliza's husband Harris flees to Canada to earn money and eventually buy his wife and child's freedom. Eliza can also escape from the slave trader with her son. Enraged by the escape of his slave, Harry's owner whips his slave's sister, Cassy, into telling him where her brother is. But she won't say anything. Legree takes a liking to Cassy and buys her from her owner. Only she reluctantly becomes Legree's mistress and doesn't have to pick cotton on the plantation.
George Shelby has every intention of buying Uncle Tom back as soon as he has the means to do so. The slaves acquired by Legree make the long journey across the Mississippi River to his plantation. Part of the journey is done on the ship. That's where Tom meets little Evangeline, who everyone calls Eva. The seriously ill girl is very outgoing and friendly and quickly becomes Tom's friend. Eva convinces her father, the Southern gentleman St. Clare, to buy Uncle Tom. Mr. St. Clare loves his daughter dearly and will do anything to grant her every wish. Tom now has a new master who treats him much more decently and humanely than all his previous masters. Meanwhile, Cassy found her sister-in-law and her young son. She offers them refuge in Legree's house, hoping that her hated lover will not search there for the escaped slaves.
Mr. St. Clare's wife, Eva's mother, is also ill, and so her husband has now begun an affair with his cousin Harriet. When Eva learns of her father's affair, she is so sad that her health is deteriorating massively. Evangeline's dying wish is that her father set all his slaves free. He promises her and announces his release the day before Independence Day. Legree considers St. Clare's decision to be a humanitarian act of sentiment and fears that his example could set a precedent and ruin his business as a slave trader. Legree comes up with an insidious plan. From a room on the top floor of the saloon, he shoots St. Clare in the head as he passes by in the carriage on Independence Day. St. Clare dies in the presence of Uncle Tom. Legree succeeds in blaming the cowardly murder on a black boy who saw him leave the room and could have betrayed him. The innocent man is then publicly lynched by the mob.
St. Clare's slaves are auctioned off after his violent death at minimum prices. Legree steps in again and buys back his former minions - including Uncle Tom. Abraham Lincoln has now been elected President of the United States, and a civil war is in the air. Harris, now a free man in Canada, is trying to buy his sister's freedom from Legree. But he says Cassy's not for sale. Shortly after, Legree also sends her to the plantation to harvest cotton, believing that she is cheating on him. When he tries to get Cassy back, she spits in his face and walks away. Legree rushes his horses on them. Tom throws himself between the horses and the girl at the last moment to protect Cassy, and is badly injured in the process. Shortly thereafter, the slaves of Legree's estate flee. The traitor then tries to recruit white men to help him recapture his slaves. Cassy, Eliza and their son also intend to escape, but first they want to get Uncle Tom. But he begs the two women to let him die in peace. As a "farewell gift" to her unloved lover, Cassy Legree sets fire to a magnificent Southern estate.
All the escaped slaves gather near a church to escape the following evening by ship to the slave-free north. Harris finds his family again. George Shelby also shows up and asks for Tom to finally buy him back. When he hears that Tom is in the cabin on Legree's burning property, he rushes there. In a shootout between Legree and the other slave traders and the escaped slaves, Cassy is shot and dies in her brother's arms. A priest explains to Legree that his crops have been wiped out by the floodwaters of the locks that have been arbitrarily opened. Legree then tries to save what can be saved. He also sees his house in flames and Uncle Tom lying half dead in the barn. He accuses Tom of inciting the other black slaves to riot and wants to murder him. But then George Shelby shows up and offers to buy Uncle Tom off. Legree's only answer is, "Dead niggers don't count", and then he disappears. Tom is dying in George's arms. In the final scene, you see the colored people on their way to freedom. And as the chorus plays, there's a melancholy Southern anthem, "Old Old Mississippi", sung by Eartha Kitt.
story_text_b: The film opens with the meeting between writer Harriet Beecher Stowe and U.S. President Abraham Lincoln and the latter's assassination at Ford's Theatre. Later, the story is told of Uncle Tom, a black slave from Kentucky, who is sold by his master and finds himself facing the harsh life in the cotton fields of the South.

story_text_a: Peter Morgan est un jeune professeur de botanique dans un collège de province dirigé par son père. Lors d'une escapade à New York en compagnie de son cousin Keith, il rencontre une chanteuse de cabaret, Francey, dont il tombe fou amoureux et il l'épouse immédiatement. De retour chez lui, il préfère ménager ses parents, surtout son père très autoritaire, et diffère l'annonce de son mariage, présentant Francey comme une amie de Keith, d'autant plus que Peter a une fiancée « officielle », Helen...Tout va se liguer pour contrarier la nuit de noces de Peter et Francey.
story_text_b:
Peter Morgan is a shy teacher of botany at the traditional college in the small town of Old Sharon. This is led by his conservative father, who has firmly envisioned his son as his former successor. One day, Peter is sent to New York with orders to bring his lively cousin Keith back to the bosom of the family. He's enjoying his time in New York and has a crush on nightclub singer Francey Brent. But while Francey shows no interest in Keith, she and Peter fall head over heels in love. Together they walk the streets of New York for a night. The next morning, Peter is sure he's found the woman for life, and he marries her right away.
As the return to Old Sharon approaches, Peter does not dare to tell his family, as well as his actual fiancée Helen, of his marriage to Francey without warning. Francey therefore leaves the train first together with her live-in husband Keith, which causes her to sink in the family's esteem. The next day, Francey pretends to be a student. However, problems arise here too, as most of the students are attracted to Francie's appearance and her closeness to teacher Morgan seems strange. Peter makes several attempts to tell his parents and his fiancée about his marriage, but these are usually interrupted by other events.
When Peter finally tells his father about Francey, he looks down on the showgirl from the pedestal of intellectual superiority. He demands separation from his son, otherwise he would fire him from his teaching position. Mrs. Morgan, on the other hand, is happy and accepts Francey. Francey, under pressure from Mr. Morgan and annoyed by Peter's lack of assertiveness, eventually leaves town. Mrs. Morgan also joins her, outraged by her husband's behavior. Peters rebels against his father for the first time: he teaches in a drunken state with the aim of lowering the reputation of him and his family so that the marriage with Francey can be considered "normal". Under pressure from his wife and son, Mr. Morgan and Peter stop the train carrying Francey and Mrs. Morgan. In the end, both marriages are saved.

story_text_a: In Boston, Massachusetts in 1935, Arthur Barret, a barren man, hired Roger, a young Harvard student, to father a child for his wife Eleanor. After Roger and the child die under strange circumstances, Eleanor grows close to Father McKinnon, who has recently arrived from England and is hiding a secret linking him to the Barret family. Their relationship, initially friendly, will evolve.
story_text_b:
Boston 1935, lawyer Arthur Barret is a man of immense wealth and high prestige in the city's high society but, despite this, he cannot give a child to his beloved wife Eleanor because she is barren. For this reason, the couple decides that the only solution is to involve a third person in the conception of the child and Hannibal Thurman, Arthur's partner, offers Roger Martin, a young law student, to lend himself to the operation in exchange for $25,000. Roger, after some hesitation, accepts and, one evening, meets Eleanor, continuing to see the woman and eventually falling in love with her.
Roger, madly in love, tries to meet Eleanor, but one night he is attacked and threatened by Arthur who, to avoid a possible scandal and to reveal the pact between him and Roger, orders his colleague Hannibal to kill the boy. When Eleanor finds out, due to a tragic accident, she suffers a miscarriage, risking her life as well. The woman, in serious crisis and feeling guilty for Roger's death, seeks more and more comfort in father Michael McKinnon. The priest, suspecting that Arthur Barret is responsible for Roger's death, begins a series of investigations, but eventually the death is definitively dismissed by the police as a suicide.
Eleanor is growing increasingly estranged from her husband, whom she accuses of Roger's murder. Eleanor begins to assiduously frequent Father Michael until both succumb to passion: the woman becomes pregnant by the priest and gives birth to twins. However, during childbirth, Eleanor dies as a result of a heavy hemorrhage. Father Michael, immediately after the birth, to which he was present, tells Arthur that those two twins are actually his children and that he wants to be their father, but, later, at the grave of his beloved Eleanor, Father Michael changes his mind and decides to leave the scene.

story_text_a: Robert L. Talbot, an American millionaire, used to return every year in September to his Italian villa in Santa Margherita Ligure, on the Riviera of Levante, for his holidays. This time, however, he decides to arrive earlier, and discovers that his butler uses the villa as a hotel (baptized "La Dolce Vista") during his absence. Upon her arrival she hosts a group of six young American girls with their escort, and then forces Maurice to find them another accommodation. Robert, meanwhile, brings to the villa Lisa, the Italian fiancée who, unbeknownst to him, was preparing her own wedding with Spencer, a distinguished and more reliable Englishman than Robert. The next day a group of four American boys who had booked the hotel also arrive at the villa; Robert, who had already met them, hunts them without hesitation but they, after meeting the girls, decide to camp just outside the villa to be able to court them. Just as the girls are about to leave the villa, the lady who has custody of them injures herself by falling on the champagne cap thrown by Robert and ends up in the hospital for a long stay. The man, who at this point can no longer send the girls away and who feels responsible for them, devotes himself to trying to defend them, now that they live in his villa without the guardian, from the all-too-hot courtship of the boys. In the days that follow, Robert takes girls and boys everywhere, from outdoor trips in the Lambretta to club nights to dance. The boys, whose hands are tied with him always present, will do anything to get rid of him with subterfuge and deception, but they will always be beaten by the cunning Robert. The situation that has been created, however, also sends the relationship with Lisa into crisis, who finally decides to leave Robert and marry Spencer. When the girls leave with their rehabilitated escort, Lisa joins the group; Robert chases her to change her mind, but to no avail. Now that the relationship with Lisa is over, Robert decides to fire Maurice, sell the villa and leave Italy never to return. Meanwhile, Lisa realizes she made a mistake by leaving Robert and joins him at the train station to stop him, but he doesn't want to know; only a sympathetic deception will be able to dissuade him from leaving and convince him to marry her. After the wedding, the newlyweds return to the villa where they find Maurice, never fired and about to marry the American lady, again managing the hotel "La Dolce Vista"...
story_text_b: The film tells the story of the Greek slave Theonis, who unwittingly causes a war between Egypt and Ethiopia after she escapes from Ethiopian slavery and the Pharaoh falls in love with her.

story_text_a:
Samir Horn (Don Cheadle) is an American ex-soldier and devout Muslim whose specialty is the manufacture of explosive devices with Centec plastic explosive to radical Islamic factions, Horn sells a powerful explosive used by radical Islamists for their attacks against the United States.
Horn is actually a CIA infiltrator whose mission is unknown to the FBI and who seeks to track down the leaders of these Islamic terrorist factions, especially Nathir, the leader who leads them.
To make the mission more credible, Horn is detained in a Yemeni prison where Omar (Saïd Taghmaoui) is imprisoned and gains his trust when he is rescued by his friends from outside. Then Horn gets into a world full of radicalized Islamic ideals and mistrust where he contacts the group of "Nathir" who carry out attacks in Spain and France; for this Horn to make credible his conviction by this group of terrorists blows up an embassy of the United States under construction causing several deaths (in reality a screen of apparent deaths) then earning Horn his complete trust being able to meet Nathir, the leader of the terrorists.
However in the FBI there is an informant who keeps Omar up to date as the FBI investigations evolve, the search actions are headed by agents Alex Clayton (Guy Pearce) and Max Archer (Neal McDonough) who are desperately looking for Horn believing that he is a genuine radical Islamic terrorist.
The terrorists are planning for Thanksgiving a masterstroke with about 30 Islamic American citizens who will serve as suicide martyrs and who will board crowded buses of people to blow them up with themselves.
story_text_b:
As a moral fable, the comedy depicts the metamorphosis of the trapped substitute teacher Bertrand Barabi, who is mocked by colleagues. But piano teacher Dominique Benech, the widowed mother of his troubled student Michel, encourages him to finish his novel.
Bertrand Barabi is an assistant teacher at a secondary school in the province. Bertrand is tormented by the students with painting and is unpopular with the director because of his teaching methods. He spends most of his time writing in order to be admitted to the Académie des Belles Lettres and to see more often Madame Thuillier, a French teacher and aspiring lecturer, with whom he is secretly in love. However, Bertrand is unaware that Dominique Benech, the mother of one of his students, the impetuous Michel Benech, is paying attention to him. Dominique Benech is a piano teacher and asks her neighbor Bertrand to tutor her son. Bertrand accepts the extra work without giving up literature. After Dominique reads his novel "Jeu d'échecs", she encourages Bertrand and urges him to write a novel, which he renames "Le Pion". At school, however, the headmaster suddenly decides to dismiss Bertrand. To accomplish this, he provokes an unannounced inspection. Michel, however, learns of the preparations by chance. He warns his classmates and on the day of the inspection, the inspector can only note that Bertrand's lessons are being carried out properly, while the rest of the high school is in turmoil. Bertrand remains in office and continues to write his novel, which he soon sends to a Parisian publisher. Dominique tells him that the famous author Albert Carreaud is coming to town. Carreaud recognized Bertrand. The book will even be crowned. Thanks to his pseudonym 'Bertrand Bergerac', Bertrand remains anonymous for a short time and Dominique keeps his secret. But Dominique also knows that Bertrand is courting Madame Tuillier. The press is quick to reveal the identity of this "undiscovered Goncourt". But success does not turn Bertrand's head. With the help of his students, he even ridicules those who have wronged him before making his way to the discreet and affectionate Dominique who is waiting for him. He's playing the Beethoven sonata that Dominique always plays. They kiss, and after a cut, they celebrate their wedding on the riverbank, together with Bertrand's students.

story_text_a:
The aging bachelor Bob, who lives by gambling, is a well-known and popular figure in the Paris Montmartre underworld. Commissioner Ledru also has high hopes for him; Bob once saved his life, and Ledru firmly believes that the prison sentence he served after a failed bank robbery 20 years ago ended his criminal career. This does not diminish his generosity. Even Marc, who asks him for money in order to escape, wants to help immediately, until he realizes that the young man lets his girlfriend, who threatens to file a complaint for bodily harm, work for him as a prostitute. Marc is arrested for pimping and released by Ledru only on the condition that he snitches for the police. The attractive, still very young Anne wandering around Montmartre awakens Bob's protective instinct. He takes her into his apartment and encourages his personal protégé Paolo, the son of an ex-complice, to work with her - not least to isolate them from Marc.
